issues.title: Scaffold repository tooling
issues.body:
## User story

As a contributor, I want the repository rules, hooks and CI in place so that every change runs through an issue, a branch, the full test gate and a pull request.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.claude/settings.json`, `hooks/{branch-guard,gate-layers,issue-context}.sh` and the branch-guard test suite are in place and pass
- [ ] `.claude/skills/gh/SKILL.md` describes the issue, branch and PR workflow for `Cloudster1/Exciter` with milestones `M0 Foundation` to `M4 Stator integration` and `Backlog`
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` covers containers only (Makefile, Go 1.26), issue branches, four test layers, `make openapi`, no mocks below the layer under test, style rules, and where Armature and Stator live for reference
- [ ] No other requirements-management product is named anywhere: code, docs, issues, PRs, commits
- [ ] `run-tests.sh` is the single gate: shell tests, Go format/vet/unit, OpenAPI drift, web lint/types/vitest, compose-backed integration and Playwright; `EXCITER_GATE=full` runs everything
- [ ] `Makefile` includes `mk/*.mk`, and each layer joins the gate with the change that introduces its target: `mk/go.mk` with #3, `mk/web.mk`, `mk/biome.mk` and `biome.json` with #6
- [ ] `release.sh` and its tests are ported; `VERSION` is 0.1.0; `CHANGELOG.md` follows Keep a Changelog
- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `./run-tests.sh` in a layer matrix; `release.yml`, issue templates (feature, bug) and a PR template with `Closes #` exist
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/decisions.md` record the architecture and the first decisions: requirement key shape `CHK-R42`, revision equals normative save, the port base, org-wide status category of linked issues, the licence
- [ ] `NOTICE` credits the Apache-2.0 code adapted from Armature and from Stator, naming the source commit

## Tests

`.claude/hooks/tests/branch-guard-test.sh`, `tests/test-ci.sh` (CI jobs cover every layer) and `tests/test-release.sh` run inside `run-tests.sh` and in CI.

## Implementation

- Port from Stator: `.claude/`, `run-tests.sh`, `Makefile`, `release.sh`, `.github/`, `tests/test-ci.sh`, `tests/test-release.sh`, `scripts/test-summary.sh`. Rename `stator`/`STATOR_` to `exciter`/`EXCITER_`.
- `CLAUDE.md` adapted from Stator's; reference paths point at `~/repos/Armature` and a Stator checkout.
- `docs/decisions.md` starts with the decisions listed above; `docs/architecture.md` uses Stator's section skeleton (Overview, Backend, Frontend, Armature integration, Testing, Deployment).
- Licensing gate: Stator is being relicensed to Apache-2.0. Until that relicense is on Stator `main`, port only code whose original is in Armature (Apache-2.0). Stator-only files wait for it, and `NOTICE` names the post-relicense Stator commit each ported file came from.

Paths: `S/` is Stator, `A/` is Armature.

issues.title: Compose stack and Makefile with containerised toolchains
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want one command to start the whole stack on ports that never collide with a Stator checkout so that Exciter, Stator and Armature run side by side.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `make up` / `make down` / `make clean` run the compose stack: Postgres primary and replica, Valkey, SeaweedFS, Mailpit, Keycloak. migrate, seed and api join with #3, the worker with #4, web with #6
- [ ] Ports derive from a hash of the checkout path: base 10000, 500 slots of 20; nothing reaches Stator's 20000-29999 or the kernel's ephemeral range (32768+)
- [ ] Slots containing 16686, 11211, 15672 or 10250 are skipped
- [ ] Each worktree gets its own compose project `exciter-<hash>`
- [ ] `deploy/keycloak/realm.json` defines realm `suite-dev` with clients `exciter`, `armature` and `stator` and the dev users, so one person is the same subject in all three products
- [ ] Postgres roles `exciter_app` (RLS bound) and `exciter_admin` are created by the init script
- [ ] `.cache/stack.env` publishes the `EXCITER_*` URLs and ports for the test layers

## Tests

Shell: `tests/test-ports.sh` checks every computed slot is below 32768, outside 20000-29999 and off the denylist.

## Implementation

- Port `S/mk/stack.mk` (re-based), `S/deploy/docker-compose.yml`, `S/deploy/postgres/{init-roles.sh,replica-entrypoint.sh}`, `S/deploy/Dockerfile.{backend,web}`.
- Realm users mirror Stator's `deploy/keycloak/realm.json`.
- Licensing gate: Stator is being relicensed to Apache-2.0. Until that relicense is on Stator `main`, port only code whose original is in Armature (Apache-2.0). Stator-only files wait for it, and `NOTICE` names the post-relicense Stator commit each ported file came from.

Paths: `S/` is Stator, `A/` is Armature.

## Depends on

- #1

issues.title: Backend skeleton: config, database, migrations, HTTP route table
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want a Go service skeleton that mirrors Armature and Stator so that every later feature plugs into the same patterns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mk/go.mk` and `scripts/go-test.sh` ported from Stator; `check-go` and `test-integration` join the gate
- [ ] `backend/cmd/{api,migrate,openapi,seed}` build
- [ ] `deploy/Dockerfile.backend`; compose gains `migrate`, `seed` and `api` (from Stator's compose), and `mk/stack.mk` gains `DOCKER_GO_STACK` for the integration suite
- [ ] Configuration from `EXCITER_*` environment variables only, with validation and sentence-style errors
- [ ] `internal/db` cluster with primary/replica transactions, read-your-writes via LSN, and org row-level security via `current_org_id()`; IDs from `uuidv7()`
- [ ] Tables use `PRIMARY KEY (org_id, id)` with composite foreign keys and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY
- [ ] goose migrations embedded and applied by `cmd/migrate`; migration 00001 creates `org`, `app_user`, `org_member`, `current_org_id()`, `current_actor_id()` and `set_updated_at()`
- [ ] chi router with the middleware chain (request id, metrics, logging, recovery, security headers, same-site check, timeout, authenticate) and a single error envelope `{code, message, fields?, requestId?}`
- [ ] The route table generates `api/openapi.json` and `web/src/api/schema.d.ts`; operations may be `pending: true` and answer 501
- [ ] A unit test fails when the committed spec is stale and when router and table disagree
- [ ] `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/metrics` and `GET /api/v1/meta` respond

## Tests

Unit: config, LSN, route table drift. Integration: RLS isolates two orgs even through raw SQL as `exciter_app`; the contract test validates every response against `api/openapi.json`; the coverage test refuses a run that left an operation unexercised.

## Implementation

- Port `S/backend/internal/{config,db,freshness,tenant,secret,keyset,openapi,observability,testorg}`.
- Port `S/backend/internal/httpapi/{router,openapi,middleware,errors,request,freshness,observe,edges,test_handlers}.go`, which bring the `operation` struct with `pending`, `tool` and `toolHelp`.
- Port `S/backend/test/{contract_test,zz_coverage_test}.go` and `S/backend/migrations/00001_foundation.sql` (trimmed).
- Originals: `A/backend/internal/db`, `A/backend/internal/freshness`, `A/backend/internal/httpapi/openapi_operations.go`.

Paths: `S/` is Stator, `A/` is Armature.

## Depends on

- #2

issues.title: Transactional outbox, worker and audit log
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want events written in the same transaction as the change and an audit log admins can read so that integrations and notifications never act on a rolled-back change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `events.Emit(ctx, tx, topic, payload)` writes to `outbox_event` in the caller's transaction
- [ ] Compose gains the `worker` service
- [ ] `cmd/worker` claims events with `SKIP LOCKED`, retries with backoff and sets an event aside after `MaxAttempts`, recording it in the audit log
- [ ] `exciter_app` may insert an event only with its own actor id
- [ ] `audit_log` is written with the act, readable only by owners and admins, never updated or deleted, pruned after `EXCITER_RETAIN_AUDIT`; `GET /audit`, `/audit/facets` and `/audit/export` are agreed in the route table as pending (served with #5, screen with #6)

## Tests

Unit: backoff. Integration: an event rolls back with its transaction; two workers never claim the same event; the audit row is enforced through SQL.

## Implementation

- Port `S/backend/internal/{events,audit}`, `S/backend/cmd/worker`, `S/web/src/routes/audit.tsx`.
- Migrations 00020 `outbox_event` (from `S/00150_outbox.sql`) and 00021 `audit_log` (from `S/00230_audit_log.sql`).
- Originals: `A/backend/internal/events`, `A/backend/internal/audit`.

Paths: `S/` is Stator, `A/` is Armature.

## Depends on

- #3

issues.title: Organizations, members and password sessions
issues.body:
## User story

As an admin, I want to bootstrap an organization, add members and sign in with a password so that the product is usable before single sign-on is configured and the test suites can sign in.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `seed bootstrap` creates the first organization and owner; `seed` creates a demo organization
- [ ] Org roles owner, admin, member and guest
- [ ] Sign in, sign out, `GET /auth/me`, switch organization; session cookie with the same hardening as Stator
- [ ] Members API: list, add, change role, remove, each recorded in the audit log; the screens come with #6 and join requests, which only SSO sign-ins raise, with #7
- [ ] Passwords hashed with argon2id
- [ ] `GET /audit`, `/audit/facets` and `/audit/export` (pending since #4) are served to administrators, ported from `S/backend/internal/httpapi/audit_handlers.go`

## Tests

Unit: argon2 parameters. Integration: session cookie, switching organizations, a member of one org cannot see another through SQL, membership changes are the administrators' through SQL. Playwright `login.spec.ts` comes with #9.

## Implementation

- Port `S/backend/internal/auth/{auth,model,password,service,members,createmember,joinrequests}.go`, `S/backend/internal/httpapi/{auth,member,join}_handlers.go`, `S/web/src/features/auth/{LoginPage,Members,AddMember,JoinRequests}.tsx`, `S/backend/internal/seed`.
- Migrations 00010 groups and 00012 sessions (from Stator 00010 and 00012).
- Originals: `A/backend/internal/auth`.

Paths: `S/` is Stator, `A/` is Armature.

issues.title: Single sign-on via OIDC with sessions and group sync
issues.body:
## User story

As a person who already signs in to Armature and Stator, I want to sign in to Exciter with the same identity so that I am the same user in all three products.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Org admins configure an OIDC provider; sign-in uses PKCE and matches people by subject
- [ ] Identity provider groups map to org roles and are synced at every sign-in
- [ ] Backchannel issuer rewrite via `EXCITER_OIDC_BACKCHANNEL` for containerised providers
- [ ] The dev seed configures the `exciter` client of the `suite-dev` realm
- [ ] Join requests for people not yet in the organization: `S/backend/internal/auth/joinrequests.go`, `join_handlers.go`, `JoinRequests.tsx`
- [ ] `session_reaches` lets a provider's sign-in reach the organizations that trust the same provider, as Stator's does

## Tests

Unit: OIDC flow helpers and group role mapping. Integration: login against the compose Keycloak. Playwright: `sso.spec.ts`.

## Implementation

- Port `S/backend/internal/oidc/*`, `S/backend/internal/httpapi/oidc_handlers.go`, `S/web/src/features/auth/{ProviderSettings,GroupRoles}.tsx`, `S/web/src/routes/sso.tsx`.
- Migrations 00011 identity providers and 00013 join requests.
- Originals: `A/backend/internal/oidc`.

issues.title: Requirements: create, edit, trash and revisions
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want to write a requirement with a statement and rationale and have every change kept as a revision so that nothing said is ever lost and later reviews, baselines and links can point at an exact revision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Requirement key `<PROJECT>-R<n>` (for example `CHK-R42`), regex `^([A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9})-R([1-9][0-9]*)$`, allocated per project
- [ ] Title, rich-text statement, rationale, owner, priority; created and edited with the shared editor
- [ ] A save whose normative content (title, statement, rationale, type, attributes) changed writes an immutable `requirement_revision`; other changes (status, owner, labels, position) go to `requirement_change`
- [ ] Optimistic concurrency: a stale save is refused with 409 and names what to do
- [ ] Trash and restore; purge by admins
- [ ] `/r/{id}` permalink redirects to the current key URL
- [ ] Old keys keep resolving after a move or project key rename

## Tests

Unit: key parsing, normative hash is stable under key order and whitespace, and no Armature or Stator issue-key pattern matches an Exciter key. Integration: revisions cannot be updated or deleted as `exciter_app`; numbers have no gaps; 409 on conflict. Vitest: editor allowlist. Playwright: `requirement-crud.spec.ts`.

## Implementation

- New `backend/internal/requirement` (`requirement.go`, `service.go`, `revision.go`, `trash.go`).
- Revision sequence trigger from `S/backend/migrations/00070_versions.sql`; old keys from `A/backend/migrations/00922_issue_old_keys.sql`; trash from `S/00022_trash.sql`; plain text from `page_plain_blocks` in `S/00100_search.sql`.
- Editor: slimmed port of `S/web/src/features/editor/{Editor,Toolbar,DocView,MentionList}.tsx` and `S/backend/internal/document/{validate,allowlist,text}.go`.
- Migrations 00120-00139. UI `/p/$projectKey/r/$reqKey`.

Paths: `S/` is Stator, `A/` is Armature.

## Depends on

- #12

issues.title: Hierarchy, sections and the specification view
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want requirements arranged in a tree with sections and read as one numbered document so that a specification reads top to bottom like the documents it replaces.

issues.body:
## User story

As a power user, I want a query language like Armature's so that I can express any filter in one line.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The grid takes a one-line query beside its words box, through a Words/Query switch; the grid's other filter controls stay and narrow together with it
- [ ] The query knows a requirement's fields (key, title, text, statement, rationale, kind, type, status, category, owner, author, priority, labels, parent, revision, created, updated), the project's attributes by their quoted names, and traceability: suspect links, approval state, trace links by type in both directions (`derivesFrom = CHK-R4`, `verifiedBy IS EMPTY`) and coverage levels (`verified = full`)

- [ ] A query that cannot run is refused with `bad_query`, a sentence and the character it went wrong at, which the box points at
- [ ] Saved views keep the query; CSV export, coverage and the matrix narrow by it as they do by the grid's filter
- [ ] The box completes fields, operators, keywords and live names (statuses, types, people, labels, options, link ends) at the caret, and offers matching requirements

issues.title: Outbound Exciter webhooks
issues.body:
## User story

As an integrator, I want signed webhooks when requirements change so that other tools can react.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An installation's administrators keep webhook endpoints: a name, an address, the events it hears, and the projects it listens to (all when none are named)
- [ ] Events: requirement.created, requirement.revised, requirement.changed, requirement.trashed, requirement.restored, requirement.moved, link.created, link.removed, link.cleared, review.requested, review.decided, review.closed, comment.created, thread.resolved and baseline.taken
- [ ] The body is a versioned envelope whose payload carries references read as the endpoint's owner (the requirement's key, title, revision, status, project and address, the actor, what the event says); what the owner may not see is withheld
- [ ] Each request is signed with HMAC-SHA256 under a secret shown once: `X-Exciter-Signature-256` over the body, and `X-Exciter-Signature-Timestamped-256` over the time and the body, with `X-Exciter-Timestamp`, `X-Exciter-Event`, `X-Exciter-Delivery` and `X-Exciter-Webhook-Version`
- [ ] A failed delivery is retried with backoff, an endpoint failing for a day is turned off, and a delivery log, a test ping and sending again are at hand
- [ ] Nothing is posted into the server's own network unless `EXCITER_OUTBOUND_ALLOW` names it

## Tests

Unit: signing, validation, backoff, envelopes. Integration: endpoints and the secret shown once, every event reaching a receiver as the owner may read it, the project filter, retries and turning off, withheld payloads, the network guard, database guards. Playwright: an administrator adds an endpoint and sees a signed delivery.

## Implementation

issues.title: Requirement reuse and variants
issues.body:
## User story

As a product line engineer, I want to reuse requirements across projects and keep variants so that common requirements are written once.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A project's administrators mark it as a library (audited); only libraries are offered as a source of reuse
- [ ] Reusing a library requirement, or a section with what is below it, puts a copy in another project that follows its source: it records the source and the source's revision it shows, and its title, statement and rationale are not edited there while it follows
- [ ] Type, attributes, status, owner, priority, labels, links and reviews stay the target's own
- [ ] When the source has a newer revision, the reuse is behind: the requirement page and the specification say so, show what changed in the source, and "Take revision N" writes the target's next revision with the source's words
- [ ] "Make a variant" lets the target change its words; a variant keeps its origin and the revision it branched from, still reports newer source revisions, and taking one makes it follow again
- [ ] The query language has `reuse` (`following`, `behind`, `variant`, `none`), for the grid, views and exports
- [ ] Watchers of a reuse are told when its source gets a new revision, if they may read the source
- [ ] The database refuses a following copy whose words are not its source's, a source outside a library, and a new source on an existing requirement, straight through SQL

## Tests

Unit: the query field. Integration: reuse, lock, take, variant, purge of the source, notifications, the query field, and the guards as `exciter_app`. vitest: the library setting, the reuse dialog, the banner, the locked editor. Playwright: reuse from a library, revise the source, take the revision.

## Implementation

- Migration 00760 (`requirement.reuse_source`, `reuse_revision`, `reuse_state`, the guard `requirement_reuse_guard`, the notification kind `source_revised`), the library mark in `project.settings`, reuse in `internal/requirement` beside copy.
- Routes: `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/reuse`, `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/reuse/take`, `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/reuse/variant`; `reuse` on a requirement and a specification entry.
- The guard compares words (title and the plain text of statement and rationale), so images copied with their own ids still count as the source's.

issues.title: Remove organizations: one installation is one team's requirements
issues.body:
## Why

Exciter is self-hosted, and an installation serves one team, as Armature has decided in its Cloudster1/Armature#208 and Stator in praetorianer777/Stator#380. Organizations add a layer such an installation never uses: an organization to type at sign-in and for single sign-on, switching between organizations, rules for people in several of them, and a tenant column on every table. This epic removes organizations from everything people and the API see, then from the schema.

It runs before the rest of M2, so #28 to #31 are built without organizations rather than reworked.

## Decisions

1. **Product first, schema last.** The product and the API lose organizations while one `org` row stays inside, so `org_id` and row security keep working. The last ticket drops the tenant layer. Every ticket keeps every layer of `./run-tests.sh` green.
2. **A database with several organizations is refused, not merged.** A migration counts them and stops, naming the first ten and saying to delete the extra ones first. Project keys, statuses, workflows and people would collide in a merge.
3. **Everyone signed in belongs to the installation.** Someone without an active membership is refused with "Your account has been switched off. Ask an administrator."
4. **Tests isolate by unique people, project keys and names**, with a serial lane for the tests that change installation-wide settings: single sign-on, the default theme, link types for all projects, all tokens and the Armature connection.
5. **Row security stays for the permission walls.** Exciter's guards live in restrictive policies; only the tenant isolation and administrator bypass policies go with `org_id`.

**What stays, under plainer names:** the audit log, groups, roles, link types for all projects, the default theme, join requests, the Armature connection, and the owner and administrator roles.

No release has shipped, so removed addresses are deleted rather than redirected. Migrations take 00400 to 00419; M2's remaining ranges move to 00420 (#28), 00430 (#29) and 00440 (#30).

## Order

- [ ] #83 The browser suite isolates spec files without an organization each. This comes first.
- [ ] #84 One installation: the organization is made at first start, and a database with several stops.
- [ ] #85 Sign-in without organizations: no switching, one provider, no slug.
- [ ] #86 Members and administrators without organizations.
- [ ] #87 The Armature connection without an organization slug.
- [ ] #88 Say "everyone" instead of "the organization".
- [ ] #89 Docs, seed and deployment for one installation.
- [ ] #90 The integration suite isolates tests without an organization each.
- [ ] #91 Drop `org_id` and the tenant layer from the schema.

#87 depends only on #84 and can run beside #85 and #86.

## Out of scope

- Merging the data of several organizations.
- Running more than one team on one installation; that takes separate installations.

issues.title: The browser suite isolates spec files without an organization each
issues.body:
## User story

As someone working on Exciter, I want the browser suite to keep its spec files apart without giving each one an organization of its own, so that organizations can leave the product.

Part of epic #82.

## What happens today

- `e2e/fixtures/org.ts` (`orgTest`) makes a throwaway organization per spec file and worker through `POST /api/v1/test/orgs`, signs alice and bob into it and deletes it when the worker stops. 20 of 22 specs use it.
- `fixtures/auth.ts` signs in by organization (`signIn(org)`, `signInToOrg`, `ownerApi` through `/auth/switch-org`).
- `fixtures/db.ts` `orgWithDeadProvider` inserts an organization and a provider straight into the database.
- `armature.spec.ts` and `armature-links.spec.ts` use `freshOrg.slug` as the stub's tenant; `audit.spec.ts` inserts audit rows with `freshOrg.id`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **A fixture inside the installation.** Each spec gets a project-key prefix made from the spec and the worker, and people made through the existing create-member route, signed in with a storage state each.
- [ ] **A serial lane.** A Playwright project runs the specs that change installation-wide settings one at a time: sso, the default theme, link types for all projects, all tokens, armature and armature-links. Each restores what it changed.
- [ ] **No straight inserts of organizations.** The dead provider is a serial step on the one provider, restored afterwards; the audit spec finds its rows by its own actor.
- [ ] **The Armature specs** pick the stub's tenant by token, not by the organization's slug.
- [ ] **Docs.** `docs/decisions.md` supersedes "Each browser spec file gets a throwaway organization (#9)"; `docs/architecture.md` describes the new isolation.

## Tests

The browser suite is green and still parallel outside the serial lane; the wall-clock time is reported against today's. Three green runs in a row.

## Implementation

- `e2e/fixtures/{org,auth,db}.ts`, `e2e/playwright.config.ts`, the 20 specs on `orgTest`.
- Follows Cloudster1/Armature#209.

- Nothing.

issues.title: One installation: the organization is made at first start, and a database with several stops
issues.body:
## User story

As the operator of an Exciter installation, I want it to be one place with one set of people and settings, made when it is installed, so nobody has to choose an organization before they can work.

Part of epic #82.

## What happens today

- `seed.Ensure` (`backend/internal/seed/seed.go:35`) makes the organization named by `EXCITER_BOOTSTRAP_ORG_SLUG` and `EXCITER_BOOTSTRAP_ORG_NAME`; the test endpoints make more.
- The default theme lives on the `org` row (`default_theme_id`, 00031) and is read in `theme/service.go`.
- A principal can be signed in with no organization: `Principal.Org` is nil, `requireOrg` (`httpapi/middleware.go:196-211`, 17 uses) answers `no_organization`, and `db.inTx` refuses with `ErrNoTenant`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Upgrade guard.** Migration 00400 refuses to run when `org` holds more than one row, naming the first ten by address and name and saying to delete the extra ones first. It changes no schema.
- [ ] **One organization at first start**, named by `EXCITER_NAME` (default "Exciter"), which replaces `EXCITER_BOOTSTRAP_ORG_SLUG` and `EXCITER_BOOTSTRAP_ORG_NAME`. `EnsureAdmin` and `EnsureMember` stop taking a slug. Compose, `mk/stack.mk` and the README variables follow.
- [ ] **An `installation` package** is the one way to the name and the default theme. `GET` and `PUT /installation` read and rename it, for administrators.
- [ ] **An Installation page** at `/settings/installation` renames it; the sidebar head and the first breadcrumb show the name.
- [ ] **Everyone is in it.** `requireOrg`, `no_organization`, `InOrg()` and the nil-organization paths go. A sign-in or token of somebody without an active membership is refused with "Your account has been switched off. Ask an administrator."; an open session whose membership is gone ends.
- [ ] **Tenant plumbing unchanged.** `org_id` and row security keep working; the integration harness may still make throwaway organizations until #90.

## Tests

- Integration: the migration refuses two organizations and passes with one or none; a first start makes exactly one; somebody without a membership is refused with the sentence; renaming is audited and administrators only.
- Vitest: the Installation page.
- Playwright (serial): renaming shows in the sidebar.

As someone signing in to Exciter, I want to land straight in it: no organization to type, none to choose, and no switcher.

## What happens today

- The login page asks for the organization and remembers it (`LoginPage.tsx`, `LAST_ORG_KEY`, `/login?org=`).

- Sessions record `current_org_id` and `proof_org_id`; `session_reaches` (00012, widened in 00015) and `session_stays_home` decide where a session may go.

- [ ] **The login page** has no organization field, `?org=` or remembered organization.
- [ ] **One identity provider.** Sign-in starts at `GET /auth/oidc/start`; the slugged route is deleted. Provider settings show the new address.
- [ ] **Sessions forget organizations.** They stop writing `current_org_id` and `proof_org_id`; `session_reaches`, the provider trust of 00015 and `session_stays_home` go in migration 00401. The session's proof stays.
- [ ] **Docs.** `make openapi` and `make web-schema` are regenerated; architecture "Identity" and `docs/decisions.md` are updated.

## Tests

issues.title: Members and administrators without organizations
issues.body:
## User story

As an administrator of Exciter, I want people to belong to the installation: letting somebody go switches their account off, and there is always an administrator left.

Part of epic #82.

## What happens today

- `DELETE /users/{userID}` takes a member "out of the organization" (`auth/members.go:99`), keeping the account for other organizations.
- An organization keeps its last owner, in the service (`ErrOwnerStays`) and the trigger `org_member_owner_stays` (00012).
- Administrators list and revoke tokens at `/org/tokens` and `/settings/organization-tokens`.

issues.body:
## User story

As someone working on Exciter, I want the schema and the code to stop carrying an organization that is always the same, so queries, triggers and new features no longer pay for multi-tenancy.

Part of epic #82.

## What happens today

- 42 tables carry `org_id`, with 44 tenant isolation and 46 administrator bypass policies beside about 109 restrictive permission policies, all under forced row security.
- Primary and foreign keys are composite on `(org_id, id)`; project keys are unique per organization.
- `current_org_id()` is used about 93 times in SQL and 127 times in Go; `internal/tenant` sets `app.org_id`; events carry `OrgID`; objects are stored under `org/<uuid>/`.

## Acceptance criteria

New migrations from 00410, in this order, because Postgres drops dependents silently and trigger bodies fail only at runtime:

- [ ] **1. Policies.** The tenant isolation and administrator bypass policies go; FORCE and the permission policies stay, without `current_org_id()`. How `exciter_admin` passes row security is decided and recorded.
- [ ] **2. Constraints.** Keys, unique indexes and foreign keys that include `org_id` are recreated without it; project keys are unique across the installation.
- [ ] **3. Functions and triggers** are rewritten, keeping their project, owner and creator rules.
- [ ] **4. Go.** `org_id` leaves inserts, conflicts and filters; `internal/tenant` and `app.org_id` go; events lose `OrgID`; per-organization loops run once; object keys lose the organization.
- [ ] **5. Tables.** `org` becomes `installation`, `org_member` becomes a role on `app_user`, and the single sign-on provider and the Armature connection become one-row tables.

## Tests

- Every layer.
- A migration test from a populated one-organization database checks every row survives.
- A check that no table, column or function mentions `org_id` or `current_org_id`.
- The raw-SQL tests prove the permission walls without a tenant.

- Follows Cloudster1/Armature#218. One PR in ordered commits; if it grows beyond review it splits at step 4.

issues.title: Report the build at GET /api/v1/meta, as all three tools do
issues.body:
All three tools answer the same unauthenticated endpoint, so a partner, an operator or Dynamo can tell which build it talks to:

```
GET /api/v1/meta
{
  "product": "stator" | "armature" | "exciter",
  "build": { "version": "1.3.0", "commit": "abc1234", "builtAt": "2026-10-14T09:00:00Z" },
  "apiVersion": "1",
  "capabilities": []
}
```

- `version` is the semver from `VERSION` (a dev build says so, e.g. `1.3.0+4.gabc1234`), `commit` the short git hash, both stamped at build time.
- `apiVersion` is `info.version` of the OpenAPI document; it rises only for a change that breaks clients.
- `capabilities` is filled by the capability issue; until then it is an empty list.
- The endpoint is in the OpenAPI document and covered by a test that compares it with the build stamp.

**Here today:** `GET /api/v1/meta` returns `{product, build}` (also the MCP tool `server_info`). Add `apiVersion` and `capabilities`; the path stays.


Part of the release plan for [Dynamo](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo), which runs Stator, Armature and Exciter together and releases the combinations that pass.

https://claude.ai/code/session_012upyidVTNM6iSeHELAc2fy

issues.title: Release by tag the same way in all three tools
issues.body:
All three tools release the same way, following the release script of [chaosflix-jellyfin](https://github.com/praetorianer777/chaosflix-jellyfin/blob/main/release.sh) and its tag workflow:

- `./release.sh [version] [--dry-run]` infers the next semver from the Conventional Commits since the last tag (breaking: MAJOR, below 1.0.0 MINOR; `feat`: MINOR; `fix` and the rest: PATCH), or takes it by hand, and prints the rule it applied.
- It refuses a checkout that is behind its upstream or not on the default branch, so it never tags code the remote lacks.
- It writes the version into every file that carries one (`VERSION`, `web/package.json` where present, `Chart.yaml` `version` and `appVersion`), adds the CHANGELOG section and makes an annotated tag `vX.Y.Z` whose message is the release notes. A test refuses these files disagreeing.
- Main takes no direct commits here, so the bump travels on a branch `release/vX.Y.Z` with its own pull request; the tag is set on the merge commit (by the script after the merge, or by the workflow), never on a commit main does not have.
- On the tag, CI builds every image from the tag, pushes it to `ghcr.io/<owner>/<tool>-<image>:X.Y.Z` (and the commit hash), packages and publishes the chart, publishes the GitHub release from the tag message, and sends a `repository_dispatch` to Dynamo with the tool and version.
- A build not made from a tag says so in its version (`X.Y.Z+N.g<hash>`), so a dev image is never mistaken for a release.

**Here today:** `./release.sh` is Stator's copy, with the same gaps (no chart, no image push), and there is no chart yet.


Part of the release plan for [Dynamo](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo), which runs Stator, Armature and Exciter together and releases the combinations that pass.

issues.title: Give the webhook envelope a version
issues.body:
The webhook envelope carries a version, so its format can change without breaking receivers silently:

```
{ "version": 1, "id": "...", "topic": "issue.updated", "occurredAt": "...", "payload": { ... } }
```

- `version` is an integer and rises only for a change that breaks receivers (a field removed, renamed or changing meaning). Adding a field or a topic does not raise it.
- It is also sent as a header `X-<Product>-Webhook-Version`, so a receiver can decide before parsing.
- A sender of version N+1 keeps sending N to endpoints that registered for N, for at least one Dynamo release.
- A receiver ignores unknown fields and topics, and refuses an envelope version it does not know with a clear status and log line, instead of misreading it.
- The format is described in the OpenAPI document (or a JSON schema next to it) and covered by a contract test on both sides.

**Here:** Exciter will store issue status from Armature's webhooks and may send its own later. Build the receiver against the versioned envelope from the start, and use the same envelope for any webhook Exciter sends.


Part of the release plan for [Dynamo](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo), which runs Stator, Armature and Exciter together and releases the combinations that pass.

Build `deploy/charts/exciter` the way Stator's (`deploy/charts/stator`) and Armature's charts are built, so the three install alike:

- Deployments for `api`, `worker` and `web` (nginx), jobs for `migrate` and `seed`, services, ingress, service account, ConfigMap and Secret for the `EXCITER_` environment.
- Postgres through CloudNativePG (primary and replica) or a bundled instance for trying it out, Valkey bundled or external, S3 storage external (SeaweedFS in the demo values); the same value names as Stator's chart wherever the meaning is the same.
- Sign-in through the shared Keycloak realm `dynamo` (#102) by issuer URL and client secret from values.
- Partners by values: Armature and Stator base URLs, so the umbrella chart can wire them.
- Images `ghcr.io/<owner>/exciter-{backend,web}`; an empty tag means `appVersion`, which the release script sets together with `version` (#101).
- `values-demo.yaml` for a one-command demo, `NOTES.txt` that says how to reach it and sign in.

issues.title: The schema stops asking for the organization: policies, keys, functions
issues.body:
## User story

As someone working on Exciter, I want the database's rules to stop asking which organization a row belongs to, so the permission walls are the only walls and the columns can go.

Part of #91, epic #82. The first of three steps; the Go code and the tables follow in their own issues.

## What happens today

- 44 `*_tenant_isolation` policies keep the one organization apart from none, and 46 `*_admin_bypass` policies let `exciter_admin` past them; 7 of the 109 restrictive permission policies also read `org_id` or `current_org_id()`.
- 26 primary and unique keys, 80 foreign keys and 36 indexes include `org_id`; project keys are unique per organization.
- 61 functions read `org_id` or `current_org_id()`, among them `current_actor_administers`, `perm_project_holds` and the guards of every table.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Policies (migration 00410).** Each table's tenant isolation policy becomes one permissive policy for every role, `USING (true)`; the admin bypass policies go as redundant. FORCE and the 109 permission policies stay, rewritten without the organization. `app_user` still shows the app role only people who belong to the installation. The upgrade stops at a policy the migrations did not make, naming it.
- [ ] **Keys (00411).** Every key, unique index, foreign key and index loses `org_id`; project keys, link type keys and the other names are unique in the installation. The upgrade checks the new keys first and names any rows that would share one. The `ON CONFLICT` clauses in Go name the new keys.
- [ ] **Functions and triggers (00412).** Every function and trigger keeps its project, owner and creator rules without reading `org_id` or `current_org_id()`; those that only held a row to its organization go, their foreign keys keeping what else they said. Messages that named the organization say "here".
- [ ] **Down migrations** put back every policy, key and function as before; up then down compares equal from the catalog on a scratch database.
- [ ] **Docs.** `docs/decisions.md` records how the roles pass row security now, and why the permission policies stay.

## Tests

- Integration: a check that no policy, key, index or function names `org_id` or `current_org_id`, apart from the `org` table's own and the columns themselves; the raw-SQL suites prove every permission wall without a tenant; a migration test from a populated one-organization database at 00403 keeps every row.
- Every layer passes; Go still sets `app.org_id` and writes `org_id`, which step B removes.

## Implementation

- Follows Cloudster1/Armature#218 steps 1 to 3 (its #232, #233, #234), except that Exciter's permission walls stay in row security.

## Depends on

- #90

issues.title: The code stops carrying the organization
issues.body:
## User story

As someone working on Exciter, I want the code to stop carrying an organization that is always the same, so no request, event or file has to say which one it means.

Part of #91, epic #82. The second of three steps, after the schema stops asking (#106).

## What happens today

- `internal/tenant` puts the organization on every context and `db` sets `app.org_id` in every transaction; `tenant.ErrNoTenant` refuses a transaction without one.

- [ ] **Defaults (migration 00413).** Every `org_id` column defaults to the installation's one row, so nothing has to write it; with more than one row the default refuses rather than guesses.
- [ ] **No tenant.** `internal/tenant`, `app.org_id`, `ErrNoTenant` and the middleware's tenant go; `current_org_id()` answers the one row until step C drops it.

issues.title: Offer webhook envelope version 2 in the CloudEvents shape
issues.body:
## User story
As an administrator connecting Exciter to a relay, a broker or any CloudEvents receiver, I want Exciter's webhooks in the CloudEvents 1.0 shape, so that the receiver understands them without code written for Exciter; and as an administrator of all three tools, I want Exciter to keep taking Armature's and Stator's webhooks when they move to that shape.

Armature, Stator and Exciter send webhooks in one shared envelope, version 1: `{version, id, topic, occurredAt, payload}` plus `source`. Version 2 follows CloudEvents 1.0 in structured mode. Armature: Cloudster1/Armature#286. Stator: praetorianer777/Stator#434. Shared list: praetorianer777/Dynamo#4.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An endpoint registered for version 2 is posted `application/cloudevents+json; charset=utf-8` with `specversion: "1.0"`, `id` (the event's, the same on every attempt), `source` (the installation's address, `EXCITER_APP_URL`), `type` (`dev.exciter.<topic>`, `dev.exciter.ping` for a test), `time`, `datacontenttype: "application/json"`, `dataversion: 1` and `data` (the version 1 payload, unchanged)
- [ ] Signatures and headers stay as in version 1; `X-Exciter-Webhook-Version` says 2
- [ ] An administrator chooses the version when registering or editing an endpoint, in Settings, Webhooks and through the existing `version` field; version 1 stays the default and keeps being sent to endpoints registered for it
- [ ] Exciter receives version 2 from Armature and Stator as well as version 1: the topic is the `type` after `dev.armature.` or `dev.stator.`, the payload is `data`; a version, `specversion` or `dataversion` Exciter does not read is refused with 422 so the sender retries
- [ ] The envelope and its event types are in `api/openapi.json`: the `event` webhook carries both bodies, and the receiving operations accept both
- [ ] `/api/v1/meta` reports `webhooks@2` next to `webhooks@1`
- [ ] Events stay thin, as in version 1

## Tests
Unit: both envelopes, decoding what Armature and Stator send in either version, the version refusals. Integration: a version 2 endpoint receives the CloudEvent signed as before; the stubs post version 2 and Exciter acts on it; version 3 is refused. vitest: the version choice in the webhook form. Playwright: register a version 2 endpoint and see it listed.

## Implementation
- `internal/webhook`: a version 2 row in `envelopes`, `Versions` for what an endpoint may choose and a receiver reads, and one decoder both receivers share. No migration: `webhook_endpoint.version` already holds any version.
- The stubs send version 2 when a test asks; their contract tests hold version 1 to the vendored documents until Armature and Stator document version 2.
- Docs: `docs/integration.md`, `docs/decisions.md`, contract in `docs/api-contract-backlog.md`, CHANGELOG. Exciter's concrete choices are posted on Armature#286 and Stator#434.

- [ ] It lists `webhooks@1` as well, with the same eight operations Stator promises under that name, so a partner can check for Exciter's outbound webhooks (#48) before it relies on them

- [ ] An entry adds a requirement or a section after it, or as its first child, opened straight in its editor

issues.title: The theme round trip test reads the theme before it is chosen
issues.body:
## What happened, and what did you expect?

`e2e/tests/themes.spec.ts` "a theme exported from Exciter imports again and draws the same, and so does one exported from Stator" fails now and then: `--color-primary` is still the previous theme's (`#b45309` where `#15803d` was expected, at line 139). It failed on `feat/154-matrix-xlsx` and on #165. The test should pass every time.

## Why

After choosing a theme with "Use" (lines 125 and 137) the test opens `/` straight away, before the choice is saved, so the page can load with the theme before it. The other tests in the file wait for the "Now using X." notice first.

## Fix

Wait for that notice after both choices, as the other theme tests do.

issues.title: Speak the current MCP protocol
issues.body:
## User story

As someone connecting an assistant, I want Exciter's MCP endpoint to speak the protocol my client speaks and to describe its tools fully, so that the client connects without workarounds and the model knows what each tool answers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `initialize` offers `2025-11-25` and `2025-06-18`, answers the version the client asks for when it is one of them and the newest otherwise
- [ ] A request whose `MCP-Protocol-Version` header names a version Exciter does not speak is refused with 400 and a sentence naming the versions it does
- [ ] `GET /mcp` answers 405, since the endpoint opens no stream; an `Origin` that is not the installation's is refused on bearer calls as well as cookie ones
- [ ] `initialize` carries `instructions`: what a key such as `CHK-R42` is, that a text change needs `baseRevision`, how outlines number the document, and that reviews are decided by people in the browser
- [ ] Each tool has a `title`, an `outputSchema` drawn from its row's response type, and `structuredContent` that fits it
- [ ] Each tool is annotated `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint` and `idempotentHint` from its operation, and `openWorldHint` when it calls Armature or Stator
- [ ] `GET /meta` lists `mcp@1`, and `docs/integration.md` says what it promises
- [ ] `docs/mcp.md` says how to connect Claude Code and other MCP clients with a personal token

## Tests

Unit: version negotiation, the header refused, every tool's output schema built and every tool annotated. Integration: a conversation with the stack driven by the official Go SDK client (`github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`, in the test only): initialize, list the tools, call a read and a write, and read the API document resource; `GET /mcp` is 405; a foreign origin is refused.

## Implementation

- `instructions` is a constant beside `MCPProtocolVersion`, worded on Exciter's own terms.
- `mcp@1` joins the `capabilities` that `GET /meta` answers, with the others.

issues.title: Connect assistants with OAuth
issues.body:
## User story

As someone connecting an assistant, I want to give it Exciter's address, sign in and say what it may do, so that a client that connects with an address alone can work with my requirements without me making and pasting a token.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (RFC 9728, also under the endpoint's path) names Exciter as the authorization server of `/api/v1/mcp`, and a 401 from `/mcp` carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="..."`
- [ ] `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414) describes the endpoints, `S256` and the grants offered
- [ ] A client is known by a Client ID Metadata Document, fetched through the outbound guard, or registers itself at `POST /oauth/register` (RFC 7591), limited in rate; a registration never used expires
- [ ] `GET /oauth/authorize` requires PKCE with `S256`, `state`, a redirect the client registered, and `resource` (RFC 8707) naming the MCP endpoint; each refusal is the error the RFC names, with a sentence
- [ ] The consent page `/oauth/consent` needs a session, names the client and the host it sends back to, and offers read-only or full and which projects, as a token does; allowing or denying returns to the client
- [ ] `POST /oauth/token` serves `authorization_code` and `refresh_token`; a code is used once; an access token lasts an hour and is stored only as its SHA-256; a refresh token turns over at each use, and one used twice ends the grant
- [ ] `POST /oauth/revoke` (RFC 7009) ends a token
- [ ] An OAuth access token is accepted at `/mcp` and for the calls it carries and nowhere else; read-only and the projects hold as for a personal token
- [ ] Switching somebody off ends their grants; administrators can switch OAuth connections off for the installation
- [ ] The audit log records `oauth.granted`

## Tests

Unit: PKCE verification, the metadata documents, the redirect match. Integration: the whole flow as a client makes it, then a tool call; a code used twice, a wrong verifier, an unregistered redirect and another resource each refused; a read-only grant refused a write; a grant limited to one project held by row level security, tried straight through SQL as `exciter_app`; a refresh token used twice ends the grant; an access token refused outside `/mcp`. Playwright: allow and deny on the consent page, with an accessibility check.

## Implementation

- A package `backend/internal/oauth` beside `internal/auth`, its tables in the contract's migration range with row level security that keeps a grant to its owner and administrators.
- `authenticate` (`backend/internal/httpapi/middleware.go`) knows the access token's prefix and puts a principal with the grant's limits on the request, as `authenticateAPIToken` does.
- The consent page reuses the scope and project choice of the token form (`web/src/features/tokens/TokensPage.tsx`).
- `netguard` fetches client metadata documents.

- #182
- #183

issues.title: Verify requirements with test results from CI
issues.body:
## User story

As a verification engineer, I want the test results of every CI run to land on the requirements they verify, and the pipeline to fail when the trace is broken, so that "verified" means a test passed against the current revision and not only that a link exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A CI job uploads JUnit XML to a project with a personal access token or an app's token, naming the repository, the commit and the run's address
- [ ] A test case names the requirements it verifies by key, in its name, a property or a tag such as `[verifies CHK-R42]`; a key of a trashed or unknown requirement is reported back, not dropped
- [ ] Each requirement shows its latest results per test and per branch: passed, failed, skipped or errored, when, which commit and run, linking to it
- [ ] A result names the requirement's revision current when it arrived; a newer revision makes the evidence outdated, as a suspect link is
- [ ] Coverage can ask, per requirement type, that verified means a passing, current result rather than a link; the matrix, coverage, the chain report and the query language (`testResult`, `testOutdated`) follow
- [ ] A trace check, `GET /projects/{projectKey}/trace-check`, answers pass or fail with the broken chains, gaps and failing or outdated tests, narrowed by a query, for a pipeline to stop on; `make` and a container image wrap it for CI
- [ ] Results are kept for a set number of runs per branch; baselines record the evidence they held

## Tests

Unit: the JUnit reader over files from common test runners, key extraction. Integration: upload with token rights, evidence per revision, outdated after a revision, coverage by evidence, the trace check's verdicts, retention. vitest: the results panel, axe. Playwright: upload a result, see the requirement verified, revise it, see it outdated.

## Implementation

- A package `internal/testresult` and its tables; upload through the worker as imports run.

As a moderator of a specification review, I want to send a section, a baseline or a query's requirements to a group of reviewers as one review with a deadline, follow its progress and close it with a report and sign-off, so that a document is agreed in one round instead of requirement by requirement.

- [ ] Participants read the session as the document in review mode (#171), approve, reject or comment per requirement, with the signature where the project signs approvals (#46)
- [ ] Progress shows per requirement and per participant; reminders go out before the deadline
- [ ] The moderator starts a new round after changes: requirements revised since are pinned anew, the rest keep their decisions, and each round compares with the last

- [ ] A session's approvals are approvals of the revisions they name, so the workflow condition "Approved" honours them

issues.title: Check requirements against writing rules as they are written
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want each requirement checked against writing rules as I write it, with a score and what to fix, so that the specification is clear, testable and consistent before it is reviewed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rules check a requirement's title and statement: vague and unbounded words, `and/or`, escape clauses, open placeholders such as TBD, passive voice without an agent, more than one shall, pronouns without a referent, negative statements, and the shape of the EARS patterns (ubiquitous, event, state, unwanted behaviour, optional feature)
- [ ] The editor marks each finding in the text as one types, with the rule and how to fix it
- [ ] Each requirement has a quality score; the specification, the grid and a project quality page show it, and the query language has `quality` and `qualityFinding`
- [ ] A project's administrators switch rules on and off, set their severity, add their own word lists, and say per requirement type which apply
- [ ] An author can mark a finding accepted with a reason, which stays with the revision
- [ ] A workflow condition can ask for a minimum score (agreed in #233: a validator, so the transition stays offered and its refusal says what to fix)
- [ ] The rules work without a network or a language model; an assistant over MCP reads the findings through a tool

## Tests

Unit: every rule over a corpus of good and bad sentences, in English and German. Integration: scores on save, settings, accepted findings, the query fields, the condition. vitest: the marks in the editor, the quality page, axe. Playwright: write a vague requirement, see the finding, fix it.

## Implementation

- A package `internal/quality`, pure functions over the plain text of `internal/document`, its findings stored per revision.
- Word lists per language in the package; the language is the project's.

## Depends on

- #13
- #47
- #232
- #233

issues.title: Find requirements that say the same thing
issues.body:
## User story

As an author or reviewer, I want to be told when a requirement says what another already says, so that the specification does not hold the same need twice in different words.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Writing or revising a requirement lists the most similar requirements of the project, and of library projects it may read, above a similarity the administrators set
- [ ] A project page lists likely duplicate pairs, best first, narrowed by type, section or query
- [ ] A pair can be dismissed as not a duplicate, with a reason; it stays dismissed until either side is revised
- [ ] A pair can be resolved by trashing one side and keeping its links on the other, or by linking them with a chosen link type
- [ ] Only what the reader may see is compared or shown
- [ ] An assistant over MCP reads the similar requirements of one requirement through a tool

## Tests

Unit: similarity over known pairs. Integration: the list on save, the project page, dismissals that come back on revision, merging links, rights. vitest: the hint in the editor, the page, axe. Playwright: write a near copy, see the hint, dismiss it.

## Implementation

- Trigram similarity in Postgres (`pg_trgm`) over the plain text, indexed, beside the full-text search of #20; no external service.
- Dismissals keep the revisions of both sides.

## Depends on

- #20
- #232
- #233
- #210

issues.title: Import a Word document as a specification
issues.body:
## User story

As a project lead taking over an existing specification, I want to import a Word document into a project, its headings becoming sections and its paragraphs requirements, so that I do not retype it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A project's administrators upload a `.docx` from the project settings, into the project or below a section
- [ ] Headings become sections by level; paragraphs, lists, tables and pictures below a heading become requirements, one per paragraph or one per heading as chosen
- [ ] Styles, a numbering pattern or a keyword such as `shall` can decide what becomes a requirement and what stays informative text
- [ ] A table can become one requirement or one per row, its columns mapped to the title, statement, rationale and attributes
- [ ] Before anything is written, a preview shows the tree with every choice and loss; the import then runs in the worker with its progress, as CSV and ReqIF imports do
- [ ] Rich text keeps bold, italics, lists, tables, links and pictures as the editor holds them
- [ ] Importing the same file again into the same place updates what it made as new revisions, by the identifiers kept from the first import

## Tests

Unit: the reader over committed documents with headings, lists, tables, pictures and odd styles. Integration: preview, import, re-import as revisions, refusals. vitest: the mapping and the preview, axe. Playwright: import a document and read it in the specification.

## Implementation

- Reading beside `internal/docx`, which writes; the result goes through the import path of #23 and #44.

- #23
- #44
- #232
- #233
- #208

issues.title: A glossary of terms, marked where requirements use them
issues.body:
## User story

As an author or reader, I want the project's terms defined once and marked where requirements use them, so that every reader understands a word the same way.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A project, or a library project for many, holds a glossary of terms, each with a definition, synonyms, terms not to use instead, and a status
- [ ] Terms have revisions and are found by search and the query language
- [ ] The editor marks a term where a requirement uses it and shows its definition on hover or focus; a word listed as not to use is a finding of the quality check (#207)
- [ ] An author can link a phrase to a term explicitly; the term lists the requirements that use it
- [ ] Changing a term's definition makes the requirements that use it suspect for their owners, as a link would
- [ ] The glossary is part of the Word, PDF and Markdown exports and of ReqIF

## Tests

Unit: term matching with synonyms and inflections. Integration: terms, revisions, usage, suspect on change, exports. vitest: the marks and the definition popover, the glossary page, axe. Playwright: define a term, see it marked in a requirement.

## Implementation

- Terms as their own table with revisions, not as requirements, so they never count in coverage.
- Matching on the plain text of `internal/document`, as the quality check does.

## Depends on

- #13
- #36
- #232
- #233
- #207

issues.title: Trace graph and impact of a requirement
issues.body:
## User story

As an engineer about to change a requirement, I want to see everything it traces to, up and down, as a graph, so that I know what a change affects before I make it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A requirement's page opens a graph centred on it: requirements, Armature issues and Stator pages as nodes, links as edges named by type and direction
- [ ] The graph follows links up, down or both, to a chosen depth, through chosen link types and relations
- [ ] Suspect links, broken links and gaps of the project's trace model are marked
- [ ] Nodes show key, title, type and status; opening one recentres the graph or opens the item
- [ ] An impact list beside the graph names everything reached, by level, and downloads as CSV
- [ ] Only what the reader may see is shown, and a node hidden from them is counted, not named
- [ ] The graph is reachable by keyboard and has a list form for screen readers
- [ ] Test results (#200) and code tags (#201) appear as nodes, with failing and outdated evidence marked

## Tests

Unit: the walk with depth, direction and types over a known graph. Integration: the endpoint with rights, Armature and Stator nodes, suspect marks. vitest: the graph and its list form, axe. Playwright: open a requirement's graph, follow a node.

## Implementation

- An endpoint in `internal/trace` beside the chain report, walking `trace_link` and the remote links.
- The graph drawn with React Flow, which the workflow designer already uses.
- Agreed in `docs/api-contract-m11.md` (#242); a neighbour the reader may not see is counted, never named.

## Depends on

- #18
- #27
- #41
- #151
- #241

issues.title: Dashboards over a project's requirements
issues.body:
## User story

As a project lead, I want a dashboard of charts and counters over my project's requirements, built from saved queries, so that I see progress, coverage and review status at a glance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A person makes dashboards, personal or shared with a project, from widgets: a breakdown by status, type, owner or an attribute; a count of a query; a query's list; coverage per dimension; review progress; suspect links; changes over time; quality scores where the quality check (#207) exists
- [ ] A widget reads a query in the query language or a saved view, live, as the reader
- [ ] Clicking a slice or a bar opens its requirements in the grid
- [ ] Dashboards are laid out by dragging, printed to PDF and shared by link to people who may read the project
- [ ] A project's home can show a dashboard; templates give a first one

## Tests

Unit: each widget's computation. Integration: widgets read as the reader, sharing, PDF. vitest: the grid, widgets, settings, axe. Playwright: build a dashboard and follow a chart to the grid.

## Implementation

- Armature's dashboards, `internal/report` and `web/src/features/dashboard`, adapted, credited in `NOTICE`, with widgets for requirements instead of issues.
- PDF through the render service of #45.
- Shared by link with the people who may read the project only; there is no public link without signing in. Agreed in `docs/api-contract-m11.md` (#242).

## Depends on

- #20
- #47
- #38
- #241

issues.title: Computed attributes and roll-ups
issues.body:
## User story

As a project administrator, I want attributes whose values are computed from other fields, from children or from linked items, so that sums, scores and rolled-up statuses stay right without anyone typing them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An attribute can be computed by a formula over the requirement's own fields and attributes: arithmetic, conditions, text and dates
- [ ] A formula can aggregate over children or linked items by link type and direction: count, sum, min, max, average, any and all
- [ ] Typical uses work out of the box: a priority score from weights, a section's share of approved children, a status rolled up from linked tests
- [ ] Computed values are read-only in the editor, update when what they read changes, and are found, ordered and exported like any attribute
- [ ] A formula that refers to itself through others is refused when saved, with the cycle named
- [ ] Changing a formula recomputes the project in the worker, with progress shown
- [ ] Computed values are not revisions; a baseline records the value it saw

## Tests

Unit: the formula language, aggregation, cycle detection. Integration: recomputation on change of the item, a child and a linked item, the worker recompute, export and query. vitest: the formula editor with completion and errors, axe. Playwright: define a roll-up and watch it change.

## Implementation

- A small expression language in `internal/attribute` with its own parser, in the style of `internal/rql`.
- Recomputation from a queue that database triggers fill in the same transaction as the change, so a change and the values it affects stay consistent; the outbox carries no event for some of what a formula reads, such as a move's old parent, and a project's recompute would outlast its lease. `docs/api-contract-m11.md` (#242) says why.
- Roll-ups read the requirement's own project only, so a stored value never counts what a reader may not see.

## Depends on

- #14
- #18
- #241

issues.title: Export through Word templates and as static HTML
issues.body:
## User story

As a documentation owner, I want to export a specification through my organisation's own Word template and as a static HTML site, so that what leaves Exciter looks like our other documents and can be read without an account.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A project's administrators upload Word templates whose styles, cover, headers and footers the export uses; placeholders bring in the project, the baseline, the date and the signers
- [ ] A template says which fields and attributes a requirement shows, in which order, and whether links, comments or change marks are included
- [ ] Templates can be shared by all projects and chosen when exporting a specification, a section, a baseline or a review report
- [ ] A static HTML export writes the specification as linked pages with its contents, trace links between them and a search, in a zip that opens offline
- [ ] Exports are audited, and a template that cannot be read is refused with what is wrong

## Tests

Unit: placeholder filling, field selection. Integration: upload, refuse, export with a template, the HTML zip. vitest: the template settings, axe. Playwright: export with a template and open the HTML.

## Implementation

- Builds on `internal/docx` of #45, which already writes documents; templates are files in the object store.
- The HTML export reuses the print view.
- A template belongs to a project and is uploaded by its administrators, who may share it with every project. The HTML site is taken from the print view by the render service. Agreed in `docs/api-contract-m11.md` (#242).

## Depends on

- #45
- #241

issues.title: Webhook guard test counts a delivery of its own setup now and then
issues.body:
### What happened, and what did you expect?

`TestRawSQLKeepsWebhooksToAdministrators` fails now and then: the administrator reads 3 rows of their webhook and its log where the test expects 2, the endpoint and the ping. It failed once in M8 and twice in M9, and passed on every rerun.

`newCommentWorld` writes requirements, and the worker handles their `requirement.created` events through the outbox. The test makes a webhook for every topic right after, so when the worker reaches one of those events after the webhook exists, it queues a delivery of it too. The test should wait for the outbox to drain before it makes the webhook, so the only delivery is its ping.

### Steps to reproduce

Run `make test-integration` a few times; the race is timing dependent.

### Version or commit

`main` at the merge of #229.

issues.title: Let a connected app take a narrower access token without narrowing its grant
issues.body:
## User story

As a connected app such as Rotor (Cloudster1/Rotor), I want a short-lived, narrower access token for one workflow run without changing the person's grant, so that a run holds only read access until a person confirms a write, and parallel runs don't fight over the refresh token.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `POST /oauth/token` accepts `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` (RFC 8693) with an access token of the grant as `subject_token`
- [ ] The requested `scope` must be within the grant's; the projects can be narrowed further
- [ ] The new token's lifetime is at most the subject token's remaining life and can be asked shorter
- [ ] Only an access token is issued, never a refresh token, and the grant is untouched
- [ ] The issued token is revocable by RFC 7009 and ends with the grant
- [ ] Capability `oauth.token-exchange@1` in `GET /api/v1/meta` and in the authorization-server metadata

## Tests

Unit: scope and lifetime checks. Integration: exchange to `mcp:read`, a write refused with it, the grant still allows writes after; a wider scope refused; revoking the grant ends exchanged tokens.

## Implementation

- Today `turnRefresh` stores `read_only` on the new refresh token and `issue()` writes it to both tokens (`backend/internal/oauth/tokens.go`), so narrowing on refresh narrows the grant for good; access tokens last a fixed hour (`oauth.go`).
- Add the exchange beside `turnRefresh`, reusing `issue()` for the access token only.

## Depends on

- #188

Needed by Cloudster1/Rotor#32 and the narrowing criterion of Cloudster1/Rotor#12.

issues.title: fix: a move can fail while computed attributes are worked out
issues.body:
## User story

As somebody who moves or edits requirements in a project with computed attributes, I want my change to go through every time, even while the worker is still working values out.

## What happens

Moving a requirement sometimes answers 500. CI caught it on #247: `TestComputedAttributesFollowWhatTheyRead` failed with "move Pedal force into Brakes: got 500".

**Cause: a lock-order deadlock on `computed_dirty`.**
- A change's trigger upserts several marks, `ON CONFLICT (requirement_id) DO UPDATE`: the requirement, its old parent and its new parent.
- At the same time, the worker locks a batch of marks (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`), deletes them, and upserts marks for the parents and link neighbours of what it worked out.
- The deadlock: the change inserts the parent's mark, then waits on a mark the worker holds. The worker then waits on the parent's mark the change just inserted.
- Postgres kills one of the two. When it picks the change, the user sees a 500.

## Acceptance criteria

- A mark never waits on the worker: the queue is append-only, with no unique key and no foreign keys whose cascades or checks take locks.
- The worker takes a project's marks under its advisory lock. Several marks of one requirement count once, with the lowest step count.
- What happens is unchanged:
  - values are worked out again after a change;
  - roll-ups follow children and links;
  - the cycle stop still holds;
  - the recompute's progress counts requirements, not marks.
- Marks of deleted requirements or projects are dropped by the worker.

## Tests

- Integration: many concurrent moves and edits while the worker drains; every change succeeds, and the values settle as expected.
- The existing computed-attribute tests pass unchanged.

## Implementation

- Migration `01121_computed_queue.sql`:
  - re-creates `computed_dirty` with an identity key and no unique or foreign keys;
  - redefines `computed_mark`, `computed_recompute` and `computed_progress`.
- `attribute.Recomputer.batch` deletes the marks it takes with `RETURNING`, instead of locking them; `mark` inserts plainly.

As a test manager and a tester, I want to group test cases into plans, run a plan against a version, a baseline or a configuration with testers assigned, record each step's result with notes and files, and file an Armature issue for a failure, so that verification is planned, done and evidenced beside the requirements.

As someone trying Exciter together with Armature and Stator, I want a demo whose requirements are the suite's own, traced to the issues that built them and to the pages that describe them, so that I see traceability on content I can check against the real tools.

issues.title: Give the database owner BYPASSRLS so a cnpg install can administer
issues.body:
## User story

As an operator installing Exciter with `cnpg.enabled`, I want the bootstrap and every administrator action to work, so that an installation on CloudNativePG is usable without a manual fix in the database.

Today the bootstrap Job stops at the identity provider:

```
seed failed: save the identity provider: ERROR: new row violates row-level security policy "oidc_provider_admins_only" for table "oidc_provider" (SQLSTATE 42501)
```

The permission functions are `SECURITY DEFINER` and read `app_user`, `org_member` and the other walled tables as the migration role that owns them. Those tables are `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, and their policies name `exciter_app` and `exciter_admin` only. In the compose stack and with the bundled Postgres the owner is a superuser, which passes every policy, so nothing noticed. Under cnpg the chart makes the owner `exciter_owner`, neither superuser nor `BYPASSRLS`: `current_actor_administers()` sees no account and answers false for everybody, so the bootstrap administrator may not save a provider, and no administrator may do anything walled.

## Acceptance criteria

- With `cnpg.enabled`, the Cluster lists the owner role under `managed.roles` with `bypassrls: true`, so the operator grants it on a fresh install and on an existing one at the next reconcile.
- `migrate up`, `up-to` and `down` refuse an owner that is neither superuser nor `BYPASSRLS`, with a sentence saying what to grant, so an external database with such an owner fails at the migration instead of at the first administrator action.
- `docs/deployment.md` says what the owner needs; `docs/decisions.md` records why.

## Tests

- `tests/test-helm.sh`: the cnpg render gives the owner `bypassrls: true`, with its own password Secret; the golden `tests/helm/production.yaml` is regenerated.
- Integration: a role made `NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS` is refused by the owner check, and passes once it is altered to `BYPASSRLS`.

## Implementation

- `deploy/charts/exciter/templates/cnpg-cluster.yaml`: add the owner to the managed roles, with the `dbOwner` Secret.
- `backend/migrations`: an owner check the migrate command runs before it changes the schema.

## Depends on

Nothing.

issues.title: Keep the outbox tests from racing the stack's worker
issues.body:
`TestTheWorkerHoldsNoLockWhileItHandles` (backend/test/outbox_test.go) fails by chance, so any PR's CI can go red without a cause in the PR. It failed on #277, whose change does not touch the outbox, and passed when CI ran again:

```
outbox_test.go:312: the stack's worker took every one of 5 events first
--- FAIL: TestTheWorkerHoldsNoLockWhileItHandles (25.10s)
```

**Why it fails:** the test plants an event in the shared `outbox_event` table and waits for its own worker to claim it, but the stack's worker polls the same table. Whichever claims first wins. The test gives up after `claimTries` (5) offers of `claimWait` (5 s) each, so on a busy runner, or when the stack's worker polls more often than the test's, the stack's worker can take all five. The other tests that use `claimTries` (the `offerer`) depend on the same race.

**What would make it reliable:** the test's worker has to be the only one able to claim its events. For example:
- plant the test's events under a topic or partition that the stack's worker does not claim, or
- pause the stack's worker for the test, or
- give the claim query a filter that only the test's worker passes.

Retrying more times only makes the failure rarer.

**Done when:** the outbox tests never depend on beating the stack's worker, and the integration layer passes them on a loaded runner, for example with `go test -count=20 -run 'Outbox|Worker'` against the running stack.

issues.title: Give settings an area of their own and keep personal pages under the avatar
issues.body:
The three tools that run together (Stator, Armature, Exciter) are moving to one menu layout, described in praetorianer777/Dynamo#12: personal pages under the avatar, administration in a settings area of its own, the sidebar for work. Exciter is close already: personal pages sit under the avatar, and `places.ts` already feeds the sidebar, the palette and the breadcrumbs. What is left is the top bar, Settings in the main sidebar and a profile page. This is Exciter's part.

## Top bar goes
- The breadcrumbs move into the page header's sticky strip, as in the other two tools.
- The quick-switcher button and the waiting-reviews button are removed.
- The avatar and its menu move to the bottom of the rail.
- On narrow screens, a thin strip with "Open the navigation" stays.
- The notification bell moves to the rail, after Search. Its panel stays as it is.

## Rail
- In order: toggle, Home, Search, Notifications (bell), Projects.
- Settings leaves the rail's main block.
- Bottom: the theme switch and the avatar.

## Avatar menu
The avatar opens the menu, folded or not:
- A header with name, email and role.
- Your profile, Notification settings, Watching, Themes, Access tokens, Connected apps, in this order.
- The connected tools (#298).
- **Settings**, for administrators only, opening the settings area.
- Sign out.

The language leaves the menu for Your profile.

**Your profile is a new page** (`/settings/profile`): Exciter has none. It holds the person's name and the interface language, still saved to the account.

## Settings area
The Settings group leaves the main sidebar. `/settings` and the pages under it get a sidebar of their own in place of the main one, headed by "Back to Exciter", which returns to the last page outside it.
- **You:** Your profile, Notification settings, Watching, Themes, Access tokens, Connected apps, Armature account, Stator account.
- **Settings**, for administrators only, in this order:
  - Installation
  - Members
  - Single sign-on
  - Default theme
  - Link types
  - All tokens
  - All connected apps
  - Armature
  - Stator
  - Webhooks
  - Audit log

`/settings` stops redirecting to Members. It becomes a hub page with a "You" card and a "Settings" card for administrators. The "Settings" breadcrumb links there.

## Sidebar
**Requirements group:** Home, Search, Notifications (`/notifications`, with the unread count), Reviews (with the waiting count that was the top-bar button), Projects.

**Project group:**
- Keeps its switcher and pages.
- Trash, Project settings and Permissions move into a nested "Project admin" group, folded by default, with today's conditions.
- When the route names no project, the last one visited is shown, as in Armature.

**Foot:** the build string.

## Done when
- The avatar menu holds personal pages, the connected tools, Settings for administrators and Sign out.
- No installation-wide page is in the main sidebar; each is reachable from the settings area and the palette, for administrators only.
- The language is set on Your profile and still saved to the account.
- The palette offers the new Your profile.
- The e2e suite checks the avatar menu and the settings area for an administrator and a member, and the drawer at phone width.
