issues.title: Architecture drawings in PlantUML, drawn in every view and edited as text
issues.body:
## User story

As a systems engineer, I want to draw architecture diagrams in PlantUML inside a requirement, so that the structure a requirement asks for is shown beside its words and stays editable as text that is versioned with it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The editor inserts a PlantUML diagram into a statement, rationale or rich text value; it is edited as PlantUML text with a live preview below it
- [ ] Every view that shows a requirement's text shows the drawn picture: the requirement, the document view, history, baselines, comparisons and print
- [ ] A diagram that cannot be drawn shows its source and the first line of why; a server without a renderer shows the source and says so
- [ ] Only the PlantUML text is stored; history diffs it as text and search finds its words
- [ ] Markdown in and out writes a diagram as a `plantuml` fenced block; ReqIF, CSV and Excel carry the source
- [ ] PDF, Word and the static site show the picture; Word embeds it as PNG and falls back to the source with a note
- [ ] Diagrams are drawn by a Kroki container that only the api reaches, in its secure mode, so a diagram can include no file or address; compose and the Helm chart ship it pinned

## Tests

Go unit: the allowlist's diagram node and its limits, the Markdown fence both ways, the source diff, the Kroki client (SVG, PNG, syntax error, timeout, busy, cache, size cap), Word with a picture and with the fallback, the settings. Integration against the stack's Kroki: the route draws, refuses broken source with Kroki's sentence and refuses an include, search finds a diagram's words, Markdown keeps it, Word holds the PNG. vitest: the figure, its fallbacks and the editor node. Playwright: add a diagram, type PlantUML, watch the preview, save, see the picture on the requirement and in the document view, with an accessibility check.

## Implementation

- A `diagram` block node (`language`: `plantuml`, `source`: up to 20000 characters), adapted from Stator's diagram node.
- `internal/diagram`: a Kroki client modelled on `internal/render`, with a small cache, behind `POST /api/v1/diagrams`; `EXCITER_KROKI_URL`, `_TIMEOUT`, `_CONCURRENCY`, blank leaving drawing off.
- The web shows the SVG as a `data:` image, so nothing in it runs and the CSP stays as it is.
- Migration range 01380 to 01399: search reads a diagram's source.

## Depends on

Nothing.

issues.title: Architecture diagrams in the suite demo's specifications
issues.body:
## User story

As someone trying Exciter with the suite demo, I want each tool's specification to carry its architecture as drawings, so that I see how PlantUML diagrams read in requirements and learn how Armature, Exciter and Stator are built, how people sign in and how the tools reach each other.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **A section of drawings:** each of the three demo projects gets a top-level section "Architecture" after the introduction, with one requirement per view, each statement holding a PlantUML diagram and a few sentences on what it shows.
- [ ] **The views:** for every tool at least its components and data stores, its deployment, its sign-in flow (password and OIDC, sessions, API tokens) and how it reaches the other two tools of the suite; a tool gets more where its architecture document has more to say.
- [ ] **True to the tool:** every diagram is drawn from the tool's own `docs/architecture.md` and code at the snapshot's commit, and its rationale links that document.
- [ ] **Traced:** each architecture requirement is linked to the tool's architecture page in Stator, as the requirement about the tool is.
- [ ] **Every diagram draws:** no diagram of the demo shows a syntax error.

## Tests

- [ ] Unit: the plan gives every project its architecture items, each statement converts to a document holding a diagram, and the build steps stay as they were.
- [ ] Integration: every diagram of the demo draws through the stack's Kroki, and a built demo holds the architecture section with its diagrams.

## Implementation

- The diagrams live as Markdown, one file per tool, embedded in `backend/internal/demo` beside the snapshot.
- The project step makes the section and its requirements after the requirement about the tool; `suite_demo_requirement` records them as issue 0 with a criterion of their position, so linking again finds them.

## Depends on

- #284

issues.title: Stop test-release.sh failing on a leftover git process
issues.body:
`tests/test-release.sh` fails by chance in the "shell and format" job. It failed on `main` at d6dd00c8:

```
The test fixture broke while removing the previous case's repository. The error above is the cause; fix it and run the script again.
```

**Cause:** `use_fixture` removes the previous case's `repo` and `repo.remote` before copying the next one. A git process the previous case left behind can still be writing into the remote, so `rm -rf` fails on a directory that isn't empty. Stator had the same fixture and the same failure (praetorianer777/Stator#475, fixed in praetorianer777/Stator#476).

**Fix:** give each case a directory of its own (`repo-1`, `repo-2`, ...) instead of removing the last one. The `EXIT` trap still removes everything.

## Done when
- `use_fixture` no longer removes anything.
- `tests/test-release.sh` passes.

issues.title: Let release.sh cut a release with a long commit history
issues.body:
`release.sh` passes the commits since the last tag to Python in the environment variable `RAW_LOG`. Before the first tag that's the whole history, now 120 KB on `main`, and Linux refuses any single environment string over 128 KB (`MAX_ARG_STRLEN`). A few more commits and `./release.sh` fails before writing anything with "python3: Argument list too long". Stator hit exactly this (praetorianer777/Stator#485, fixed in praetorianer777/Stator#486). The release commit's `-m "$(cat notes)"` has the same limit.

**Fix:** as in Stator: the log goes to a temporary file whose path Python reads, and the commit uses `-F`.

## Done when
- `tests/test-release.sh` has a first release with a history far over 128 KB, and it passes.

issues.title: Shard the integration tests in CI
issues.body:
In CI, `test-integration` is the slowest job: about 10 minutes in a single job on the last green `main`. The whole run takes about as long as that job. Stator runs the same layer as 3 jobs of about 6 minutes each, each with its own stack.

**Change:** split `test-integration` into shards, as Stator does:
- `mk/go.mk` lists the tests with `go test -list`, and a `SHARD=i/n` variable picks every n-th one into `-run`;
- CI runs a matrix of 3 jobs, each starting its own stack, and the report job merges their JSON reports.

Pick the shard count from the measured time, so no shard runs much over 4 minutes.

## Done when
- CI's integration jobs each take at most about 4 to 5 minutes, and the report still lists every test once.
- `make test-integration` without `SHARD` still runs everything locally.

issues.title: Find why /risks answered 500 in the FMEA timing test
issues.body:
On `main` at 50087fed, `TestTheFMEATableReadsManyRisksInGoodTime` (`backend/test/risk_mitigations_test.go:255`) failed:

```
/risks?limit=200: got 500, want 200: {"error":{"code":"internal_error",...,"requestId":"40a4193d-a23b-4531-b756-5a1d0afc7534"}}
```

It passed on fe745e6f, and the only change between them was `release.sh`. It also passed 10 of 10 times locally on its own. So it fails only some of the time, probably under the load of the whole suite.

**What's missing:** the cause. The test talks to the stack's api container, which logs `request failed` with the error. CI keeps the test reports but not the stack's logs, so request 40a4193d can't be traced.

**Leads:**
- `risk.Service.Rows` reads through `db.Read`, which routes to the streaming replica (`hot_standby=on`). A long read there can be cancelled with "canceling statement due to conflict with recovery" (SQLSTATE 40001) while the primary vacuums, which comes back as a 500. `hot_standby_feedback` isn't set.
- Alternatively, a statement or request timeout under CI's load: the test writes 100 risks with 300 links just before.

**Fix:**
1. CI keeps `docker compose logs` of the stack as an artifact when a stack layer fails.
2. With the cause known: fix it at its source. For a replica conflict, that means `hot_standby_feedback=on` on the replica, or retrying a read cancelled for recovery on the primary. Don't loosen the test.

## Done when
- A failed CI run keeps the stack's logs.
- The cause is named here, and the fix makes the test pass 20 times in a row inside a full suite run.

issues.title: Sign in silently when the identity provider already has a session
issues.body:
Someone signed in to Armature, Stator or Exciter through the suite's Keycloak realm, who then opens another of the three, lands on its sign-in page and has to click "Sign in". Keycloak still has their session, so the click sends them there and straight back, signed in, without a password. The click is all that's left, but it happens on every first visit and on every link from one tool to another. This was seen on a real Dynamo install, where Keycloak returns at once.

**Change:** on a visit without a session, Exciter first tries a silent sign-in:
- **The request:** a top-level redirect to the provider's authorization endpoint with `prompt=none`, the usual `state`, PKCE and `nonce`, and the page the person asked for.
- **Keycloak still has a session:** the callback signs the person in, as a normal sign-in does, with the same group mapping and membership checks, and returns them to that page.
- **No session** (`error=login_required`, `interaction_required` or `consent_required`): the callback shows the sign-in page as today, and remembers for the browser session (a short-lived cookie) that the silent try already failed, so there's no redirect loop and no second round trip on the next page.
- **Only when single sign-on is configured:** with local accounts only, nothing changes.
- **Not after signing out:** a sign-out sets the same marker, so the person isn't signed straight back in. With RP-initiated logout at the provider, the provider's session ends too.
- **Can be turned off:** a setting, for example `auth.silentSignIn` in the chart, on by default when an OIDC provider is set.

## Done when
- In the integration or browser tests, with a provider that has a session, opening a deep link without a session lands on that page signed in, with no click. Without a provider session, it lands on the sign-in page, and the next page doesn't redirect again.
- After signing out, the next visit shows the sign-in page.
- `GET /api/v1/meta` lists `auth.silent-sign-in@1`, so the suite's tests can rely on it (praetorianer777/Dynamo#2).

issues.title: Send relation requirement with the remote links synced to Armature
issues.body:
When Exciter syncs a trace link to Armature, it puts the requirement on the issue through `POST /issues/{issueKey}/remote-links` with `url`, `title`, `source` and `iconUrl`, but no `relation` (`backend/internal/armature/sync.go`, `RemoteLinkRequest`). Armature then files it as a `page`, so the issue shows the requirement it implements among its pages.

Armature's remote links take `relation: requirement` for "a requirement the issue implements" (`backend/internal/issue/remotelinks.go`, `RemoteLinkRequirement`); sending a url already there updates the relation when one is sent, so existing links would be corrected on the next sync.

Seen in Dynamo's sample import (praetorianer777/Dynamo#24) against Exciter 0.1.0 and Armature 0.1.0: `GET /api/v1/issues/SPARK-1/remote-links` lists the Exciter requirement with `"relation":"page"`, though Exciter traced SPARK-R1 to SPARK-1 as `implements`.

**Expected:** the remote link of an `implements` (and `verifies`) trace carries `relation: requirement`, when Armature's capabilities list it.

issues.title: Link the connected tools in the avatar menu
issues.body:
Clicking one's profile picture opens a small menu. When Exciter is connected to Armature or Stator, that menu should also link to them, so people can switch tools in one click.

## What the menu shows
- Under the account entries, a group "Switch to" with one entry per tool Exciter is connected to: its name and its icon.
- Each entry opens that tool's home at the public address of the connection an administrator set up, the one dynamo-connect configures.
- It is a plain link, so the browser's open-in-new-tab works too.
- A tool is listed once the organization's connection to it is configured, whether or not the person connected their own account there; with single sign-on the other tool signs them in.
- A tool that is not connected, or whose connection an administrator removed, is not listed. With none, the group is not shown.
- Everyone signed in sees it, guests included, since the other tool decides what they may see.

## Fits the shared layout
The menus of the three tools are moving to one layout (praetorianer777/Dynamo#12). The group belongs in the avatar menu wherever that layout keeps it, in the same place and under the same name in all three. The same issue is filed in each tool.

## Done when
- With Armature and Stator connected, the avatar menu lists both and each link opens that tool's home.
- With one connected, only it is listed; with none, the group is gone.
- A test covers each of these.

issues.title: Make a provider group before its first member signs in
issues.body:
Exciter learns a sign-in provider's group only when one of its members signs in (groups are synced at sign-in, `GET /groups` only). So an administrator, or Dynamo's connect job, cannot grant a realm group access to a project (`PUT /projects/{key}/grants`) before anyone in that group has signed in.

Armature already allows it: `POST /groups` with `name` and `externalRef`, matched to the claim at sign-in.

## Done when
- `POST /groups` with `name` and `externalRef` makes a provider group that a later sign-in with that group in its claim joins, instead of making a second one.
- A second request for the same `externalRef` answers 409, or returns the group, as Armature does.
- The group can be named in project permissions straight away.
- Integration test: make the group, grant it on a project, sign in a person of that group, and they see the project.

Needed so the three tools can grant the same access per group (praetorianer777/Dynamo, issue filed with this one).

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XsypREK6CTfvi1885SVu2k

issues.title: Map a provider group to a read-only standing
issues.body:
A group mapping (`POST /oidc-provider/group-roles`) grants only `member` or `admin` (`grouproles.go`). A realm group of readers therefore gets every grant `everyone` has, such as editing each new project, with no way to admit them read-only by group.

## Done when
- A group can map to `guest` (or a read-only standing named so), which admits its people at sign-in without the rights `everyone` grants to members.
- Integration test: a person in a group mapped this way can sign in and read a project open to everyone, and cannot change it.

Asked for so the three tools give a realm group of readers the same standing everywhere (see the Dynamo issue filed with this one).

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XsypREK6CTfvi1885SVu2k

issues.title: Provision and deprovision people and groups through SCIM
issues.body:
Groups and roles reach Exciter only when a person signs in. Somebody removed from a group in the realm, or switched off there, keeps their access in Exciter until their next sign-in, and their sessions and tokens keep working.

Armature has the same need as Cloudster1/Armature#108; the three tools should take the same SCIM 2.0 shape, so one provider configuration serves all three.

## Done when
- `/scim/v2/Users` and `/scim/v2/Groups` (create, update, patch, deactivate) behind a SCIM token an administrator makes.
- Deactivating a user ends their sessions and tokens at once.
- Group membership changes apply without a sign-in, including the roles the group maps to.
- Tests against the SCIM endpoints, as Armature's.

issues.title: Branch-guard test fails when EXCITER_GATE=full is in the environment
issues.body:
`./run-tests.sh` run with `EXCITER_GATE=full` in the environment fails its shell layer, on main as on any branch:

```
FAIL  gate ran 'shell check-format check-go test-integration test-e2e'
FAIL: branch-guard tests
```

`.claude/hooks/tests/branch-guard-test.sh` (around line 323) runs the guard once expecting the quick gate (`shell check-format check-go`) and once with `EXCITER_GATE=full`. It does not clear `EXCITER_GATE` first, so a caller that exported `EXCITER_GATE=full`, as a full local run or a push with the full gate does, makes the first case run the full layers and the test fail.

Reproduce: `EXCITER_GATE=full ./.claude/hooks/tests/branch-guard-test.sh`.

**Expected:** the test sets the variable for each case itself (`env -u EXCITER_GATE` for the quick case), so it passes whatever the caller's environment holds.

issues.title: test-traceability.spec reads the execution before the pipeline's result is recorded

issues.title: Test requirements, their history, locks, labels and the editor end to end
issues.body:
Writing and reading requirements is well covered. `requirements_test.go` refuses bad fields, a viewer, a stale save and a save without its comment, and walks the trash through restore, purge and empty with the editor refused. `history_test.go` lists, compares, restores and pages the activity with their refusals. `labels_test.go` and `label_rls_test.go` cover putting labels on, the bound of fifty and the suggestions. `control_test.go` covers the status lock and the hand lock, also through SQL. `requirement_rls_test.go` covers numbering, history that only grows and purging. `markdown_test.go` and `diagram_test.go` cover Markdown and PlantUML. In the browser, `requirement-crud.spec.ts` writes, revises, owns, trashes, restores and purges, `history.spec.ts` compares with the previous revision and restores, `labels.spec.ts` coins and finds a label, and `markdown.spec.ts`, `diagrams.spec.ts` and the lock scenario in `control.spec.ts` cover the rest. Vitest covers the list, the page, the permalink, the trash's restore and purge, the history, labels and locks. What is missing: nobody asks a viewer to restore a revision, and nobody restores a revision of a locked or trashed requirement. Nobody copies a trashed requirement, copies past the limit or copies into a project they only read. Locking is refused only to an editor and only on a section. No MCP test calls `list_revisions`, `get_revision` or `diff_revisions`. Through SQL, nobody writes in an archived project, forges another person's name on a revision or change, or passes the label bound. In the browser, nobody locks or unlocks by hand, copies, removes the owner, empties the trash, opens one revision, compares two selected ones, or uses any toolbar button but Bold. The link dialog, the trash's empty and the owner's controls have no component test. The editor has no slash items: the toolbar is the only way into its blocks.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these writes were never answered 403: `POST /diagrams`, `POST /projects/{projectKey}/trash/{requirementID}/restore`, `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/revisions/{revisionNumber}/restore`; these were never answered 422: `DELETE /projects/{projectKey}/trash`, `DELETE /projects/{projectKey}/trash/{requirementID}`, `POST /projects/{projectKey}/trash/{requirementID}/restore`, `DELETE /requirements/{reqKey}`, `DELETE /requirements/{reqKey}/labels/{labelName}`, `DELETE /requirements/{reqKey}/lock`, `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/revisions/{revisionNumber}/restore`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #379: the trash routes, `DELETE /requirements/{reqKey}` and `DELETE .../lock` take nothing past the path, so their 403 and 409 are asserted; the label route's 422 on `labelName` and the restore's 422 on `comment` are; `POST /diagrams` is 403 for read-only, project-limited and evidence tokens)
- [x] `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/revisions/{revisionNumber}/restore`: a viewer is 403 `forbidden` and no revision is written. Restoring on a requirement locked by its status or by hand is 409 `requirement_locked`, the database's sentence is the message, and the revision count is unchanged. On a trashed requirement it is 409 `requirement_trashed`, and in an archived project 409 `project_archived`. With `requireRevisionComment` set, a restore without a comment either takes the default "Restored revision N" or is refused: decide which and assert it. Only a guest (404) and bad numbers are tried today, in history_test.go. (decided in #379: it takes the default)
- [x] `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/copy`: copying a trashed requirement is 409 `requirement_trashed`. A copy `children: true` of more than `requirement.MaxCopy` is 422 on `children`. A viewer of the project copying within it is 403. An editor copying into a project they only view is 403, and into an archived project 409 `project_archived`. In every case the target's requirement count is unchanged. A copy with `children: true` of a section whose child was trashed on its own leaves that child out, and `copied` counts only the live ones. Only a guest (404) and bad places are tried today, in tree_test.go.
- [x] `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/lock`: a viewer is 403 and a guest 404. A trashed requirement is 409 `section_not_locked`. A reason of 501 characters is 422 on `reason`. In an archived project it is 403 and the row keeps `locked_at` NULL. Locking again with a new reason answers the new reason and logs a second `lock` change from `locked` to `locked`. Only an editor's 403, a blank reason and a section are tried today, in control_test.go. (decided in #379: 409 `project_archived`, as every change in an archived project)
- [x] A locked requirement and labels: `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/labels` and `DELETE /requirements/{reqKey}/labels/{labelName}` on a requirement locked by hand either succeed, like owner and priority, or are refused. Decide and assert it. control_test.go checks comments, owner and priority but not labels. (decided in #379: they succeed)

Database guards:

Only an editor's call is tried today, in control_test.go.

Test what happens today, and decide whether a restore must pass (see the separate report). Browser (e2e scenario):

issues.title: Test moves in the tree, the specification page and its document exports end to end
issues.body:
The tree and the document are covered well where they were built: `tree_test.go` numbers the tree, moves within a project and to another and refuses a move under itself, `tree_rls_test.go` tries the cycle, same project and fixed number guards and two moves that would close a loop together through SQL, `document_test.go` covers editing in place, bulk transitions, the status and category filter, the three change bases and the bulk review request, and `documents_test.go`, `export_templates_test.go` and `mcp_resources_test.go` read the project, a section and a baseline as JSON, Word, PDF, HTML site and Markdown. In the browser `spec-tree.spec.ts` drags in the tree and moves to another project, `document.spec.ts` edits from the keyboard, adds after an entry, asks before a draft is lost, moves states in bulk, marks changes against the previous revision and a baseline and reviews in place, and `documents.spec.ts` downloads the whole specification as PDF and Word; `tree.test.tsx`, `document.test.tsx`, `documentReviews.test.tsx` and `print.test.tsx` test the pieces. What is missing is every refusal of a move but the guest's 404 and the lock's 409: nobody tries a reader, an archived project, a status left unmapped or a bad place, and a move with a status mapping never succeeds in any test. The `requirement.moved` webhook is skipped in `webhook_events_test.go`, `get_tree` is never called over MCP, and no test reads an entry's `can` flags. The document is never read for a nested section, past its 1000 entries, or with a link into a project the reader cannot see. In the browser nobody uses the tree from the keyboard, turns to the next page of the document, narrows it by one status, shows only what changed, enters review mode from the page, opens an entry's comments, adds first below a section, exports a section, or signs an approval in the document.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these writes were never answered 403: `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/copy`, `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/move`, `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/reuse`, `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/reuse/variant`; these were never answered 422: `DELETE /export-templates/{templateID}`, `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/reuse/take`, `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/reuse/variant`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #378: copy and move 403 are tested here, reuse and variant 403 in #376; take, variant and a template deletion have no 422 to give, a take's revision being refused with 409 `source_moved_on`, a variant taking no body and a deletion no input.)
- [x] `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/move` refused to a non-editor: a member who only reviews the project gets 403 `forbidden`, and `GET /projects/{projectKey}/tree` still reads the same outlines. Only a guest's 404 is tried today in tree_test.go.
- [x] `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/move` in an archived project, and to an archived project by `projectKey`, are both 409 `project_archived` and nothing moves. A move by `projectKey` into a project where the mover only reads is 403, over the API (only the SQL policy is tried, in tree_rls_test.go).
- [x] `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/move` to another project whose workflow has no status of the requirement's name: without `statusMapping` it is 422 on `statusMapping` naming the missing status, and no requirement of the subtree moved or got a new key. With a mapping to a status of that workflow it lands in that status, and a mapping to a status of another workflow is refused the same way. Only the within-project refusal of a mapping is tried today in tree_test.go.
- [x] `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/move` with a bad place: `afterId` of a sibling under another parent, `afterId` equal to the moving requirement, and `parentId` of a requirement in the trash are each 422 on `place.afterId` or `place.parentId`. Only `place under itself` is tried for a move; the afterId case is tried only for copy.
- [x] A section whose child is locked (`requirement_lock`) moved by `projectKey` to another project is 409 `requirement_locked`, and the section and every child keep their project, keys and numbers. control_test.go only moves the locked requirement itself within its project.
- [x] After a move to another project, somebody who views only the old project asks for the old key with `GET /requirements/{reqKey}` and gets 404 `not_found`, and the answer names neither the new key nor the title. Only an editor of both projects follows the old key today.
- [x] Webhook `requirement.moved`: a move to another project posts one delivery per moved requirement with `fromKey`, `toKey`, the actor and the requirement's new url, and a move within a project posts none. webhook_events_test.go skips this topic today.
- [x] `GET /projects/{projectKey}/spec` answers each entry's `can` as the reader stands: an editor gets edit, delete, link and transition; a reviewer gets transition and comment but no edit; everything but comment is false in an archived project (decided in #378: comment is false too, since a comment in an archived project is refused with 409 `project_archived`); and edit, delete and link are false on a locked entry. No test reads `can` on a spec entry today.
- [x] MCP `get_tree` through `/api/v1/mcp` answers the outlines and keys `GET /projects/{projectKey}/tree` answers, and a guest's token gets `isError`. No test calls the tool today.
- [x] `GET /projects/{projectKey}/document?section=` of a nested section (1.2 with children, followed by 1.3 and 2): the document holds 1.2 and what is below it only, the section is at depth 0, and `total` counts only those entries. A section key in the trash is 404. Only a top-level section is read today in documents_test.go.
- [x] A document whose requirement links to a requirement in a project the reader cannot view: `GET /projects/{projectKey}/document`, `document.docx` and `document.md` leave that link out, and none of them carries the other key or title. Today both ends of every link tried are in one project.
- [x] A project with more than `specdoc.MaxEntries` (1000) requirements, written through SQL: `GET /projects/{projectKey}/document` answers 1000 entries with `total` 1001, the Word file ends with the sentence "This document holds the first 1000 of the 1001 requirements", and `?section=` of the last section holds all of it. Truncation is tried only in the Markdown unit test today.

Database guards:
- [x] Two sessions as `exciter_app` move one requirement from project A to B and another from B to A at the same moment, each `UPDATE requirement SET project_id`: both land, neither deadlocks, and each takes a distinct number in its new project. Only two moves within one project are raced today in tree_rls_test.go.
- [x] Through SQL, `UPDATE requirement SET rank = 'a-b'` is refused by `requirement_rank_shape`, and `UPDATE requirement SET parent_id` to a requirement in the trash: decide whether the database refuses it, as `rankAt` does, and try it either way. (decided in #378: the database now refuses it with `requirement_parent_live`) Today the trigger only checks the project.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] Tree from the keyboard: focus a tree item, ArrowLeft folds a section and ArrowRight opens it again, M opens "Move <key>" (`data-place-dialog="move"`), pick a parent under "Below" and press "Move" (`confirm-move`). The tree and the document both read the new outline. Only dragging is used today.
- [x] Paging: a project with 55 requirements shows 50 entries, "Show more" (`data-action="spec-more"`) adds the rest with their outlines continuing at 51, and no entry repeats. No scenario clicks it today.
- [x] Status filter: pick one status under "Status" (`data-filter-status`), only those requirements and the sections above them stay and the address keeps it; "Show every status" (`clear-status-filter`) brings back everything. A filter matching nothing shows "No requirement is in those statuses". Only a category chip is clicked today.
- [x] Changes: with "Show changes" on, "Only changed" (`data-filter="only-changed"`) folds unchanged entries to their heading, "Previous change" (`previous-change`) steps back, and against a baseline a requirement trashed since then is listed under "No longer in the document" (`data-spec-removed`). Only "Next change" and the base selects are used today.
- [x] Review mode from the page: bob opens `/p/<key>/spec`, presses "Review what waits for me" (`data-action="review-mode"`), sees only what waits for him with "0 of 2 decided", and with nothing waiting sees the empty notice. document.spec.ts reaches review mode only through the link on /reviews today.
- [x] Entry comments and adding below: "Comments (1 open)" (`entry-comments`) opens the threads inside the entry and a reply posted there shows on the requirement's page. "Add next to <key>" then "First below this" (`add-below`) on a section writes 1.1 and moves the old 1.1 to 1.2. Only "After this" is used today.
- [x] Section export and its print view: the section's own "Export <title>" menu on the spec page, then "Word", downloads a file holding the section and what is below it and nothing else. `/print/p/<key>/document?section=<key>-R1` reads "Section <key> of <name>" and says it is ready. documents.spec.ts uses only the page's first export menu today.
- [x] Signed approval in the document: in a project with signed approvals, bob's "Approve" (`approve-entry`) in review mode opens the signature dialog, his password signs it, the entry shows his decision and the review's decision is signed. The document scenario today only approves without signing.

Component (vitest):
- [x] RequirementTree: Arrow keys, Home and End move focus, ArrowRight and ArrowLeft open and fold, Enter navigates to the requirement, and M calls the move only when the project is editable and open. A reader's rows are not draggable and carry no `aria-keyshortcuts`. A drag over its own descendant is not accepted and sends no POST. Only the drop-zone arithmetic is tested today in tree.test.tsx.
- [x] EntryReview with `settings.signedApprovals`: "Approve" opens SignDialog and sends no decision itself, and a signature resumed after the identity provider (`resumeSigning`) reopens the dialog for that review only. PlaceDialog: a 422 on `statusMapping` from a move to another project shows its sentence in the banner and keeps the dialog open.

Go unit:
- [x] `httpapi.documentError`: `render.ErrBusy` maps to 503 `render_busy`, `ErrTimeout` to 504 `render_timeout`, `ErrTooLarge` to 422 `render_too_large`, `ErrFailed` to 502 `render_failed`, `docx.ErrTooLarge` to 422 `docx_too_large`, `specdoc.ErrNoSection` to 404, and anything else to nil. None of these codes appears in any test today. Also cover the truncation note `docx/spec.go` writes when `doc.Truncated()`.

## Done when
- Every control of `/p/$projectKey/spec` (the tree, the export menus of the page and of a section, Show more, the status filter, the changes bar, review mode, entry comments, add, edit) is used by a browser scenario that checks what it changed.
- `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/move` has an integration test for each of its refusals (403, 409 archived, 409 locked, 422 place, 422 statusMapping) that checks nothing moved, and one for a move with a status mapping.
- The document, Word and Markdown exports are tested for a nested section, a document past 1000 entries and a link the reader may not follow.
- The `requirement.moved` webhook and the `get_tree` tool are tested.

issues.title: Test the grid's paging, inline edits and shared views, and the search screen's filters and pages
issues.body:
The grid's narrowing and the query language are well covered. `grid_test.go` tries every field filter, every attribute operator and the column orders, and refuses bad conditions with 422. `query_test.go` and `query_trace_test.go` run the language over fields, attributes, links, coverage and approval, place a refused query at its character, and test the completions. `view_rls_test.go` and `matrix_views_test.go` hold saved views to their owners through SQL. `search_test.go` covers words, ranking, marks, the category, label, project and day filters, quick search and the trash. In the browser, `search.spec.ts` finds by words and a label, sorts the grid by title, filters by priority, edits a priority in place, saves and opens a shared view, and completes and refuses a query. `grid.test.tsx`, `search.test.tsx` and `query.test.tsx` cover the sort heading, the suspect chip, one attribute condition, a cell edit, saving a view, the search's paging and the query help.

What is missing is paging and the second person. No integration test turns a page of the grid or the search. No test sends `owner` or `updatedAfter` to `/search`. A token limited to one project never searches. Neither MCP tool of the area is ever called. Views are refused only when created: nobody tries to share a view by changing it, to delete somebody else's view, or to change a shared view after losing the right to edit. In the browser nobody edits a title or an attribute in the grid, nobody uses any grid filter but priority, and no second person ever sees a shared view. "Save changes to this view" and "Delete this view" are never clicked. On the search screen nobody uses the owner, date or order filters, "Clear filters", or the result pages.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these writes were never answered 403: `DELETE /views/{viewID}`; these were never answered 422: `DELETE /views/{viewID}`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #380: DELETE takes no input, so a malformed id stays 400 `bad_request` as on every path; asserted beside the 403 with the rows unchanged)
- [x] Grid paging and reach: `GET /projects/{projectKey}/requirements?limit=2&offset=2` answers the next rows in outline order with `total` unchanged and no row repeated, and the same holds under `sort=title` and under a query's `ORDER BY`. `limit=501` and `offset=-1` are 422 `validation_failed` naming the field. A guest no grant names is 404 `not_found`. Only `limit=0` is tried today (requirements_test.go), and the grid is never read by an outsider.
- [x] Search paging: `GET /search?q=...&limit=2&offset=2` answers a second page with no hit from the first and the same `total`. `terms` is filled on the first page and `[]` when `offset` is above 0, as `handleSearch` says. `limit=101` and `offset=-1` are 422. search_test.go never sends `limit` or `offset`.
- [x] Search filters never tried over the API: `owner=<id>` keeps only that person's requirements, and `updatedAfter=<today>` keeps those changed today. `owner=nope`, `updatedAfter=2026-13-01` and `sort=oldest` are each 422 `validation_failed` with that field in `fields`. Only `TestParseQueryRefusesBadInput` (unit) reads them today.
- [x] Views refused when changed: a viewer's `PATCH /views/{viewID}` with `shared: true` on their own view is 403 `forbidden` and the view stays private (`ErrShareForbidden` is tried only on `POST`). A viewer's `DELETE /views/{viewID}` of a shared view is 403 and the view stays listed. A project administrator's `DELETE` of somebody else's shared view is 204. A `PATCH` renaming to a name the owner already has is 422 on `name`. A name of 101 characters and 31 columns are each 422 on `name` and `columns`. grid_test.go refuses only at create time, and only the owner deletes.
- [x] Views after a right is lost: an editor shares a view and is then made a viewer, or the project is archived. Their `PATCH /views/{viewID}` renaming it, and an administrator's in the archived project, must be refused with a status and code that a sentence explains, and the row must stay unchanged. Taking the share back (`shared: false`) still answers 200. No test covers this today. The service does not check it, and the update reaches `saved_view_changed`'s WITH CHECK. (decided in #380: a lost edit right stays 403 `forbidden`, which the service checks; in an archived project it is now 409 `project_archived`)
- [x] A token limited to project A: `GET /search?q=<word in A and B>` answers only A's hits, its `total` counts only them, and `project=B` gives none. `GET /search/quick` likewise. `GET /projects/B/requirements` and `GET /projects/B/views` are 404. Nothing tests search with a limited token today.
- [x] MCP: `search_requirements` and `list_requirements` through `/api/v1/mcp` answer the hits and rows the HTTP calls answer. `list_requirements` takes `label` and `attr` as arrays and a `query` with `ORDER BY`. A query that cannot run comes back as `isError` with the sentence and the position. No test calls either tool today. (fixed in #380: the refusal now names the character)

Database guards:
- [x] As `exciter_app`, `UPDATE saved_view SET project_id = <another project>` is permission denied (the column grant leaves it out). Only `owner_id` (view_rls_test.go) and `kind` (matrix_views_test.go) are tried today.
- [x] Through SQL, a project administrator's `DELETE FROM saved_view` affects 0 rows for somebody's private view and 1 for a shared one, and the same holds for `UPDATE`. view_rls_test.go deletes only as a viewer and as the owner.
- [x] With `app.token_projects` limited to one project (the `limitTo` helper), `SELECT` on `saved_view` returns only that project's views, and `requirement_search_rows` and `requirement_key_id` reach only its requirements. token_rls_test.go tries only `project` and `requirement`.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] Grid filters: words in "Words" then "Apply" (`apply-words`). Then "Kind" set to sections, "Status", and "Owner" set to "Owned by me". Then a label typed into the label filter, then "Add condition" (`add-condition`) on an attribute, and "Remove condition <text>" (`remove-condition`). After each step the rows and the address change and the count reads right. Only "Priority" and "Clear filters" are used today (search.spec.ts).
- [x] Inline edit: "Title of <key>" (`edit-title`), type a new title and press Enter. The notice says "Saved <key>." and the requirement page shows the new title. Escape leaves the old one. A text or number attribute cell saves on Enter. Change the requirement over the API in between, then edit the cell: an error banner appears and the value is not overwritten. Only the priority select is used today.
- [x] A shared view seen by a second person: alice shares a view. Bob, a viewer, finds it as "<name> (Shared)" under "Views" and gets no "Save changes to this view" or "Delete this view". His "Share with everybody in the project" is disabled with "Only the project's editors share views.". Alice changes the order and clicks "Save changes to this view" (`update-view`), and bob sees the new order on reload. "Delete this view" (`delete-view`) removes it from bob's list. Today alice only saves and opens her own view.
- [x] Search filters and pages: "Owner" set to "You (<name>)", "Changed on or after", "Changed before", and "Order" set to "Latest change first" each narrow or reorder the hits and land in the address. "Clear filters" (`clear-filters`) takes them away and keeps the words. "Search" (`run-search`) runs the box. With 25 hits, "Next" (`next-results`) shows "21 to 25 of 25 results" with `page=2`, "Previous" (`previous-results`) goes back, and the browser's Back returns to page 1. Today only words, a label and the project are used.
- [x] Query help and keys: "What a query can say" (`query-help`) opens the dialog. An example puts its query into the box, and "Run" (`run-query`) narrows the rows. Tab takes the first completion. No scenario opens the help or clicks "Run" today. search.spec.ts only clicks suggestions and presses Enter.

Component (vitest):
- [x] GridPage paging: with `total` 250 it shows "1 to 100 of 250 requirements". "Next" asks for `offset=100` and "Previous" is disabled on the first window. A new filter or order asks for `offset=0` again. No test turns a grid page today.
- [x] TitleCell and ValueCell: Enter saves the trimmed title with `baseRevision`, Escape sends nothing, and an unchanged or blank title sends nothing. A 409 from `PATCH /requirements/{reqKey}` shows its message in the error banner. A row with `can.edit` false, a retired attribute, an attribute the row's type does not show, and a field a status rule closes all show plain text and offer no control. grid.test.tsx changes only a select and the priority.
- [x] GridViews: "Save changes to this view" sends the grid's filter, sort and columns. "Delete this view" sends `DELETE`, says "Deleted the view <name>." and goes back to "All requirements". A 403 from either shows its message. For a project the reader does not edit, the share checkbox is disabled with its hint. Only opening and saving a new view are tested.
- [x] SearchScreen and its route: the owner, both date fields and the order each change the address and the request. "Clear filters" keeps `q` and `sort`. Removing a label chip drops it. Terms show above the hits on page 1 and not on page 2. `validateSearch` drops `page=1`, `page=abc` and `sort=oldest`. search.test.tsx covers only the category, words, Next and a refusal.
- [x] QueryInput keys: ArrowDown opens a closed list, and ArrowDown and ArrowUp wrap around it. Tab takes the active completion, or the first when none is active. Shift+Tab leaves the box. Escape closes the list without leaving the box. Clicking "Run" submits what is typed. query.test.tsx picks rows only by clicking.

Go unit:
- [x] `checkView` in search/views.go: it trims the name and refuses a blank name, 101 characters, 31 columns and a column that is none. A filter's field error is reported under `filter` but a sort's under `sort`. Labels come back normalized. `keepKnown`, `firstWords` and `detailOf` (each slot, a quoted attribute and a function) deserve table tests too. Package search is at 23.6%.
- [x] `orderBy` in search/grid.go with a stub `bind`: a query's `ORDER BY` outranks the column sort, a column sort ends in `NULLS LAST, w.path`, and no sort gives `w.path`. It is a pure function and is only reached through the API today.

- Every search and view operation has an integration test for paging and for a specific 403 or 422 with its code, with the rows unchanged, and is tried with a token limited to one project.

issues.title: Test comments, files, notifications and watching end to end
issues.body:
The happy paths are well covered. `comments_test.go` walks a thread through start, reply, resolve, reopen, edit and moderation, with 403s for a reader and for somebody else's words, and refuses a comment on a requirement in the trash or in an archived project. `attachments_test.go` uploads, lists, downloads in place or not, deletes, copies and purges, with refusals for viewers, strangers, size and emptiness. `watching_test.go` follows a revision, comment, reply, resolution and transition through the worker into the app, Mailpit and a daily digest, and `attachment_rls_test.go`, `TestRawSQLHoldsCommentsToTheirRules` and `TestRawSQLKeepsWatchesAndNotificationsToTheirPeople` try the guards through SQL. `markdown_test.go` and `mcp_review_test.go` cover comments in Markdown and most comment tools. In the browser, `comments.spec.ts` posts, mentions, replies, resolves and deletes, `attachments.spec.ts` attaches, shows, downloads and deletes, and `notifications.spec.ts` watches a requirement and follows a mention from the bell and from a mail. CommentsSection, AttachmentPanel, NotificationBell, NotificationList, NotificationSettings, WatchMenu, ProjectWatchButton and WatchingList all have vitest suites. What is missing is the edges. Nobody edits, reopens or cancels a comment once it is resolved, deleted, trashed or archived. Mentions and the mention picker are never narrowed to who may read. An edit or a reopening never shows that it tells anybody. Watching and notifications are never shown to follow what a person may still view. The hourly digest, a mail switched off on its own and auto watch switched off are never tried. In the browser nobody stops watching, watches a project, opens Who is watching, the Watching page or the Notifications page, or drops a file on the panel. The settings page also offers switches for only nine of the twenty kinds the server sends.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these writes were never answered 403: `PUT /comment-threads/{threadID}/resolution`, `POST /comments/{commentID}/replies`, `PUT /notification-preferences`, `POST /notifications/read`, `DELETE /projects/{projectKey}/watch`, `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/watch`, `DELETE /requirements/{reqKey}/watch`, `PUT /requirements/{reqKey}/watch`; these were never answered 422: `DELETE /attachments/{attachmentID}`, `DELETE /comment-threads/{threadID}/resolution`, `PUT /comment-threads/{threadID}/resolution`, `DELETE /comments/{commentID}`, `PATCH /comments/{commentID}`, `POST /comments/{commentID}/replies`, `DELETE /projects/{projectKey}/watch`, `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/watch`, `DELETE /requirements/{reqKey}/watch`, `PUT /requirements/{reqKey}/watch`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #381: watches, preferences and notifications are a person's own, so their 403 is a read-only token's `read_only_token`; the routes without a body have no field for a 422, and a malformed id is asserted at 400 `bad_request`)
- [x] Comments refused past what is tried: `PATCH /comments/{commentID}` on a deleted comment is 404 `not_found`. `PUT /comment-threads/{threadID}/resolution` with a reply's id is 404. The same PUT by carol, who may only read, is 403 `forbidden` (only her reopening is tried). `DELETE /comments/{commentID}` in an archived project is 409 `project_archived`. `PATCH /comments/{commentID}` and `PUT .../resolution` on a requirement in the trash are 409 `requirement_trashed`. In each case the comment's body, `edited_at` and the thread's `resolved_at` are unchanged. Today trash and archive are tried for `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/comments` alone.
- [x] Mentions narrowed to who may read: a comment that mentions a member with no grant on the project and a deactivated member leaves both out of the `comment.created` event's `mentioned`, and after `drained` neither has a notification. `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/mentionable?q=car` returns carol alone. A `q` of `%` or `_` matches literally. A member without a grant comes back with `canView` false. Carol, who may only read, is 403. Today every mentioned person may read R1, and only `limit=50` and `limit=0` are sent. (decided in #381: `q=car` is asserted to offer carol alone among the test's people, since the shared installation may hold other members who match)
- [x] An edit and a reopening tell people: a `PATCH /comments/{commentID}` that adds a mention of the owner gives the owner a `mentioned` notification carrying the edited excerpt. Carol, already told of the comment as a watcher, gets no second row. `DELETE /comment-threads/{threadID}/resolution` gives the thread's writers a `resolved` row. A second PUT on a resolved thread writes no event and no row. Today `comments_test.go` checks only the edit's outbox event, and `watching_test.go` only resolves.
- [x] MCP `list_comments` through `/api/v1/mcp` returns the threads `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/comments` returns, with `bodyMarkdown` on each comment. A token whose person may not view the requirement gets `isError`. No test calls the tool today.
- [x] Watching follows visibility and pages: `PUT /requirements/{reqKey}/watch` and `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/watchers` on a requirement in a project the caller has no grant on, and `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/watch` on that project, are 404 `not_found` and write no `watch` row. Today only keys that do not exist are tried. After carol's grant is taken away, or R1 goes to the trash, `GET /watches`, `GET /notifications` and `GET /notifications/unread-count` leave R1 out, and `/watchers` leaves carol out. Restoring the grant or R1 brings them back. `GET /notifications?limit=2&offset=2`, `?unread=true` and `GET /watches?limit=1&offset=1` return the next window and a `total` that counts only what is listed. Today only a `limit` over the maximum is sent.
- [x] Preferences each have their effect: with `autoWatch` false, revising R1 and being made its owner write no `watch` row (only the default is tried). With `email.revised` false and `inApp.revised` true, a revision writes the row in the app and Mailpit receives no mail for it. Today only a kind switched off in the app is tried.
- [x] The worker's mail: with `digest` set to `hourly`, `notify.NewDigester(...).Once` with a clock before the next full hour sends nothing, and after it sends one bundle. A notification read before the hour is left out of the bundle. A queue whose rows are all read is emptied and sends nothing. Running `notify.NewFanOut(...).Handle` twice with the same event writes one row per person and one mail. Only the daily digest is tried today.
- [x] Files refused: `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/attachments` and `DELETE /attachments/{attachmentID}` in an archived project are 409 `project_archived`. `DELETE` on a file of a requirement in the trash is 409 `requirement_trashed` and the row and its bytes stay. Decide whether a locked requirement takes a new file, and test that answer. `control_test.go` checks only that a locked requirement still takes comments. Today only an upload to the trash is tried. (decided in #381: a locked requirement takes a new file, since a file becomes part of its words only through a revision, which the lock refuses)

Database guards:
- [x] Through SQL as `exciter_app`, an editor's `INSERT INTO comment_thread` and `INSERT INTO comment` on a requirement in the trash, and in an archived project, are refused by `perm_requirement_commentable`. An `UPDATE comment SET body` by its author after the project is archived is refused, and so is an `UPDATE comment_thread SET resolved_at`. Today only a reader and wrong names are tried.
- [x] The `notification_about_live_comment` trigger: a notification row naming a comment that is already deleted, inserted as the worker, is silently not written. A row naming a live comment is written. Nothing tries the trigger today. Only `comment_deleted_forget` is reached, through the API.
- [x] Through SQL as carol, a `watch` of kind `project` on a project she may not view is refused, and so is an `attachment` insert by an editor on a requirement in the trash or in an archived project. `SELECT * FROM requirement_watchers($1)` on a requirement she may not view returns no rows. As a viewer, it leaves out a watcher who lost their grant. Today only `requirement_watch_coverage` and requirement watches are tried.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] Discussion: alice clicks "Edit" (`edit-comment`) on her comment, changes it and saves. The comment shows "edited" and bob's bell gains the mention the edit added. After bob resolves, "Reopen" (`reopen-thread`) shows the thread open again. "Comment" then "Cancel" (`cancel-comment`) leaves no thread. Today only post, reply, resolve and delete are clicked.
- [x] Moderation and readers: alice, the project's administrator, deletes bob's comment after the confirm that names him, and bob sees "This comment was deleted.". A viewer sees "You may read this discussion but not take part" and no "Comment" or "Reply". Typing `@` and the name of a member who has no grant on the project offers no option for them.
- [x] Watch menu: "Stop watching this requirement" (`unwatch-requirement`) turns the button back to "Watch". "Watch the whole project" (`watch-project`) shows "Covered by your watch on the whole project". "Who is watching" (`show-watchers`) opens a dialog that lists alice under "Watches this requirement" and bob under "Watches the whole project". Today only "Watch this requirement" is clicked.
- [x] Project watch: on `/p/$projectKey`, bob presses "Watch project" (`watch-project`, `aria-pressed`) and it reads "Watching project". Alice revises a requirement bob never opened, and bob's bell says so. "Watching project" again stops it. No scenario presses the button today.
- [x] Watching page: `/settings/watching` lists bob's requirement and project watches with what each covers. "Stop watching <name>" (`stop-watching`) removes the row and says "You no longer watch ...". The requirement then shows "Watch". No scenario opens the page today.
- [x] Notifications page: "See all notifications" (`all-notifications`) in the bell opens `/notifications`. "Unread only" narrows the list. "Mark all as read" (`mark-all-read`) turns the bell's name back to "Notifications". With more than 50 rows, "Next" and "Previous" walk the pages. No scenario opens `/notifications` today.
- [x] Notification settings have an effect: bob unticks "By email: Somebody mentions you in a comment" and saves. Alice mentions him, the bell lists it and Mailpit holds no mail for it. Then bob chooses a daily digest under "When emails go out", and after a reload the choice is still there. Today a box is unticked and saved, and nothing checks what it changed.
- [x] Files: a file dropped on the panel (a `drop` event with a `DataTransfer`) is attached, and the panel reads "Drop the files to attach them." while dragging. "Attach files" (`attach-files`) opens the chooser (`filechooser` event). An oversized file shows its refusal line. A viewer sees no "Attach files" and no "Delete". Today the hidden input is filled directly.

Component (vitest):
- [x] CommentsSection: "Cancel" closes the box without a request. A failed post keeps the words and shows the error. Deleting somebody else's comment asks with `confirmDeleteOthers(author)`. "Reopen" sends `DELETE /comment-threads/{id}/resolution`. A requirement in the trash or an archived project shows `t.comments.closed` and no "Comment". `useMentionSource` drops a person whose `canView` is false. Today only posting, replying, resolving, editing and deleting one's own are tried.
- [x] NotificationRow and NotificationList: a session's, an execution's and a code scan's row lead to `/p/$projectKey/sessions/$sessionId`, `/p/$projectKey/tests/executions/$executionId` and `/p/$projectKey/code-tags`. A row with no requirement renders as text. Following a row already read sends no `POST /notifications/read`. On the page, "Next" and "Previous" move the offset when `total` exceeds the page size, the range reads "51 to 100 of 120", and "Unread only" goes back to the first page. Today only requirement rows and the unread filter are tried.
- [x] NotificationSettings offers a switch in the app and by email for every kind in the API's `Notification.kind` enum, and one switched off is saved as false. Today the fixture lists nine kinds, the same nine `NOTIFICATION_KINDS` holds, so the missing eleven go unnoticed.
- [x] WatchingList and ProjectWatchButton: "Next" and "Previous" page the list when `total` exceeds 20. Stopping the last row of a later page still offers the earlier rows. A failed stop shows `t.watch.failed`, and so does a failed project watch. Today only one page, the stop and the empty state are tried.

Go unit:
- [x] `attachment.(*Service).reapBatchWith` with fake read and write functions: a store that fails keeps the tombstone for the next run, and one that succeeds removes it. `comment.cleanBody`: a nil body, text that is only spaces, a lone mention and a node outside the comment subset each come back as a `FieldError` on `body` with its sentence. The comment package has no unit tests today, and the reaper is reached by a single integration call. (decided in #381: a lone mention is a comment, as in Stator, so `cleanBody` keeps it)

## Done when
- Every control in CommentsSection, AttachmentPanel, NotificationBell, NotificationList, NotificationSettings, WatchMenu, WatchersDialog, ProjectWatchButton and WatchingList is reached by a browser scenario that checks its effect on another person or on the mail sent.
- Every comments, attachments, watching and notifications operation has an integration test for its specific refusals (403, 404, 409 or 422 with the code), and the test checks that the rows are unchanged.
- Visibility, archive and trash hold for comments, files, watches and notifications both through the service and straight through SQL.

issues.title: Test trace links, link types and suspect links to the last control
issues.body:
Trace links are among the best tested parts of Exciter. `TestLinkTypesOverTheAPI` and `TestTraceLinksOverTheAPI` in trace_test.go walk making, renaming, retiring, limiting and deleting link types and every refusal of a link (self link, section, repeat, circle, viewer). suspect_test.go follows a link turning suspect, its notifications, the grid, specification and project list, clearing with every refusal, both ends and the trash; `TestRawSQLKeepsSuspectLinksHonest`, `TestRawSQLGuardsTraceLinks` and `TestRawSQLKeepsLinkTypesToTheirAdministrators` try the guards as exciter_app. In the browser trace-links.spec.ts links, removes, is refused a circle, makes a type for all projects and turns it off in a project, and suspect.spec.ts confirms a link from the project's suspects page; links.test.tsx and suspect.test.tsx cover the panel, the pairs dialog and the check dialog. What is missing: a project administrator is never refused a type for all projects, a type is never brought back from retirement, a link type's name is never refused as taken, the link cap and archived projects are never tried, the suspects list is never paged and never read across projects, and `list_links` is never called. In the browser nobody checks a suspect link from the requirement page, edits, retires, restores or deletes a link type, sets pairs, makes a project's own type, picks another requirement in the form or pages the suspects list.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these were never answered 422: `DELETE /link-types/{linkTypeID}`, `DELETE /links/{linkID}`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #382: neither takes input but its id, so neither answers 422; a malformed id is 400 `bad_request`, and their 403, 404 and 409 are tested)
- [x] `PATCH /link-types/{linkTypeID}` and `DELETE /link-types/{linkTypeID}` on a type for all projects by a project administrator (not an installation administrator) answer 403 `forbidden`, and the type is unchanged. Today only a plain member is refused, in trace_test.go.
- [x] `PATCH /link-types/{linkTypeID}` on project A's own type by the administrator of project B, and `PUT /projects/{B}/link-types/{A's type}`, answer 403 or 404 and A's type is unchanged. (decided in #382: 403 to change or delete it, 404 to set it in B)
- [x] `PATCH /link-types/{linkTypeID}` with `retired: false` brings a retired type back: `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/links` with it succeeds again, and its old links were listed all along by `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/links`. Today only retiring is tried.
- [x] `POST /link-types` and `POST /projects/{projectKey}/link-types` with a `name` another type already has answer 422 on `name` (the `link_type_name_taken` guard). Today only a taken key is tried.
- [x] `PATCH /link-types/{linkTypeID}` with `acyclic: true` on a type whose links already go round a circle: decide and assert the answer (refused, or the circle kept and the next one refused). Today only turning acyclic off with a formula is tried, in computed_test.go. (decided in #382: allowed, the circle kept and the next one refused)
- [x] `PATCH /link-types/{linkTypeID}` with `acyclic: false` by a plain member answers 403 before anything else. Today it answers 409 `type_in_formula` naming the formula of a project the member may not see (see the separate report).
- [x] `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/links` past `trace.MaxLinksPerRequirement` answers 422 on `otherKey` naming both keys and the limit (`trace_link_limit`), and no link is written.
- [x] Archived project: `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/links`, `DELETE /links/{linkID}` and `POST /links/{linkID}/clear` on links whose ends are all in archived projects are refused with a specific code (`POST /links/{linkID}/clear` returns `project.ErrArchived`, so 409 `project_archived`), and the links and their confirmed revisions are unchanged. (decided in #382: all three answer 409 `project_archived`; linking and removing answered 403 and are fixed there)
- [x] `GET /projects/{projectKey}/suspects?limit=1&offset=1` returns the second waiting link and `total` stays 2. A suspect link whose other end lies in a project the reader cannot see is not listed and not counted. Today only `limit=101` is refused.
- [x] A link turns suspect on every revision of its watched end, not only a title change: a `PATCH` of the description and of an attribute value each turn it, and a change of owner or priority, which makes no new revision, leaves it as it was. Today every scene in suspect_test.go revises the title only.
- [x] MCP: `list_links` through `/api/v1/mcp` answers the same links, phrases and other ends as `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/links`, and for a requirement the token may not see answers `isError`. No test calls it today. In mcp_review_test.go, the check after `clear_suspect_link` compares `suspect` to `true`, but `suspect` is a list, so it can never fail: assert that the list is empty. (the check already asserted an empty list since 5d6a9ce)

Database guards:
- [x] As exciter_app, an editor's `UPDATE link_type SET name = ...` on a type for all projects and on the project's own type affects no row, and a project administrator's `UPDATE link_type SET project_id = <other project>` is refused. Today only INSERT, DELETE and a key change are tried.
- [x] As exciter_app, a link of a type the source's project turned off (`link_type_project.enabled = false`) and a link between requirement types no `link_type_rule` allows. Decide whether `trace_link_type` should refuse them, as it refuses a retired type, and try it either way. Today only the service refuses them. (decided in #382: the database does not refuse them, the service does)
- [x] As the superuser, `UPDATE trace_link SET type_id = ...` is refused by `trace_link_fixed`, and `trace_link_clear` on a link whose end is in the trash is refused by `trace_link_clear_trashed`. Neither constraint is named in any test today. (decided in #382: `trace_link_clear` acts for an actor, so the superuser calls it acting for the editor in a rolled-back transaction, and as `exciter_app` too)

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] On the requirement page, after the other end changes, "Check the link to <key>" (`data-action="check-link"` in LinksPanel) opens the dialog, "Confirm link" clears it, the badge goes, and the suspects page says "No link waits to be checked." Today a link is only checked from the suspects page.
- [x] `/settings/link-types`: "Edit" (`edit-link-type`) renames a type and the requirement page's "Link type" options read the new phrase; "Cancel" (`cancel-link-type`) leaves it. "Retire" (`retire-link-type`) takes it out of the options but keeps its links shown, and "Use again" (`restore-link-type`) brings it back. "Delete" (`delete-link-type`) on a type with no link removes the row, and is not offered on a type with links.
- [x] Project settings, Links tab: "New link type" makes a project's own type, which shows "This project" and is offered on that project's requirements only. "Pairs" (`edit-pairs`), "Add a pair" (`add-pair`) and "Save pairs" (`save-pairs`) limit a type to two requirement types, after which linking two requirements of the default type shows the refusal beside the form.
- [x] Add a link form: after picking a requirement, "Pick another" (`pick-another`) clears it, and a requirement of another project the person can see is found and linked; the link reads from both ends.
- [x] Suspects page with more than 20 links: "Next" and "Previous" walk the pages and "21 to 25 of 25" is shown. A reader of the project sees the list without "Check".

## Done when
- Every control of LinksPanel, LinkTypeList, LinkTypeForm, PairsDialog, Suspect and SuspectList is reached by a browser scenario that checks its effect on the requirement page.
- Every link and link type operation has an integration test for its 403 by somebody one step short of the right role, and for each guard's specific code.
- The database refuses, or is decided not to refuse, links that a project turned off or a pair rule forbids, and a test proves it through SQL.

issues.title: Test coverage and the trace graph against every way they are narrowed
issues.body:
Coverage and the trace graph are well covered on the server. `TestCoverageFollowsTheRulesAndTheLinks` in coverage_test.go sets and removes rules, reads levels and totals, narrows, pages and keeps rows at a level and sees a revision turn links partial once the worker cleared the cache; code_tags_test.go, test_results_test.go and test_traceability_test.go count code, test results and executions; `TestRawSQLKeepsCoverageRulesToAdministrators` tries the guards as exciter_app. trace_graph_test.go walks the graph up and down, to a depth, through types and relations, counts what the reader may not see without naming it, and marks suspect and broken links, gaps, tests and code; query_trace_test.go keeps link, coverage and approval fields in step with the report. In the browser coverage.spec.ts ticks one box of the rule for every type and narrows by a level, trace-graph.spec.ts opens a graph, centres it, lists it and downloads it, and coverage.test.tsx and graph.test.tsx cover rule editing, sources and the graph's controls. What is missing: a change to a link type never shows in coverage (and today it does not, see the separate report), the cache is never shown to be per reader, archived projects are never tried, Stator pages are never nodes in a tested graph, `get_trace_graph` is never called and `get_coverage` is called without a single assertion, and the query language is never asked about links whose far end the reader cannot see. In the browser nobody adds or removes a rule for a type, picks what verifies, pages the coverage list, or changes the graph's direction, depth, link types or relations, opens a node, uses the keyboard on the canvas or goes back to the requirement.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these were never answered 422: `DELETE /coverage-rules/{ruleID}`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #384: the removal takes no body, so there is no 422; a malformed id is 400 `bad_request`, one nobody has 404, a reader 403, and the rules stay as they were)
- [x] Coverage follows link types: `PATCH /link-types/{linkTypeID}` with `counts` from `nothing` to `verification`, then `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/link-types/{linkTypeID}` with `enabled: false`, each change the levels of `GET /projects/{projectKey}/coverage` once the worker drained. Today neither clears the coverage cache (see the separate report), so this test fails until it does. (decided in #384: a type turned off for the project or retired keeps its links, which still count, as the matrix shows them; only `counts` changes the levels)
- [x] The coverage cache is per reader: the owner and carol, who cannot see a requirement in another project that verifies R1, read R1 as `full` and `none` one after the other, within `trace.CoverageCacheTTL`, each in both orders. No test reads coverage as two people in a row today.
- [x] Archived project: `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/coverage-rules` and `DELETE /coverage-rules/{ruleID}` answer 409 `project_archived` and the rules are unchanged. Only the SQL delete is tried today, in coverage_test.go.
- [x] `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/coverage-rules` by a project's reader answers 403 `forbidden` (only an editor is tried), and with `typeId` of a retired requirement type answers 422 on `typeId` or is decided to be allowed. (decided in #384: allowed, since a retired type's requirements are still counted)
- [x] `GET /projects/{projectKey}/coverage?limit=0`, `?limit=` past the maximum and `?offset=-1` answer 422 naming the field; `?offset=` past the end answers no rows and the right `total`.
- [x] `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/graph` with Stator pages traced: a page is a node of kind `page` below its requirement for `relation=specifies`, missing for `relation=implements`, and marked broken when the page was deleted. No graph test has a Stator page today.
- [x] `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/graph?type=<a project's own type key>` follows that type, and `?type=` naming another project's own type answers 400 `bad_request` on `type`. Today only the seeded keys and `blocks` are tried.
- [x] `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/graph` of a section answers what the page expects (refused, or a graph of its children), and of a requirement in the trash answers 404. (decided in #384: a section's graph is the section alone; the trash answers 404 to a reader who may not open it, and to its editors the centre alone, marked broken)
- [x] Query language over hidden ends: as carol, `verifiedBy IS NOT EMPTY` and `verifiedBy = <key of a requirement she cannot see>` neither keep R1 for a link from a project she cannot read nor say the key exists. Today every query in query_trace_test.go runs over one project the reader sees whole.

issues.title: Test baselines, their comparisons and their signatures to every refusal
issues.body:
Baselines are tested thoroughly where they are frozen. `TestABaselineIsTakenReadAndCompared` in baselines_test.go takes, reads, compares, locks, deletes and names a purged requirement; `TestATakenBaselineIsOneSnapshot` proves a baseline is one snapshot while links and revisions change under it; baseline_matrix_test.go keeps the matrix with its suspect state and compares it with now; `TestABaselineIsSignedAndKeptForGood` and `TestRawSQLGuardsBaselineSignatures` in control_test.go cover the signing rule, the meaning, the password, tokens, the frozen signers, the hash and every signature guard; `TestRawSQLKeepsBaselinesFrozen` tries the items and the lock through SQL; xlsx_test.go and documents_test.go read the workbook and the printed baseline. In the browser baselines.spec.ts takes, compares with now, opens a change and locks, and reads the recorded matrix compared with now; control.spec.ts names a signer and signs with the password; baselines.test.tsx covers the list, the page, comparisons, signing and the rule. What is missing: an archived project is never tried, a section of another project or in the trash is never refused as the scope, a comparison with another project's baseline is never refused, signing a baseline with a sign-in at the provider and the run of wrong passwords are only tried for reviews, the signing rule's signer refusals are mostly untried, and the `baseline_fixed` and `baseline_signature_no_rule` guards are never named. In the browser nobody renames or deletes a baseline, takes one of a section, compares two baselines, downloads a baseline's matrix as Excel, changes or stops the signing rule, or signs a baseline as the second of two signers.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these were never answered 422: `DELETE /baselines/{baselineID}`, `PATCH /baselines/{baselineID}`, `DELETE /projects/{projectKey}/baseline-signing`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #387: the two deletes take no input, so an id that is none answers 400 and an unknown one 404; `PATCH` answers 422 on name and description)
- [x] Archived project: `POST /projects/{projectKey}/baselines`, `PATCH /baselines/{baselineID}`, `DELETE /baselines/{baselineID}` and `POST /baselines/{baselineID}/signatures` each answer 409 `project_archived` (`keeping` and `Sign` return `project.ErrArchived`), and nothing is written. No baseline test archives its project today.
- [x] `POST /projects/{projectKey}/baselines` with `rootKey` of a section in another project, of a section in the trash, and of a section that does not exist each answer 422 on `rootKey`. Today only a requirement that is no section is tried.
- [x] `GET /baselines/{baselineID}/compare?with=<id of a baseline of another project the reader can see>` and `GET /baselines/{baselineID}/matrix?with=<the same>` answer 422 on `with`. Today only an unknown id is tried, which takes the same branch only partly.
- [x] A baseline being signed: after one of two signatures, `PATCH /baselines/{baselineID}` with a new name and `DELETE /baselines/{baselineID}` answer 409 `baseline_signed`, and `PATCH` with `locked: false` answers 409. Today these are tried only once both have signed.
- [x] `POST /baselines/{baselineID}/signatures` with `reauthentication` from a fresh sign-in at the provider signs with that method; one from another session, one already spent and one too old answer their refusals and write no signature. Today the provider path is tried only for review decisions, in signatures_test.go.
- [x] `POST /baselines/{baselineID}/signatures` with a run of wrong passwords answers 429 `too_many_attempts`, then refuses the right password for a while, and the counter is the same one review decisions use (or a separate one, as decided). Today only review decisions run into it. (decided in #387: one counter per person, shared with reviews)
- [x] `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/baseline-signing` refusals on `signers`: a signer of subject type `everyone`, the same person twice, an id that is no person or group, and more than `baseline.MaxSigners` each answer 422 on `signers`. A reader of the project answers 403 (only an editor is tried).

issues.title: Test reviews, signed approvals and review sessions through every role and scope
issues.body:
Reviews and signatures have deep integration tests. `TestARevisionIsReviewedAndApproved` in reviews_test.go walks rules, requests, the inbox, decisions, transitions asking for approval, superseding, withdrawing and the refusals, and `TestRawSQLHoldsReviewsToTheirRules` tries each guard as exciter_app; signatures_test.go signs with the password, runs into the wrong password limit, signs after a sign-in at the provider and tries the signature guards through SQL; review_sessions_test.go opens a session over a section, decides, starts a second round, closes it with a baseline, reads the report as JSON, Word and PDF, tries the session guards through SQL and works out the quorum over a baseline scope; mcp_review_test.go asks for reviews through the assistant. In the browser approval.spec.ts sets a rule, asks, approves from the inbox and signs with the password, and sessions.spec.ts opens a session from the document, decides in two rounds and closes it with a baseline; reviews.test.tsx and sessions.test.tsx cover the panel, the rules, the signature dialog and the session page. What is missing: a rule for one requirement type and `authorMayApprove: true` are never used, another editor is never refused a session that is not theirs, sessions over a query and with `since` are never opened, the round limit, an empty scope and a bad quorum are never refused, the deadline reminder job is never run, `list_review_sessions` and `get_review_session` are never called, and the `review_session_fixed` and `review_session_round` guards are never named. In the browser nobody rejects or withdraws a review, changes or removes an approval rule, signs at the provider or cancels a signature, opens the project's sessions page, opens a session over a baseline or a query, or downloads a session's report.
