issues.title: Test stopping, discarding and refusing imports, and the archive limits
issues.body:
The round trips are well covered: `TestExportThenImportMakesTheSameProject` (imports_test.go), `TestReqIFExportThenImportMakesTheSameProject`, `TestReqIFReimportUpdatesByIdentifier` and `TestReqIFImportAsksBeforeItWrites` (reqif_test.go), the Word tests in word_import_test.go and the template tests in export_templates_test.go each go out and back and try a member, a bad file, a file too large and a start with problems. `import_rls_test.go`, `reqif_rls_test.go` and `TestRawSQLGuardsWordImports` try the import guards through SQL. In the browser, import.spec.ts, reqif.spec.ts, word-import.spec.ts and export-templates.spec.ts each walk the happy path once, and ImportPanel, ReqIFPanel, WordImportPanel and TemplateSettings have vitest suites. What is missing is everything after the happy path: nobody stops an import that runs, so the `cancelled` state is never reached; `DELETE` is only tried on an import that waits for its mapping. Nobody but the maker and a plain member touches an import, so the rule that only the maker maps and starts it (`ErrForbidden`) is never tried. Only the Word upload is refused in an archived project. `ziplimit`, which keeps a small `.reqifz` or `.docx` from unpacking into more than the server allows, has no test at all. In the browser nobody answers a problem, discards, stops or imports another file, and nobody deletes or shares a template.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these writes were never answered 403: `DELETE /imports/{importID}`, `PUT /imports/{importID}/mapping`, `POST /imports/{importID}/start`, `DELETE /reqif-imports/{importID}`, `PUT /reqif-imports/{importID}/choices`, `POST /reqif-imports/{importID}/start`; these were never answered 422: `DELETE /imports/{importID}`, `PUT /imports/{importID}/mapping`, `POST /imports/{importID}/start`, `DELETE /reqif-imports/{importID}`, `POST /reqif-imports/{importID}/start`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #390: `DELETE` has no 403 or 422, since everybody who sees an import may stop it and it takes no input; a mapping that names what the file or project lacks is a problem in the preview and the start then 409 `import_problems`, not 422)
- [x] Stop a CSV import that runs: upload a file of a few hundred rows, `POST /imports/{importID}/start`, then `DELETE /imports/{importID}` while it is `queued` or `running`. Assert `state` becomes `cancelled`, `imported` holds fewer rows than `total`, the requirements already made stay, and a second `DELETE` then removes the job (404 after it). Today `DELETE` is only tried on an `uploaded` import in imports_test.go, and `cancelled` appears only as a state the poll stops at.
- [x] The same for ReqIF: `DELETE /reqif-imports/{importID}` while it runs ends `cancelled` and keeps what it made. Only an uploaded ReqIF import is discarded today in reqif_test.go.
- [x] Another administrator of the project: they `GET /imports/{importID}` (200, `Service.Get` says they may), but `PUT /imports/{importID}/mapping` and `POST /imports/{importID}/start` are 403 `forbidden` and the job's mapping and state are unchanged. The same for `PUT /reqif-imports/{importID}/choices` and `POST /reqif-imports/{importID}/start`. Decide and assert whether they may `DELETE` it (`csvio.Service.Cancel` checks no maker today). Only a plain member, who gets 404, is tried. (decided in #390: they may `DELETE` it, as the policies have always let administrators stop an import; the database now refuses them mapping and starting through SQL too)
- [x] Archived project: `POST /projects/{projectKey}/import`, `POST /projects/{projectKey}/reqif-imports` and `POST /projects/{projectKey}/export-templates` are 409 `project_archived`, and `PATCH` or `DELETE /export-templates/{templateID}` of a template kept there too. Only `POST /projects/{projectKey}/word-imports` is tried, in word_import_test.go.
- [x] Start reads the project again: upload a CSV mapped to type `Feature`, then delete that type (or the mapped attribute), then `POST /imports/{importID}/start`. Assert 409 `import_problems`, that `GET /imports/{importID}` now lists the new problem, and that no requirement was written.
- [x] `GET /projects/{projectKey}/export.csv` by somebody who does not view the project is 404 `not_found` (tried for `export.reqif` only), and `column=<attribute id>` carries the attribute under its name and an import maps it back to the same attribute.
- [x] A zip bomb: a `.reqifz` whose one entry unpacks past `reqifio.MaxUnpackedBytes`, and a `.docx` for `POST /projects/{projectKey}/word-imports` and `POST /projects/{projectKey}/export-templates` whose parts together unpack past `docx.MaxUnpackedBytes`, are each refused with 413 `too_large` or 422 naming the file, and nothing is stored. Only the upload size is tried today. (decided in #390: one `.reqifz` entry trips `MaxDocumentBytes` before the total, so that is what the test sends; it answered 500 and is now 422 on `file`; Word imports are 422 on `file`, templates 413 `too_large`)
- [x] Export templates refused to the reader of a shared template: somebody outside the project who reads a shared template still gets 403 on `PATCH /export-templates/{templateID}` (only `DELETE` is tried), and `fields` with the same field twice or more than `MaxFields` is 422 naming `fields`.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] CSV import with problems: upload a file with a type nobody has and an owner nobody is. The problems card lists both and "Start the import" (`start-import`) is disabled. Answer "What Feature means here" with a type and "Who nobody@exciter.test is" with "Nobody"; the card then says "Nothing keeps the import from starting." and the import ends done. import.spec.ts only imports an export that maps itself. (fixed in #390: Nobody could not be picked in a browser while it was already shown; the list now reads "Pick who it is" until answered)
- [x] CSV "Discard" (`discard-import`) returns to the upload form and the job is gone from the API. "Stop" (`stop-import`) on a long file shows the cancelled state, and "Import another file" (`import-another`) brings back the upload form. None of the three is clicked today.
- [x] ReqIF: "Discard" (`discard-reqif`), "Stop" (`stop-reqif`) and "Import another file" (`reqif-another`) do the same on the ReqIF tab. reqif.spec.ts only starts an import that has no problems.
- [x] ReqIF: an attribute that does not fit the project's (the vitest case of Weight) is left out in the schema card in the browser, and the import then ends done without it. "Download .reqif" (`export-reqif`) downloads a file that a second project imports.
- [x] Word: "Discard" (`discard-word`) leaves the upload form and makes nothing; a changed heading pattern in the choices step changes the preview tree before the start. word-import.spec.ts only starts with the default choices.
- [x] Export templates: "Offer it to every project" on a template makes it selectable in another project's export dialog, and "Delete" (`delete-template`) then "Delete" in the confirm (`confirm-delete-template`) removes the card and the template from the export dialog. Only upload, add field and save are clicked today.

Component (vitest):
- [x] ImportPanel and ReqIFPanel: "Upload" is disabled for a file over `IMPORT_MAX_BYTES`; "Stop" shows while the state is queued or running and "Import another file" once it has ended; a failed cancel shows its error banner. import.test.tsx and reqif.test.tsx only walk the happy path and the non-administrator. (fixed in #390: a failed stop showed no banner)

Go unit:
- [x] `ziplimit.Open`, `CommonFolder` and `Bundle.ReadFile` (0% today): an entry that claims a small size but unpacks past its limit gives `TooLargeError`; several entries together past the total give `TooLargeError` with `Whole`; `../` and duplicate names are left out; one common folder is stripped and two folders are not. (decided in #390: an entry claiming a smaller size than it unpacks into is refused as damaged, `ReadError` wrapping `zip.ErrFormat`, since Go's zip reader stops at the claim; `TooLargeError` is asserted for an entry past its limit)
- [x] `exporttemplate.checkFields`: an unknown field, an attribute field without an attribute, the same field twice and more than `MaxFields` each give a `FieldError` on `fields`; a non attribute field drops its attribute name.

## Done when
- Every import state, including `cancelled` and `failed`, is reached by an integration test, and every refusal of the import services is asserted with its status and code.
- The archive limits are proved by a test with a file that is small to upload and large to unpack.
- Every control of the CSV, ReqIF, Word and template panels is clicked by a browser scenario that checks what it did.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XsypREK6CTfvi1885SVu2k

issues.title: Test sharing, limits and printing of dashboards, and computed attributes in the browser
issues.body:
The service side is in good shape: dashboards_test.go walks a private dashboard, sharing, the home dashboard, every widget kind, views, ordering and the PDF as the reader, and `TestRawSQLKeepsDashboardsToTheirOwnersAndReaders` tries the dashboard policies through SQL. computed_test.go covers values from fields, sums over children, links, recompute progress, the query language, baselines, the formula check, cycles and the guards (`TestRawSQLKeepsComputedValuesToTheWorker`). The `formula` package has 85% unit coverage. In the browser, dashboards.spec.ts builds a dashboard from a template, adds a widget, moves it and follows a bar to the grid, and computed.spec.ts defines one roll-up and watches it change; dashboard.test.tsx and computed.test.tsx cover the client. What is missing: nobody in the browser shares, unshares, renames or deletes a dashboard, copies its link, downloads its PDF, changes or removes a widget, or sets the home dashboard, and no second person ever opens a shared one. `/p/$projectKey/dashboards/$dashboardId` is never opened directly and `/print/dashboards/$dashboardId` never at all. The dashboard and widget limits (`too_many_dashboards`, `too_many_widgets`) are never reached, the widget policies are not tried through SQL beyond an insert, and the MCP tools `list_dashboards` and `get_dashboard_widget` are never called. A computed attribute is never refused or recomputed in the browser, and the pure helpers of the `attribute` package that drive the worker have no unit tests.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these writes were never answered 403: `PUT /dashboards/{dashboardID}/order`, `POST /dashboards/{dashboardID}/widgets`, `POST /projects/{projectKey}/widget-preview`; these were never answered 422: `DELETE /dashboards/{dashboardID}`, `PATCH /dashboards/{dashboardID}`, `DELETE /widgets/{widgetID}`, `PATCH /widgets/{widgetID}`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #394: the widget preview is a read, so whoever may not read the project gets 404, never 403; the two deletes take no input and answer 404 for what is not there, never 422)
- [x] Limits: the 51st `POST /projects/{projectKey}/dashboards` by one person is 409 `too_many_dashboards` (`MaxDashboards` is 50, shared ones count) and the 31st `POST /dashboards/{dashboardID}/widgets` is 409 `too_many_widgets`. Assert the count is unchanged. Neither code appears in any test today.
- [x] Widget config refused with the field named: `config.groupBy` of `colour`, `config.shape` of `pie`, `config.rows` of 0 and 51, `config.days` of 731, `config.series` of `deleted`, `config.source` with both a query and a view, `width` of 4 on `PATCH /widgets/{widgetID}`, and `config.attributeId` of a rich text attribute or another project's. Only `kind` and a private view are tried in dashboards_test.go. (decided in #394: `config.rows` and `config.days` of 0 mean left out and take the defaults 10 and 90; the rich text and other project's attribute were not refused and are fixed there)
- [x] Losing the project: once bob is removed from the project, `GET /dashboards/{dashboardID}` of his own dashboard and `GET /widgets/{widgetID}/data` are 404, and `PATCH /dashboards/{dashboardID}` is 404, not a write. A project administrator changing the widgets of bob's shared dashboard succeeds, and of his private one is 404.
- [x] `PATCH /dashboards/{dashboardID}` renaming to the name of another of the owner's dashboards is 422 on `name`, and unsharing the home dashboard clears `settings.homeDashboardId` (tried for an unshared dashboard set as home, line 97, and through the home page, but not that the setting is gone after an unshare by a non administrator owner).
- [x] MCP: `list_dashboards` and `get_dashboard_widget` through `/api/v1/mcp` answer what `GET /projects/{projectKey}/dashboards` and `GET /widgets/{widgetID}/data` answer for the same reader, and a widget of somebody else's private dashboard gives `isError`. No test calls either tool.
- [x] Computed values when a child is trashed and restored: `DELETE /requirements/{reqKey}` on a child drops it from its section's `sum(children, ...)`, and `POST /projects/{projectKey}/trash/{requirementID}/restore` brings it back. Only a move away is tried in computed_test.go.

Database guards:
- [x] Through SQL as exciter_app: carol, a reader, `UPDATE dashboard_widget SET title` and `DELETE FROM dashboard_widget` on bob's shared dashboard change no row; a project administrator may do both; and `UPDATE dashboard SET project_id` is refused (`dashboard_fixed`). Only an insert of a widget and the owner change are tried today. (decided in #394: `exciter_app` has no privilege on `project_id`, so it is refused before `dashboard_fixed`, which the superuser meets)
- [x] `project_clear_home_dashboard` called through SQL by a reader for another project leaves its home dashboard alone while that dashboard is still shared.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] Share and read: alice makes a private dashboard, then "Arrange" (`arrange-dashboard`) and "Share" (`share-dashboard`). Bob opens `/p/$projectKey/dashboards/$dashboardId` directly and sees the same widgets but no "Arrange". "Stop sharing" takes it from bob's list. No scenario shares a dashboard or has a second person open it.
- [x] "Copy link" (`copy-dashboard-link`) on a shared dashboard puts the dashboard's address on the clipboard and shows "The link is copied. Whoever reads the project opens it."; "Export as PDF" (`dashboard-pdf`) downloads a PDF named after the dashboard.
- [x] While arranging: "Rename" saves a new name into the heading and the list, "Change <title>" opens the widget form and "Save the widget" (`save-widget`) changes its title, the width select widens a card, "Remove <title>" takes it off, and "Delete the dashboard" (`delete-dashboard`) returns to the list without it. Only add and move are clicked today.
- [x] Home dashboard: an administrator picks a shared dashboard as "Home dashboard" in the project settings; the project's home then shows it above the requirements and its heading links to the dashboard.
- [x] Print: `/print/dashboards/$dashboardId` as the reader shows every widget and sets the print ready marker, and for a dashboard the reader may not read shows the failure text. No spec opens the route.
- [x] Computed attribute refused in the browser: a formula naming an attribute nobody has shows the error under "Formula" and the form does not save; a formula that would make a cycle is refused with the attributes named; deleting an attribute a formula reads (`delete-attribute`) shows the `attribute_in_formula` sentence and the attribute stays. computed.spec.ts only saves a formula that holds.
- [x] Changing a formula with "Save" (`save-attribute`) shows the recompute status with its count until it ends, and the grid column of the computed attribute then sorts by the new values.

Go unit:
- [x] `attribute.selfOrder`, `sameValues`, `checkComputed`, `formulaKind` and `kindOf`, and `cyclesOf` over defs alone: order of formulas that read each other, equal and unequal value maps, a computed input that also asks for options or a default, and each kind there and back. `attribute` has 16.8% unit coverage and these need no database.

## Done when
- Every control of the dashboard pages, including share, copy link, PDF, rename, delete and the widget controls, is used by a browser scenario, and a second person reads a shared dashboard.
- Each dashboard refusal code (`too_many_dashboards`, `too_many_widgets` and every `config.*` field) is asserted with its status, and rows are shown unchanged.
- A computed attribute is refused and recomputed in the browser, and the worker's pure helpers have unit tests.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XsypREK6CTfvi1885SVu2k

issues.title: Test accepting findings, editing terms and merging duplicates in the browser
issues.body:
The services and their guards are well covered: quality_test.go scores, checks drafts, accepts, carries and takes back a finding, switches rules and words and reads the score in the query language, and `TestRawSQLKeepsFindingsToTheirRevision` tries every quality table through SQL. glossary_test.go defines terms, finds their uses in any inflection, marks uses suspect and confirms them, reaches library glossaries and deletes a term, with `TestRawSQLKeepsGlossariesToTheirReaders`. duplicates_test.go finds, dismisses, links and merges pairs and sets the threshold, with `TestRawSQLKeepsDuplicatesHonest`. The vitest suites of quality, glossary and duplicates cover most panels. What is missing is the browser beyond the first look: quality.spec.ts, glossary.spec.ts and duplicates.spec.ts each check that marks show and one pair is dismissed, but nobody accepts or takes back a finding, changes the writing rules or word lists, edits, deletes or reloads a term, confirms a suspect use, unlinks a term, chooses a library glossary, links or merges a pair, filters or pages the pairs, or saves the threshold. On the API side, the refusals of linking, merging and taking back are tried only in part, the pairs are never paged, and the MCP tools `get_quality_findings`, `check_requirement_text`, `list_terms` and `get_similar_requirements` are never called. The `glossary` and `duplicates` packages have no unit tests for their pure checks.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these writes were never answered 403: `POST /projects/{projectKey}/duplicates/link`, `DELETE /requirements/{reqKey}/quality/accepted/{findingKey}`, `PATCH /terms/{termID}`; these were never answered 422: `POST /projects/{projectKey}/duplicates/link`, `POST /projects/{projectKey}/duplicates/merge`, `POST /projects/{projectKey}/similar`, `DELETE /requirements/{reqKey}/quality/accepted/{findingKey}`, `DELETE /terms/{termID}`, `PATCH /terms/{termID}`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #395: `DELETE /terms/{termID}` takes no input, so it has no 422; its address is refused 400 or 404)
- [x] `POST /projects/{projectKey}/duplicates/link`: carol, a reader, is 403 `forbidden`; a side at an old revision is 409 `stale_revision`; the same requirement twice is 422 on `target`; a `linkTypeKey` the project lacks is 422; and no link or decision is written in any of them. Only the success is tried today. (decided in #395: an unknown `linkTypeKey` was refused on `typeId`; fixed to `linkTypeKey`)
- [x] `POST /projects/{projectKey}/duplicates/merge`: a stale side is 409 `stale_revision`; `keep` and `trash` the same is 422 on `trash`; a side of another project is 422 on that side; a `comment` over `MaxReasonChars` is 422 on `comment`; a trash side locked by somebody else (`POST /requirements/{reqKey}/lock`) is refused. In each case neither side is trashed and no link moved. Only carol's 403 is tried.
- [x] `GET /projects/{projectKey}/duplicates` paged: with `limit=1` the `next` cursor returns the second pair and no pair twice; `limit=0` and `limit` over `MaxLimit` are 422 on `limit`; `type=<not a uuid>` is 422 on `type`; `section` and `query` narrow the pairs. pairsOf in duplicates_test.go only reads the first page with no narrowing.
- [x] `DELETE /requirements/{reqKey}/quality/accepted/{findingKey}`: carol is 403, a key that was never accepted is 404, and `revision` missing or not a number is 422 on `revision`; the acceptance stays in each. Only bob's success is tried. (decided in #395: a key never accepted is 422 on `key`, as accepting one the revision lacks is)
- [x] `PATCH /terms/{termID}`: carol is 403; renaming to a synonym of another term is 409 `term_exists`; a project that only uses a library's glossary cannot change the library's term (403 for its editors). Only a stale `baseRevision` is refused today. (decided in #395: these answered 404 because the term was locked before the right was judged; fixed to 403)
- [x] `GET /terms/{termID}/uses` and `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/terms` as somebody outside the project are 404, and a term of a library the reader may not read does not appear in `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/terms`.
- [x] MCP: `get_quality_findings` and `check_requirement_text` answer what `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/quality` and `POST /projects/{projectKey}/quality-check` answer, `list_terms` what `GET /projects/{projectKey}/terms` answers, and `get_similar_requirements` what `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/similar` answers; a reader's token gets `isError` from `check_requirement_text`. No test calls any of the four.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] Findings: on a requirement with a vague word, "Show in text" (`show-finding`) marks the words; "Accept: <words>" (`accept-finding`), a reason and the confirm (`confirm-accept-finding`) raise the score in the badge; "Take back: <words>" (`withdraw-acceptance`) lowers it again. quality.spec.ts only sees the mark and the row on the quality page.
- [x] Quality settings: an administrator switches a rule off and "Save rules" (`save-quality-rules`); the finding goes from the requirement and the quality page. Adding a word in "Word lists" and "Save word lists" (`save-quality-words`) marks it on the next check.
- [x] Glossary: "New term" (`new-term`) and "Save term" (`save-term`) add a row; on the term page "Edit" (`edit-term`) changes the definition, which makes the use on R1 suspect; "Delete term" (`delete-term`) and the confirm (`confirm-delete-term`) remove it and its row. glossary.spec.ts makes the term over the API.
- [x] Suspect use: after the definition changes, the requirement's terms panel shows the use as suspect; "Confirm..." (`confirm-term`), a comment and the send (`send-confirm-term`) clear it. A second tab that edits the term shows "Load the latest revision" (`reload-term`) on the first.
- [x] Linking a term by hand: select words in the statement, use the term button in the toolbar (`format-term`) and pick the term; the terms panel lists it as explicit. "Remove the link" (`unlink-term`) takes it away. No spec links or unlinks a term.
- [x] Library glossaries: in the settings, "Add" (`add-glossary`) a library and "Save libraries" (`save-glossaries`); a term of the library is then marked in this project's requirement and listed on its glossary page.
- [x] Duplicates: "Link..." (`link-pair`) and its confirm (`confirm-link-pair`) remove the pair and add a link on both requirements; "Merge..." (`merge-pair`), the confirm (`confirm-merge-pair`) and "Done" (`close-merge`) trash one side and list the links moved. Only dismiss is clicked today.
- [x] Duplicates: "Filter" (`filter-pairs`) narrows the pairs by a query, "More" (`more-pairs`) loads the next page, and after a side is changed in another tab the stale notice offers "Read the pairs again" (`read-pairs-again`), which reloads them.
- [x] Threshold: "Save threshold" (`save-duplicate-settings`) in the quality settings changes which pairs the duplicates page lists. duplicates.spec.ts sets it over the API.

Component (vitest):
- [x] DuplicatesPage: "Link..." sends the pair and the link type and removes the pair; "More" asks with the cursor; "Filter" sends `query`. duplicates.test.tsx covers dismiss, merge and the stale notice only.
- [x] TermPicker and QualitySettingsCards: "Remove the link" sends the unlink, and "Save word lists" sends the added and removed words. glossary.test.tsx and quality.test.tsx never use either.

Go unit:
- [x] `glossary.checkName`, `checkWords`, `checkDefinition`, `checkStatus`, `checkComment`, `patched` and `sameDocument`, and `duplicates.textOf`: blank, too long and duplicate words, a definition that is no document, an unknown status, a patch that changes nothing. Both packages have no unit test today.

## Done when
- Every control of the quality, glossary and duplicates pages and panels is used by a browser scenario that checks its effect.
- Link, merge, take back and term changes are refused in integration tests with their status and code, with rows shown unchanged, and the pairs are paged.
- The four MCP tools of the area are called by a test.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XsypREK6CTfvi1885SVu2k

issues.title: Test variants, refused reuses and the via stamp on every table
issues.body:
Reuse is covered as one long story: `TestLibraryRequirementsAreReusedAndKeptAsVariants` (reuse_test.go) refuses a reuse from no library and into the library itself, follows, falls behind, takes a revision, makes a variant, hides the source from a reader and purges the source; `TestRawSQLGuardsReuse` tries the reuse columns through SQL. reuse.spec.ts reuses a requirement in the browser and takes its next revision, and reuse.test.tsx covers the banner. For via, `TestWhatIsWrittenThroughATokenSaysSo` checks revisions, activity, comments, links, the audit log, the event and an OAuth client, and `TestRawSQLStampsWhatARowWasWrittenThrough` tries the stamp through SQL on `audit_log`; via.spec.ts sees the stamp in the history. What is missing: nobody makes a variant or takes the source again in the browser, and "Reuse" from the similar hint is never clicked. A reuse into a project the person may not edit, or into an archived one, is never refused, and nobody reuses a section with what is below it and checks the children. Taking a source in the trash, a revision the source never had, and a take while the requirement is locked are never tried. The files a source's words show are never checked on the reuse. The via stamp is tried through SQL only on `audit_log`, and reviews, Armature and Stator links and test runs are never checked for it.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/reuse` refused: into a project the person only reads is 403 `forbidden`; into an archived project is 409 `project_archived`; into a project key nobody has is 422 on `projectKey` (decided in #376: 404 `not_found`, so a refusal never tells which keys exist). In each the target project has no new requirement. Only no library, the library itself and a guest (404) are tried today.
- [x] Reuse with `children: true`: every requirement below the section arrives in the same order, each `following` its own source, and a later child added to the library section does not arrive by itself. reuse_test.go only reads the section's kind and R2.
- [x] `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/reuse/take` refused: a reuse in the trash is 409 with the trash code (`ErrTrashed`); a revision above the source's is 409 `source_moved_on` naming the source's revision; a requirement locked by somebody else is refused with the lock's code; a source in the trash (not purged) is either taken or refused, decided and asserted. Only revision 1 after 2 and a hidden source are tried.
- [x] `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/reuse/variant`: a reader of the target project is 403; a second variant call on a variant answers 200 and writes no second change entry (the code skips it); a variant in the trash is refused. Only success and `not_reused` are tried.
- [x] Files: a library requirement whose statement shows a picture is reused; the reuse has its own copy of the picture and its statement points at it. After the source drops the picture and the reuse takes that revision, a newly shown file arrives and the dropped one does not come again (`filesShown`). No reuse test has an attachment.
- [x] Test case and risk: taking a source of type test case brings its steps, and a risk rating comes along only as far as the target project's scales hold its values (`fitRating`). Assert the rating left out when a scale lacks the value.
- [x] Via on the other stamped tables: a review (`POST /requirements/{reqKey}/reviews`), an Armature issue link, a Stator page link and a test run written through a token each read back with `via.kind` `token` and the token's name, and the same written in the browser carry none. Only revisions, changes, comments, trace links and the audit log are checked today.

Database guards:
- [x] Through SQL as exciter_app holding a token: `UPDATE comment SET via_name = 'x'` and `UPDATE trace_link SET via_kind = NULL` are refused with `via_fixed`; an insert into `requirement_revision` with a forged `via_name` is stamped with the held token's name instead. Only `audit_log` is tried, and its update only as the superuser.
- [x] Through SQL, `app.via` set to an OAuth grant the person holds stamps `oauth` and the client's name; a grant of somebody else's, or a revoked grant, stamps nothing (`via_held`). Only tokens are tried through SQL.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] Variant: on a reused requirement "Make a variant" (`make-variant`) shows "This is a variant now. Its words are its own."; editing the title is then allowed and saves. After the source moves on, "Take revision N and follow again" brings the source's words back and the banner reads "Follows" again. reuse.spec.ts only takes a revision while following.
- [x] Reuse from the similar hint: in a project that uses a library, writing a new requirement like a library one shows it in "Similar requirements"; its reuse button (`reuse-similar`) makes a reuse in this project and opens it. No spec clicks it.
- [x] Reuse of a section with "Reuse everything below it too": the target project's tree shows the section and its children, each with the "Reused" badge.
- [x] Via in comments and reviews: a comment and a review written through a token show "through <token name>" in the requirement's comments and review panel (the `Through` element), and the same written in the browser show nothing. via.spec.ts only checks the history.

## Done when

- "Make a variant", taking a source again and reuse from the similar hint are used by browser scenarios.

issues.title: Test every workflow rule, the designer's inspector and the type and status controls
issues.body:
The shaping of a project is well tested over the API: `TestTypesAndAttributesOverTheAPI` (attributes_test.go) refuses editors, bad bodies, a changed kind, deleting what was used and a retired default; field_rules_test.go covers a field required from a status, dependent choices, who may change a field, trace and discussion validators and the bulk transition; workflow_test.go covers the default workflow's conditions, a stale transition, statuses in use, saving, assigning with a mapping and deleting a followed workflow; `TestRawSQLKeepsTypesAndAttributesToTheirProject`, `TestRawSQLHoldsFieldRules` and `TestRawSQLMovesStatusesOnlyByTransitions` try the guards through SQL. The client has strong vitest suites (workflows.test.tsx, graph.test.ts, flow.test.ts, types.test.tsx, fieldRules.test.tsx), and attributes.spec.ts, workflow.spec.ts, field-rules.spec.ts and control.spec.ts make a type, a select attribute, a workflow, a links rule and a locking status in the browser. What is missing: five of the fourteen workflow rules (`condition.is_owner`, `validator.owner_required`, `validator.required_attributes`, `validator.coverage_full` and `postfunction.clear_owner`) are never put on a transition in any integration test, and a bad rule configuration is never refused. Archived projects are tried only through SQL. A workflow step can name another project's status through SQL, and nothing tries it. In the browser nobody edits, retires or deletes a type or attribute, sets a field rule, makes or deletes a status, deletes a workflow, or uses the inspector's buttons (add transition, starting status, remove status or transition). The MCP tools `list_transitions` and `transition_requirement` are never called.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these writes were never answered 403: `POST /projects/{projectKey}/transitions`, `PATCH /projects/{projectKey}/types/{typeID}`; these were never answered 422: `DELETE /projects/{projectKey}/attributes/{attributeID}`, `DELETE /projects/{projectKey}/statuses/{statusID}`, `PATCH /projects/{projectKey}/statuses/{statusID}`, `DELETE /projects/{projectKey}/types/{typeID}`, `DELETE /projects/{projectKey}/workflows/{workflowID}`, `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/workflows/{workflowID}`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #396: the DELETE routes take no body and so never answer 422; their 400, 403, 404 and 409 are asserted)
- [x] The untested rules, one transition each, saved with `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/workflows/{workflowID}`: `condition.is_owner` offers the transition in `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/transitions` only to the owner; `validator.owner_required` refuses `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/transitions` with 422 on `ownerId` until an owner is set; `validator.required_attributes` refuses with the attribute's field named; `validator.coverage_full` refuses with "is not fully" until the requirement is covered; `postfunction.clear_owner` leaves the requirement with no owner. The status stays put on every refusal.
- [x] Rule configuration refused on save: an unknown rule type, `validator.links_exist` without `linkTypeId` or with a link type of another project, `validator.quality_min` with `minimum` outside its bounds, and `condition.project_role` with a role nobody has are each 422 naming the rule's field, and `GET /projects/{projectKey}/workflows/{workflowID}` still returns the saved graph. Only a workflow without a start is tried. (decided in #396: refused on `transitions` with a sentence naming the rule; a link type of another project was saved and is now refused)
- [x] Workflows across projects: `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE /projects/{projectKey}/workflows/{workflowID}` with a workflow id of another project the administrator also runs are 404; a graph naming a status of another project is 422; `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/workflow` mapping a status to one the new workflow lacks is 422.
- [x] Statuses: `PATCH /projects/{projectKey}/statuses/{statusID}` to the name of another status is 422 on `name`; `DELETE` of a status a workflow names but no requirement has is 409 and the status stays (tried only through SQL); a status id of another project is 404.
- [x] Types and attributes: `PATCH /projects/{projectKey}/types/{typeID}` to another type's name and `PATCH /projects/{projectKey}/attributes/{attributeID}` to another attribute's name are 422 on `name`; in an archived project `POST /projects/{projectKey}/types`, `POST /projects/{projectKey}/attributes` and `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/field-rules/{field}` are 409 `project_archived`. Today the archive is tried only through SQL in attribute_rls_test.go.
- [x] `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/field-rules/{field}`: a field that is not fixed (`colour`) is 404, `editableBy` with an unknown role is 422 on `editableBy`, and `GET /projects/{projectKey}/field-rules` as a guest is 404.
- [x] MCP: `list_transitions` answers what `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/transitions` answers for the same person, and `transition_requirement` takes one and is refused with `isError` naming the reason for a transition the person is not offered. No test calls either.

Database guards:
- [x] Through SQL as a project administrator: `INSERT INTO workflow_step` (and `UPDATE ... SET on_revision_status_id`) naming a `req_status` of another project. Today `workflow_step_status_id_fkey` only checks the status exists, so this needs a guard as well as a test (see the separate report). (the guard came with #340; #396 adds the project administrator's test)
- [x] Through SQL as an editor: `INSERT INTO transition_rule` on a transition of the project and `UPDATE workflow_step SET status_id` change nothing. Only renaming a transition and deleting its rules are tried.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] Types: "Edit" (`edit-type`) renames a type and the new name shows in the requirement form's type select; "Retire" takes it from the select for new requirements; "Delete" (`delete-type`) on an unused type removes the row, and on a used one shows the `in_use` sentence. attributes.spec.ts only makes a type.
- [x] Attributes: "Edit" (`edit-attribute`) adds an option that the requirement form then offers; "Delete" (`delete-attribute`) on an unused attribute removes the row; "Move <name> up" reorders the form's fields.
- [x] Field rules: on an attribute, "Required from" a status makes the transition into it refuse without the value; "Who changes it" with "Add a line" (`add-permit`) keeps an editor from changing it in that status; on the fixed fields card "Save" (`save-field-rule`) makes Owner required from In review. No spec sets a field rule in the browser.
- [x] Statuses: "New status" (`new-status`) and "Create status" add a row; "Delete" (`delete-status`) removes an unused one and is refused for one in use with the sentence shown. control.spec.ts only edits a status. (decided in #396: the one in use is a status a workflow names, since Delete is hidden on one that holds requirements)
- [x] Designer inspector on `/p/$projectKey/settings/workflows/$workflowId`: select a status and "New requirements start here" (`make-initial`) moves the start; "Add transition" (`add-transition`) from the inspector draws an arrow; "Remove transition" (`remove-transition`) and "Remove from the workflow" (`remove-status`) take them away; a new status made in the designer (`create-status`) appears on the canvas and in the status list after "Save workflow". workflow.spec.ts only adds statuses and drags one arrow.
- [x] "Delete <name>" (`delete-workflow`) on a workflow nobody follows removes its card, and on a followed one shows the `in_use` sentence. (decided in #396: Delete is hidden on a followed workflow, so the scenario has it followed while the page is open)

Go unit:
- [x] `attribute.applyType` and `workflow.applyStatus`: blank and long names, an icon outside the offered set, a colour that is not #rrggbb (and one in capitals made lower case), an unknown type role, an unknown status category, a long description and a negative position kept at 0. Neither has a unit test and both need no database. (decided in #396: an icon is held to its shape, not to the client's set)

## Done when
- Every rule in `workflow/rules.go` is put on a transition in an integration test that shows it refusing or acting, and bad rule configurations are refused with the field named.
- A workflow step cannot name another project's status, and a test proves it through SQL.
- Every control of the types, attributes, field rules, statuses and workflow designer settings is used by a browser scenario that checks its effect on a requirement.

issues.title: Test verification evidence, the trace check and exciter-ci against a real stack
issues.body:
The way evidence lands is tested well in the Go suite. `test_results_test.go` covers a run landing with its counts and the keys that verify nothing, a run read only by its uploader and the administrators, a reader's upload refused with 403, field refusals for `commit`, `runUrl`, `repository` and the files, a revision outdating a result, a second branch counting once it is named, coverage, the matrix and chains of tests, the trace check on `failing`, `outdated` and `broken`, baselines and signatures holding the evidence, pruning, the evidence token and its refusals, and the policies through SQL. `code_tags_test.go` does the same for scans: problems per tag, the revision a tag carries, outdated and orphaned tags, the tag words read at query time, notifications, the token, and `code_scan_replace` and the tag policies through SQL. `testresult/junit_test.go`, `codescan/scan_test.go` and `cmd/exciter-ci/main_test.go` cover parsing, the comment scanner and the command against a fake server. In the browser, `test-results.spec.ts` and `code-tags.spec.ts` upload with a token and see the result, the code link and an orphaned tag. `evidence.test.tsx` and `code.test.tsx` cover the panels, the counting branch form and the tag words form. What is missing is the archived project, the upload limits other than the tag count, a run the worker cannot land, paging and the branch filter of the code tags, the `gaps` reason, the three MCP tools, the guards that keep a run and a scan unchanged, and any run of the real exciter-ci image or the `make` targets in `mk/evidence.mk` against a stack. In the browser nobody names the counting branch, sets the tag words, filters the code tags page or turns its pages. `codetrace` has no unit tests at all.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Archived project: `POST /projects/{projectKey}/test-runs`, `POST /projects/{projectKey}/code-scans`, `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/evidence-settings` and `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/code-tag-words` on an archived project are 409 `project_archived`. No `test_run` or `code_scan` row is added and the settings and words are unchanged. Today only a reader's 403 is tried.
- [x] Upload limits of a test run: 101 parts named `file` (`MaxRunFiles`) are 422 on `file`, a body past `MaxRunBytes` is 413 `too_large`, a form field over 4 KiB (`maxFormField`) is 422 naming the field, a `job` over 200 characters is 422 on `job`, and a JSON body instead of multipart is 400 `bad_request`. In every case no run is queued. Today only `commit`, `runUrl`, a missing `repository`, no file and a stray file are tried.
- [x] A run the worker cannot land: insert a queued `test_run` whose `cases` the worker cannot read and run `testresult.Handler`. Assert that `GET /test-runs/{runID}` shows `state` `failed` with the sentence "The run could not be read onto its requirements...", that `cases` is cleared and that no `test_result` row exists. Today every run in the suite lands as `done`.
- [x] Code scan refusals: a body with an unknown field is 400 `bad_request` (`DisallowUnknownFields`), a body past `MaxScanBytes` is 413 `too_large`, and a missing `repository`, `commit` or `branch` is 422 naming it. Also 422 for `tags[0].path` empty, `tags[0].word` empty, and a `fileUrl` without `{path}`. Today only a `javascript:` `fileUrl`, `tags[0].line`, `tags[0].key` and the tag count are tried.
- [x] `GET /projects/{projectKey}/code-tags`: with more tags than one page, `limit` and `offset` walk the pages with no tag repeated and `total` unchanged. `limit=501` (over `MaxLimit`) is 422. `branch=` a second scanned branch lists that branch's tags. Today only `state` is tried.
- [x] `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/code-links?branch=...` keeps only that branch's links and returns `countingBranch`. A person outside the project gets 404. Today only the unfiltered read is tried.
- [x] `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/code-tag-words` with 11 words for one relation (`MaxWords`) or with an empty list is 422 on that relation. The saved words are unchanged afterwards. Today only a badly shaped word and a word in both relations are tried.
- [x] `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/evidence-settings` with a `countingBranch` of 201 characters is 422 `countingBranch`. A person outside the project gets 404 from `GET`. Today only a blank branch and an editor's 403 are tried.
- [x] `GET /projects/{projectKey}/trace-check?fail=gaps`: a requirement whose coverage rule asks for `verified` without a passing test fails the check and is listed under `gaps` with its dimension and level. With `fail=failing` alone the same project passes. A `query` that does not parse is 422 with the query's error. Today `gaps` is never asserted and no bad query is tried. (decided in #398: a query that does not parse stays 400 `bad_query` with its position, as every reader of the query language answers it)
- [x] MCP: `get_test_results`, `get_code_links` and `run_trace_check` through `/api/v1/mcp` answer what the HTTP calls answer, including `branch`. `run_trace_check` with an unknown `fail` reason returns `isError`. No test calls any of the three today.

Database guards:
- [x] As the uploader through SQL, `UPDATE test_run SET branch = 'other'` and `UPDATE test_run SET commit_sha = ...` are refused by `test_run_fixed`, and setting `cases` back to a non-empty array is refused by `test_run_cases`. Today only moving the state back is tried. (decided in #398: `exciter_app` holds no update grant on the branch or commit, so it is refused by privilege first; `test_run_fixed` is proven as the superuser)
- [x] As the uploader through SQL, `INSERT INTO test_result` for a requirement of another project, a trashed requirement or a section, while the run is `running`, is a policy violation (`test_result_writers`). Today only a run that is not running is tried.
- [x] As an editor through SQL, `UPDATE evidence_settings` and `UPDATE code_tag_words` touch no row, and as the administrator of an archived project the same updates and an `INSERT` are refused (`project_open`). Today only an editor's `INSERT` is tried for each. (decided in #398: row security leaves those updates no row to touch, so they change nothing rather than erroring; the `INSERT` is the policy violation)
- [x] As the uploader within the transaction that made a scan, `UPDATE code_scan SET branch = 'other'` is refused by `code_scan_fixed`. A `code_tag` naming a requirement of another project is a policy violation. Today only a later counts update and a revision ahead are tried. (decided in #398: refused by privilege first for `exciter_app`; `code_scan_fixed` is proven as the superuser)

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] Project settings, Trace tab: an administrator types a branch into "Counting branch" and clicks "Save" (`save-evidence-settings`). "Saved." shows, and on the requirement the results panel heading reads "On <branch>, which counts". The coverage of the requirement follows that branch's result. No scenario saves the counting branch today.
- [x] Project settings, Trace tab: add a word to "Words for implements" and click "Save" (`save-code-tag-words`). A tag using that word, uploaded earlier, now shows on its requirement's Code panel with no new scan. No scenario sets the tag words today.
- [x] Code tags page: "Show" set to "Orphaned" leaves only the orphaned row and "Outdated" only the outdated one. With more than 50 tags, "Next" and "Previous" walk the pages. Today the scenario only reads the unfiltered table.
- [x] A shell test or e2e setup that builds the `ci` image (`make ci-image`) and runs `make test-results`, `make code-scan` and `make trace-check` against the stack with an evidence token. It asserts the exit codes 0, then 1 on a failing check, then 2 on a wrong token, and that the run and the tags show in the API. Today exciter-ci is only tested against a fake server and the image is only checked to be released.

Go unit:
- [x] `codetrace`: table tests for `checkWords` (trimming, duplicates kept once, a word in both relations, `MaxWords`, `MaxWordLength`), `checkScan` (every field, `fileUrl` shape), `relationOf` (case folding), `placed` and `FileLink` (a path with spaces and `#` escaped per segment, no template). The package has no unit tests today. Also `cmd/exciter-ci`: a run that ends `failed` exits 2 with its error, `--wait 0` exits 0 without polling, a run still `queued` past the wait exits 2 naming `/test-runs/<id>`, a pattern that matches no file says "no report matches", a 422 from Exciter prints "Exciter refused:" with the field, and `Unreported` prints its count.

## Done when
- Every evidence operation has an integration test for the archived project and for each field refusal and limit it has, and checks that nothing was written.
- The guards on `test_run`, `test_result`, `code_scan`, `code_tag`, `evidence_settings` and `code_tag_words` are each tried through SQL as `exciter_app`.
- Both settings cards and the code tags filter and paging are driven by a browser scenario that checks the effect elsewhere.
- The released `ci` image and the `mk/evidence.mk` targets run against a real stack in the gate.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XsypREK6CTfvi1885SVu2k

issues.title: Test plans, executions and the step runner past the happy path
issues.body:
The main path through test management is tested well. `test_executions_test.go` starts an execution of a plan against a baseline, pins the iterations, records step by step, puts files on a step and deletes them, refuses a reader's result and another person's file deletion with 403, closes the execution and refuses a later result and change with 409 `execution_closed`, and reads the report as JSON, Word and PDF. It also covers plans picked or found by a query and a 404 for each unknown id, and through SQL that only the start pins cases, only a tester records as themselves and a closed execution does not change. `test_cases_test.go` covers steps, parameters and their revisions. `test_traceability_test.go` covers CI filling open executions, coverage, queries, chains, the matrix and baselines from the last result, and its guard through SQL. `TestAFailedCaseIsFiledAsAnIssue` files a failure in the Armature stub. In the browser, `test-cases.spec.ts` writes a case with steps, and `test-executions.spec.ts` makes a plan, adds a case, starts an execution, fails a step with a note and a file, closes it and downloads the PDF. `test-traceability.spec.ts` sees a CI result fill an execution. `tests.test.tsx` covers the list, making a plan, closing or aborting and the step runner. What is missing is almost every field refusal of a start, a plan, a file and an issue, aborting, the due reminder, group testers, the archived project, the guards on what an execution was started over, and all eleven MCP tools. In the browser nobody edits an execution, deletes a plan, changes a plan's query, moves or removes a plan's case, walks the step runner with "Previous" and "Next", sets the case outcome by hand, deletes a file or files an issue. The print view of an execution is only checked to be a PDF.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these writes were never answered 403: `POST /projects/{projectKey}/test-executions`, `POST /test-executions/{executionID}/cases/{reqKey}/files`, `POST /test-executions/{executionID}/cases/{reqKey}/issues`, `DELETE /test-plans/{planID}`, `PUT /test-plans/{planID}/cases`; these were never answered 422: `DELETE /test-execution-files/{fileID}`, `PATCH /test-executions/{executionID}`, `POST /test-executions/{executionID}/cases/{reqKey}/files`, `POST /test-executions/{executionID}/close`, `DELETE /test-plans/{planID}`, `PATCH /test-plans/{planID}`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed.
- [x] `POST /projects/{projectKey}/test-executions` refusals, each 422 with its field and no execution row: no tester and 51 testers (`MaxTesters`), the same tester twice, a tester with `subjectType` `role`, a `dueAt` in the past or more than a year ahead, a `planId` of another project, a `baselineId` of another project, and a plan whose cases the baseline does not hold ("The plan holds no test case to run here"). A reader starting one is 403. Today only a tester outside the project is tried.
- [x] Plans refused with 422 naming the field: `scope` `mixed`, `scope` `query` with no query and with a query that does not parse, 501 cases (`MaxPlanCases`), a case key of another project, and `PATCH /test-plans/{planID}` with a `query` on a picked plan. A reader's `PUT /test-plans/{planID}/cases` and `DELETE /test-plans/{planID}` are 403 and the plan is unchanged. Today only a requirement that is no case, cases on a query plan and a guest's create and rename are tried.
- [x] Archived project: `POST /projects/{projectKey}/test-plans`, `POST /projects/{projectKey}/test-executions`, `PUT /test-executions/{executionID}/cases/{reqKey}/result` and `POST .../files` on an archived project are 409 `project_archived` and write nothing.
- [x] Abort: `POST /test-executions/{executionID}/close` with `abort: true` leaves `state` `aborted`, refuses later results with 409 `execution_closed`, and the passed result it held no longer counts. `casesResult = passed` drops the case and coverage from runs falls back to partial. Closing twice is 409. A close comment over the limit is 422 `comment`. Each tester gets one `execution_closed` notification (kind), which no test checks today. Today only a plain close is tried, and aborting only in vitest.
- [x] Due reminder: an execution due within `ReminderLead`, then `testexec.NewReminder(...).Once`. Each tester gets one `execution_reminder` notification, a second `Once` adds none, and `PATCH /test-executions/{executionID}` with a new `dueAt` lets it remind once more. A closed execution is never reminded. No test runs the reminder today.
- [x] A group as tester: start an execution with `subjectType` `group`. A member of the group may record and sees it under `GET /test-executions/mine`, and is told `execution_assigned`. A person outside the group gets 403 on `PUT .../result`. Today every tester is a single user.
- [x] `PUT /test-executions/{executionID}/cases/{reqKey}/result`: `outcome` `maybe` is 422 `outcome`, iteration 3 of a case with two is 404, a case key not in the execution is 404, and an explicit `outcome` overrides what the steps say. Today only a step the case lacks is tried.
- [x] Files: an empty file is 422 `file`, a file past `MaxFileMB` is 413 `too_large`, `step=9` on a two step case is 422 `step`, and the 21st file on one step (`MaxFilesPerStep`) is 422 `file`. Upload and delete after closing are 409 `execution_closed`. A reader uploading is 403. `GET /test-execution-files/{fileID}` of a file sent as `text/html` answers `Content-Disposition: attachment` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Today only a good upload, a download and two deletions are tried.
- [x] `POST /test-executions/{executionID}/cases/{reqKey}/issues`: with no Armature connected it is 409 `armature_not_configured`, a reader is 403, a `typeId` that is no uuid is 422 `typeId`, and `step: 0` or `step: 101` is refused before anything reaches Armature, with no issue made in the stub. Today only a case that did not fail and one good filing are tried.
- [x] Lists: `GET /projects/{projectKey}/test-executions?state=closed` and `?state=aborted` keep only those, and `GET /test-executions/mine` leaves out an execution the caller neither tests nor manages. `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/test-executions` leaves out an aborted execution's results.
- [x] MCP: `list_test_plans`, `get_test_plan`, `start_test_execution`, `list_test_executions`, `list_my_test_executions`, `get_test_execution`, `get_test_execution_case`, `record_test_result`, `close_test_execution`, `file_test_failure_issue` and `get_test_case_results` through `/api/v1/mcp` answer what the HTTP calls answer. A reader's token gets `isError` from `record_test_result` and `start_test_execution`. No test calls any of them today.

Database guards:
- [x] As the manager through SQL, `UPDATE test_execution SET plan_id`, `baseline_id`, `manager_id` or `excluded` to another value is refused by `test_execution_fixed`. Today only a change after closing is tried.
- [x] As the manager through SQL after the start, `INSERT INTO test_execution_tester` is a policy violation (`test_execution_tester_namers`). An editor inserting a `test_execution` with somebody else as `manager_id`, or into an archived project, is a policy violation.
- [x] Through SQL after closing, a tester's `INSERT INTO test_execution_step`, `test_execution_file` and `test_execution_issue` are refused by `test_execution_closed`, and a `DELETE FROM test_execution_file` deletes no row. An `INSERT INTO test_execution_file` with an `object_key` of its own gets the key `test_execution_file_key` writes, and a delete leaves an `attachment_tombstone` row.
- [x] Through SQL, `INSERT INTO test_plan` and `test_plan_case` by a reader and by an editor of an archived project are policy violations. A plan case naming a trashed case or a case of another project is refused by `test_plan_case_kept`. Today only a requirement that is no test case is tried.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] Plan page: "Move <key> down" and "Remove <key>" reorder and drop a case, and the order holds after a reload. For a plan by query, changing the query and clicking "Save" (`save-plan-query`) changes the cases listed. "Delete the plan" (`delete-plan`), then confirm (`confirm-delete-plan`), returns to the Tests page without the plan, while the executions it started keep its title. No scenario does any of this today.
- [x] Execution page: "Edit" (`edit-execution`), change the version and configuration and "Save" (`save-execution`). The header shows them, and so does the report. Close with "Abort it, so its results count for nothing" checked, and the coverage page shows the case no longer verifies. Today only a plain close is clicked.
- [x] Step runner with two cases or two iterations: "Next" (`next-case`) and "Previous" (`previous-case`) move between them, keeping each recorded outcome. "Outcome of the case" set to "Blocked" overrides the steps, and "Delete <file>" removes an uploaded file. Today only one case is recorded.
- [x] With the Armature stub connected, fail a step, click "File an issue" (`file-issue`), pick the failed step and "File it" (`file-issue-send`). The issue key shows on the case, and the requirement it verifies lists the issue. No scenario files an issue today.
- [x] Home page: an open execution the person tests shows under "Your test executions" and opens the execution. After it is closed it is gone from there. The print view `/print/executions/$executionId` shows the title, version, configuration, each case with its outcome and the step note. Today only the PDF's first bytes are checked.

Component (vitest):
- [x] StartExecutionDialog: a 422 on `dueAt`, `testers` or `planId` shows beside its field, the start button stays disabled with no tester, and removing a tester takes them out of what is sent. FileIssueDialog: only Armature projects the person may create in are offered, the step select offers the failed steps, and a 409 `armature_not_configured` shows its sentence. Only the step roll-up is unit tested today, in `rollup_test.go`.

issues.title: Test the risk scheme editor, the FMEA table and the risk report end to end
issues.body:
Ratings and mitigations are tested well in the Go suite. `risks_test.go` covers a risk rated on its scheme with its levels and priority number, a rating on a requirement and a value off the scale refused with 422, a member's 403 on the scheme, a missing matrix cell, a value in use (409 `risk_scale_held`) and a risk type turned back (409 `type_role_held`), revisions and their diff, the query fields, Go and SQL agreeing on every level, a rating moving and copying with its risk, and the rating guards through SQL. `risk_mitigations_test.go` covers a mitigation claimed, in effect once verified and suspect after a change, the FMEA table narrowed by query and cell, the matrix on both sides, the workbook with its colours, a link type that may count as mitigation, the mitigation triggers through SQL and a hundred risks read in good time. `risk_reporting_test.go` covers baselines, the graph and chains marks, the report as JSON and Word, 404 outside the project, 409 `risk_scheme_missing` and both templates. `risk/risk_test.go` unit tests `CheckScheme` and the level rules. In the browser, `risks.spec.ts` starts the five by five scheme, sets one cell, rates a hazard and compares revisions. `risk-matrix.spec.ts` sees a risk move cells once its mitigation is verified, and `risk-report.spec.ts` opens the print view of a template's project. `risks.test.tsx`, `fmea.test.tsx` and `report.test.tsx` cover the rating fields, starting and saving the scheme, a held value, the mitigations panel, rating in the table, the matrix and the report. What is missing is the archived project, turning detection off over the API, the FMEA table's paging and cell refusals, query narrowing of the matrix, the report and the downloads, the audit rows of a scheme and an export, a hidden mitigation, and the five MCP tools. In the browser nobody switches the method, rates detection, adds or removes a level or a value, rates in the table, turns the table's pages, switches the matrix's side or downloads anything. Only the hrefs of the downloads are checked.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/risk-scheme` on an archived project is 409 `project_archived` and `GET` returns the scheme unchanged. A save writes one `risk_scheme.saved` audit row naming the actor. No test asserts either today.
- [x] Turning detection off over the API: with a risk rated on detection, `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/risk-scheme` with `detection: false` is 409 `risk_scale_held` with "Risks are rated on detection...", and the rating keeps its detection. Today this is only tried through SQL in `TestRawSQLKeepsRatingsToRisks`.
- [x] `GET /projects/{projectKey}/risks`: `limit` and `offset` walk the rows with `total` unchanged and no risk repeated, and `limit` past `risk.MaxRows` is 422. `severity=0`, `severity=abc` and `probability=11` are 422 naming the field. Today only `side` and a bad query are refused.
- [x] A project with risks and no scheme: `GET /projects/{projectKey}/risks` and `GET /projects/{projectKey}/risk-matrix` answer every risk as unrated with no cells. `GET /projects/{projectKey}/risk-report.docx` and `.pdf` are 409 `risk_scheme_missing`. Today only the JSON report is tried without a scheme.
- [x] Query narrowing: `GET /projects/{projectKey}/risk-matrix?query=...` counts only the risks kept, and `GET /projects/{projectKey}/risk-report?query=...` lists only them with the level counts to match. `GET /projects/{projectKey}/risks.xlsx?query=...&severity=4&probability=3` holds only that cell's risks. Today only the table is narrowed.
- [x] Export audit: `risks.xlsx`, `risk-report.docx` and `risk-report.pdf` each write one `specification.exported` row with its format and the number of risks. Today no risk test reads the audit log.
- [x] A mitigation from a project the reader may not view: `GET /requirements/{reqKey}/mitigations` and `GET /projects/{projectKey}/risks` show its source as hidden with no key or title, and the risk's state still counts it. A person outside the project gets 404 from the mitigations of a risk. Today every mitigation is visible to the reader and only a requirement that is no risk is refused.
- [x] MCP: `list_risks`, `get_risk_scheme`, `get_risk_matrix`, `get_risk_mitigations` and `get_risk_report` through `/api/v1/mcp` answer what the HTTP calls answer. `get_risk_report` on a project without a scheme and `get_risk_mitigations` on a requirement that is no risk return `isError`. No test calls any of them today.

Database guards:
- [x] Through SQL, a member's `INSERT INTO risk_level`, `DELETE FROM risk_level`, `INSERT INTO risk_matrix_cell` and `INSERT INTO risk_scale_level` touch no row or are policy violations. The administrator of an archived project changing `risk_scheme`, `risk_level` or `risk_matrix_cell` is refused by `risk_scheme_keeper`. Today only a member's scheme update and scale delete are tried.
- [x] A mitigation whose ends change role: an unrated risk with a `mitigates` link moved by `UPDATE requirement SET type_id` to a type of requirements, and the mitigating requirement moved to a type of risks. `trace_link_mitigates_risk` only fires on the link, so decide whether the database refuses these, add the guard if it should, and try both through SQL.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] Project settings, Risks tab: set "A rating gives its level by" to the priority number, tick "Rate detection too", give detection its values, set "<level> from priority number" for each level and "Save" (`save-risk-scheme`). A rated hazard's level in the FMEA table changes to what the priority number gives. Today only the matrix is saved.
- [x] Risks tab: "Add a level" (`add-risk-level`), name it, pick its colour, tick "<name> is acceptable", give it cells and save. A risk in such a cell shows the new level. "Remove the level <name>" takes it out of the matrix. "Add a value to severity" adds a row, and "Remove the highest value of severity" is disabled while a rating uses that value. No scenario does any of this today.
- [x] FMEA table: rate a risk in place through its comboboxes. The row's level tag changes and the risk's history gains a revision. With more risks than one page, "Next" and "Previous" turn the pages. A query narrows the rows, and "Export as Excel" (`export-risks`) then carries the query. Today the table is only read.
- [x] Matrix: "Before mitigation" and "As they stand" move a mitigated risk between its two cells without a reload, and a query narrows the counts. Today only the effective side is read, after a reload.
- [x] Downloads: "Export as Excel" saves a workbook holding the risk, "Report as Word" (`risk-report-docx`) a document holding it, and "Report as PDF" (`risk-report-pdf`) a file starting `%PDF-`. With a query, `/print/risks/$projectKey?query=...` lists only the risks it keeps. Today only the hrefs are checked and the print view is opened unfiltered.

Component (vitest):
- [x] RiskSchemeCard: switching to the priority number shows a threshold field per level and hides the matrix. "Rate detection too" adds the detection scale. Removing a level re-maps its cells. A 422 on `levels[1].name` or `matrix` shows beside its field. Today only starting, saving and a held value are tested.
- [x] RiskMatrixView: the side switch asks for `side=before` and closes an open cell, and a query that does not parse shows its error. RisksPage: the table's paging asks for the next `offset`. None of these is tested today.

Go unit:
- [x] `risk`: table tests for `stateOf`, `viewOf` (no scheme, mitigated without an after level falls back to before, claimed keeps before) and `risky.effective` and `on`. Only `CheckScheme`, `Level` and `RPN` are unit tested today.
- [x] `csvio.RisksSheet` and `docx.RiskReportBytesWith`: a unit test each for an unrated risk, a hidden mitigation and a level colour, so the formats are checked without a stack. Neither has a unit test today.

## Done when
- Every risk operation has an integration test for the archived project or a missing scheme, for each query parameter it refuses, and for query narrowing.
- Every control on the Risks settings tab, the FMEA table, the matrix and the three downloads is reached by a browser scenario that checks its effect.
- The five risk MCP tools answer as their HTTP calls do.
- The mitigation invariant holds through SQL when either end of the link changes its type.
