issues.title: Test the Armature integration's refusals, sign-in exchange and browser paths
issues.body:
The Armature integration is among the best tested parts of Exciter. `armature_test.go` walks the connection and each person's token with their refusals, an unreachable Armature and a revoked token. `armature_links_test.go` covers lookup, search, linking with its 409 and 422 codes, the worker's remote links, outbox retries, suspect links and trash. `armature_create_test.go` refuses every bad round before and after Armature is asked. `armature_webhook_test.go` covers signatures, envelope versions, the size limit, transitions, moves, deletions and detached links. `armature_capabilities_test.go`, `armature_theme_test.go` and `token_exchange_test.go` cover what an older Armature lacks, theme following and connecting at sign-in. `armature_rls_test.go` and `armature_links_rls_test.go` try the walls through SQL, and the stub's `contract_test.go` holds every route and the token exchange to Armature's document. In the browser, `armature.spec.ts`, `armature-links.spec.ts`, `armature-create.spec.ts`, `armature-webhooks.spec.ts`, `armature-theme.spec.ts` and `connect-at-sign-in.spec.ts` cover the happy paths, and ArmatureLinks, Armature, CreateIssues and FollowArmatureTheme have vitest suites. What is missing is the refusals to a person who may read but not edit, since only people without a token are tried over the API. Archived projects, the API's bounds and the session-only rule are never tried either. On the sign-in exchange, the failure sentences other than a wrong secret are untried, and so are a slow Armature and two renewals at once. Through SQL, nobody tries clearing a link, the sync records' updates or a deactivated person's token. In the browser, nobody confirms a suspect Armature trace, follows a chip's connect hint, leaves a requirement out of a round, watches a round partly fail or copies the webhook address. IssueChip, chipState and IssuePicker have no tests of their own.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these writes were never answered 403: `DELETE /armature-links/{linkID}`, `POST /armature-links/{linkID}/clear`, `PUT /armature/account/token`, `PUT /armature/theme`, `POST /armature/webhook`, `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/armature-links`; these were never answered 422: `DELETE /armature-links/{linkID}`, `POST /armature/account/check`, `DELETE /armature/account/token`, `DELETE /armature/connection`, `DELETE /armature/theme`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #410: `POST /armature/webhook` is vouched for by its signature alone, so its refusal is 401; a malformed link id is 400 `bad_request` as every path id is; the check and the three DELETEs take no input, so none has a 422.)
- [x] A viewer who holds an Armature token: `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/armature-links`, `DELETE /armature-links/{linkID}` and `POST /armature-links/{linkID}/clear` are 403 `forbidden`, and the links, `armature_remote_link` rows and `trace_link_clearance` rows are unchanged. Today the API is only refused to people without a token (409 `armature_not_connected`), and the viewer's refusal is only tried through SQL in `armature_links_rls_test.go`.
- [x] Archived project: `POST /armature-links/{linkID}/clear` is 409 `project_archived`, and creating and removing a link are refused. A link of a trashed requirement cannot be cleared. Nothing in `armature_links_test.go` archives the project. (decided in #410: creating and removing answered 403 `forbidden`, and now answer 409 `project_archived` as confirming does.)
- [x] Bounds: `GET /armature/issues` with 51 distinct keys is 422 naming `key` (`armature.MaxLookupKeys`). `GET /armature/search` with a `q` of 201 characters is 422 naming `q`, and `limit=abc` is 422 naming `limit`. Today only a key of the wrong shape, a blank search and `limit=21` are tried.
- [x] `PUT /armature/account/token` called with a personal access token instead of a session is 403 `session_only`, and no Armature token is stored. The Stator twin is tested in `stator_test.go:224`, Armature's is not.
- [x] `PUT /armature/connection` client fields: a `clientId` of 256 characters is 422 naming `clientId`. `"clientSecret": ""` removes the secret, so `clientSecretSet` is false and the next sign-in's account sentence reads "Exciter has no client id and secret for Armature yet". The audit entry records `clientSecret` as `set` or `removed` and never the secret. Today `token_exchange_test.go` only sets both and tries a wrong secret.
- [x] Sign-in exchange sentences not tried for Armature: an Armature that drops `oauth.token-exchange@1` from `/meta` (tried only for Stator). An exchanged token whose `/auth/me` names another organization, which gets the "another organization than the one connected" sentence and stores no row. An Armature slower than `tokenexchange.SignInTimeout`: the sign-in still succeeds within about three seconds, and `GET /armature/account` then carries the "did not answer when you signed in" sentence (see the separate report on the timed out context). (decided in #410: since #348 the slow sentence reads "did not answer within 3 seconds when you signed in".)
- [x] Two reads at once while alice's exchanged grant is due (`accessTtlSeconds` short): the stub's `/oauth-grants` shows exactly one more refresh, and the grant is still standing afterwards. Today the test only checks `refreshes >= 1`, and a rotated refresh token sent twice would end the grant without failing it.
- [x] A refresh refused without ending the grant (change the app's secret at the stub to get `invalid_client`) marks the row `rejected`, and the account says so. Count how often the next reads send the refresh again: today `Viewer` renews a rejected grant from a sign-in on every read (see the separate report). An app the stub allows only `read` gives an account with `readOnly` true, and its `POST .../armature-links` is 409 `armature_rejected`. (decided in #410: #349 already makes the next reads wait; the test counts by `refresh_failed_at`.)
- [x] `POST /armature/webhook`: a correctly signed body that is no envelope (`[]`, `{"hello":1}`) answers 204 and changes no link. An `issue.updated` with `movedFrom` onto a key the requirement is already linked to with the same relation leaves one link and one `armature_remote_link` row (the first step of `rekeyLinks`). Today the move is only tried without such a collision.
- [x] Development panel (`armature.Service.Commits`): a reader without an Armature token, and a reader whose Armature cannot see CP-1, get results with no `armature` field. A broken or detached link's issue is not asked. Only the happy path is tried, in `test_results_test.go` `TestAResultLinksToItsCommitInArmature`.
- [x] MCP: `link_armature_issue` and `create_armature_issue` for an assistant whose person holds no Armature token answer `isError` with the sentence naming Your account, Armature account. Through a `read` scoped assistant token both are refused and no link is made. Today `mcp_review_test.go` only walks the happy path.

Database guards:
- [x] As exciter_app: `SELECT armature_issue_link_clear(...)` by a viewer and by a guest is refused. So is clearing against a revision the requirement never had, a direct `INSERT INTO trace_link_clearance (armature_link_id, ...)`, and an `UPDATE` of a stored clearance. The Stator twins are in `stator_links_rls_test.go:60-91`; `armature_links_rls_test.go` tries none of them.
- [x] As an editor: `UPDATE armature_remote_link SET state = ...` and `DELETE FROM armature_remote_link` are refused (only the `INSERT` is tried). An `armature.links` outbox event in the owner's name is refused (`outbox_event_own_acts`), as `stator_links_rls_test.go:151` already checks for Stator.
- [x] Switching a person off (`app_user.role` to NULL, trigger `app_user_left`) deletes their `armature_token` row, both a pasted one and one from a sign-in. `armature_token_held_by_a_member` refuses a row for somebody without a role. No test checks either. (decided in #410: the role going to NULL is tested; switching off through `DELETE /users/{id}` only sets `is_active` and keeps the tokens, which is #408.)

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] Suspect Armature trace: alice revises a requirement traced to CP-1. "Check the trace to CP-1" (`check-armature-link`) opens "Check the trace of KEY-R1 to CP-1", she fills "Why the link still holds", and "Confirm link" removes "Suspect". Only Stator's twin is in `stator-links.spec.ts`, and Armature's is only in vitest.
- [x] bob holds no Armature token and opens a traced requirement. The chip shows the key and the stored status, and "Connect your Armature account to see this issue" (`connect-armature-hint`) takes him to `/settings/armature-account`. After pasting a token the chip shows the summary and status live.
- [x] Trace form: after picking an issue, "Pick another" (`pick-another-issue`) brings the picker back. Typing a key of an issue alice may not see gets Armature's refusal by the field and makes no link. (decided in #410: the picker never offers an issue alice may not see, so there is no refusal by the field to reach; the test asserts the picker's sentence and that no link is made.)
- [x] Create Armature issues: "Leave out KEY-R2" in the dialog makes only one issue. A round whose second summary the stub refuses (`/refused-summary`) shows "1 of 2 issues were made." with the refusal. "Clear the selection" (`clear-selection`) empties the bar. Today only the happy path is in `armature-create.spec.ts`.
- [x] `/settings/armature`: "Copy address" (`copy-webhook-url`) puts the webhook address on the clipboard. "Forget the stored secret" and "Save" makes the stub's next signed delivery 401, so the panel stops following transitions.

Component (vitest):
- [x] `chipState` and IssueChip: `not_configured`, `not_connected` and `rejected` give connect, `unreachable` and `outdated` give their sentences, a key not yet answered gives loading and a `null` gives "Not available to you in Armature". "Moved in Armature since" shows only with a stored category and `stale`. Only the outdated and connect states are reached, through ArmatureLinks.test.tsx.
- [x] IssuePicker: ArrowDown and ArrowUp move the active option, Enter picks without submitting the trace form, Escape closes the list, and fast typing sends one search after the debounce. No test file exists, and only the stator e2e presses Escape.

Go unit:
- [x] `tokenexchange.Exchange`: an answer whose `token_type` is not Bearer, a 302, and an answer longer than 64 KiB all give `ErrUnreachable`. `Why` with `unauthorized_client` and no description reads "it gave no reason." `TestAnswersAreToldApart` covers neither of these.
- [x] `armature.NormalizeKey` agrees with the database's `issue_key` CHECK: ` cp-12 ` becomes CP-12, while CP-0, an 11 character project key and a 19 digit number are refused. `cmd/suite-seed`: with httptest fakes, a second run of `webhook`, `partnerApp` and `freshToken` gives new secrets and makes no second endpoint, app or token, as the command's doc comment promises. `isConflict` is true for 409 only. Neither has a test today.

## Done when
- Every Armature operation that writes has an integration test for a viewer's 403, an archived project's refusal and its bounds, and each checks the rows are unchanged.
- Every sentence the sign-in exchange can store for Armature is produced by a test, including a slow Armature and two renewals at once.
- Every control in `features/armature` is reached by a browser scenario or a vitest that checks its effect.

issues.title: Test the Stator integration's refusals, webhooks and the suite smoke
issues.body:
The Stator integration has broad coverage. `stator_test.go` walks the connection and each person's token with their refusals, the session-only rule, a Stator that does not answer and what Stator offers. `stator_links_test.go` covers lookup, search, linking with its 409 and 422 codes, suspect links cleared against a page version, and every webhook topic with replays, older versions, both envelope versions and bad signatures. `stator_remote_links_test.go` covers the worker's remote links with retries, refusals, links taken off in Stator, trash and the catch-up once Stator takes remote links. `token_exchange_test.go` connects alice to Stator at sign-in and forgets an ended grant. `stator_rls_test.go` and `stator_links_rls_test.go` try the walls, clearing and the sync records through SQL, `render_token_rls_test.go` keeps a print's token brief, and the stub's `contract_test.go` holds its routes to Stator's document. In the browser, `stator.spec.ts`, `stator-links.spec.ts`, `connect-at-sign-in.spec.ts` and the suite's `e2e/suite/smoke.spec.ts` cover connecting, linking, confirming, the matrix and a link taken off in Stator, and StatorLinks and Stator have vitest suites. What is missing is the refusals to a person who may read but not edit, archived projects and the API's bounds. The Stator webhook's size limit and a late publish from another space are untried, and so are the remote link sentences other than a reader's 403. The sign-in exchange is only tried when Stator answers. The stub's token endpoint is outside its contract test, and `exchangestub` has no tests of its own. In the browser, nobody sees a page deleted or moved in Stator or follows a chip's connect hint. The suite smoke never sees a Stator change reach Exciter, because the suite seed never points Stator's webhooks at Exciter, and its Stator part passes with only an annotation when the exchange is not offered. Exciter has no embed in Stator; the nearest thing is the print token adapted from Stator's, which is only tried through SQL and by the PDF scenario.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these writes were never answered 403: `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/stator-links`, `DELETE /stator-links/{linkID}`, `POST /stator-links/{linkID}/clear`, `POST /stator/webhook`; these were never answered 422: `DELETE /stator-links/{linkID}`, `POST /stator/account/check`, `DELETE /stator/account/token`, `DELETE /stator/connection`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #411: the webhook has no permission to refuse and answers 401 `bad_signature`; account check, token removal and connection removal take no input to refuse; a malformed link id is 400 `bad_request`, as every path id is)
- [x] A viewer who holds a Stator token: `POST /requirements/{reqKey}/stator-links`, `DELETE /stator-links/{linkID}` and `POST /stator-links/{linkID}/clear` are 403 `forbidden`, and the links, `stator_remote_link` rows and clearances are unchanged. Today the API is only refused to carol without a token (409 `stator_not_connected`), and the viewer's refusal is only tried through SQL.
- [x] Archived project: `POST /stator-links/{linkID}/clear` is 409 `project_archived` (`stator/links.go:249`), and creating and removing a link are refused. A link of a trashed requirement cannot be cleared. Nothing in `stator_links_test.go` archives the project. (decided in #411: creating and removing a link in an archived project stay 403 `forbidden`, as Armature's twin and the database answer; clearing is 409 `project_archived`)
- [x] Bounds: `GET /stator/pages` with 51 distinct ids is 422 naming `id` (`stator.MaxLookupPages`). `GET /stator/search` with a `q` of 201 characters is 422 naming `q`, and `limit=abc` is 422 naming `limit`. Today only an id that is none, a blank search and `limit=21` are tried.
- [x] `POST /stator/webhook`: a body over `stator.WebhookMaxBytes` is 413 `too_large`, as Armature's is in `armature_webhook_test.go:199`. A correctly signed body that is no envelope answers 204 and changes nothing. A `page.moved` whose space key is longer than 100 characters leaves the link as it was.
- [x] A late `page.published` of an older version from the page's former space, after a `page.moved`, leaves `spaceKey` and `url` at the new space. Today "an older version late" is sent with the same space, so it cannot catch that `notePublished` moves the link before checking the version (see the separate report). (fixed in #411: a move now keeps its version and a publish moves a link only when newer)
- [x] Remote link refusals: dave's link with a `read` scoped Stator token fails with "Stator token may only read" (`sync_run.go:107`). A page Stator answers 404 for fails with "Stator has no page with this id". Both end "The next change to the requirement tries again." Today only the reader's 403 ("did not let") is tried.
- [x] Sign-in exchange towards Stator: a wrong client secret stores the `invalid_client` sentence naming Stator, and leaves Armature's outcome alone. A Stator slower than `tokenexchange.SignInTimeout` lets the sign-in succeed within about three seconds and stores the "did not answer" sentence. Two reads at once while the grant is due cause one refresh at the stub. Today `token_exchange_test.go` tries the wrong secret for Armature only, and never tries a slow partner or renewals at once. `stator/exchange.go` is its own copy of the code.
- [x] Moving `PUT /stator/connection` to another address forgets a grant from a sign-in as well as a pasted token, and `DELETE /stator/account/token` removes one. The next sign-in then connects alice again. Today only bob's pasted token is moved away, in `stator_test.go:234`.
- [x] MCP: `search_stator_pages` and `link_stator_page` for an assistant whose person holds no Stator token answer `isError` naming Your account, Stator account. `clear_stator_link` on a suspect link clears it and answers the link (only its refusal is tried in `mcp_review_test.go`). (decided in #411: `search_stator_pages` answers `status: not_connected` with no pages, as its route and `search_armature_issues` do; `link_stator_page` is `isError` with the sentence)
- [x] Print tokens (`auth.MintRenderToken`): while a print runs, `GET /tokens` does not list its token. A request made with it that writes is 403. It stops working when its owner is switched off. Today `documents_test.go` only checks that none is left after the print.

Database guards:
- [x] As exciter_app: inserting a `stator_page_link` whose `url` is `javascript:alert(1)` is refused by its CHECK. An editor's `UPDATE stator_page_link SET url = ..., space_key = ...` is refused. Also decide whether a `url` outside the connection's address should be refused, and try it. None of these is tried in `stator_links_rls_test.go`. (decided in #411: a `url` outside the connection's address is now refused, by `01518_stator_link_address.sql`)
- [x] `stator_token_needs_a_connection`: storing one's own `stator_token` while no `stator_connection` exists is refused through SQL. Switching a person off (`app_user_left`) deletes their `stator_token` rows, pasted and from a sign-in. `stator_rls_test.go` tries neither.

Browser (e2e scenario):

issues.title: Test outbound webhooks through retries, redelivery and the settings page
issues.body:
The webhook settings and the worker's delivery are tested well in the Go suite. `webhooks_test.go` covers the secret shown once and sealed, a signed ping, version 1 and version 2 envelopes, rotation, ownership by saving, field refusals, a 403 to a member for all eight operations, and the log deleted with its webhook. `webhook_events_test.go` covers every topic but one reaching its receiver as the owner may read it, scoping by project, a redelivery of the same event, the first retry's wait, turning off after a day of failures, withholding, the guard against private addresses and the policies through SQL. `outbox_test.go` covers the outbox and `netguard_test.go` covers redirects and the allow list. In the browser, `webhooks.spec.ts` adds a webhook, copies its secret by reading the field, checks a signed revision in both envelopes, sends a ping, opens the log and turns the webhook off. `webhooks.test.tsx` covers the list, the add form, the log, rotate and delete. What is missing is the end of the retry chain, `requirement.moved`, cancelling what is pending, pruning the log, the failure sentences other than a 503 and a blocked host, the audit rows for a save and a rotation, and refusing a delivery that belongs to another webhook. In the browser, nobody clicks "Send again", "Copy secret", "Rotate the secret", "Delete" or "Turn on", and nobody sees a failing webhook.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these were never answered 422: `DELETE /webhooks/{webhookID}`, `POST /webhooks/{webhookID}/deliveries/{deliveryID}/redeliver`, `POST /webhooks/{webhookID}/rotate-secret`, `POST /webhooks/{webhookID}/test`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #415: these four take no body, so nothing is a 422; an id that is none is 400 `bad_request` and a token held to some projects 403 `projects_token`, with nothing changed)
- [x] `requirement.moved`: move a requirement in a project a `*` webhook listens to and assert one delivery with the new parent in its payload, in version 1 and version 2. Today `TestRequirementEventsReachTheReceiverAsTheOwnerMayReadThem` skips this topic in its loop over `webhook.Topics`. (decided in #415: the payload carries no parent, so the new project, key and URL are asserted; the project the requirement left now hears the move too, fixed in #415)
- [x] Retry chain to the end: a receiver answering 503 to every attempt. Move each `next_attempt_at` to now and assert that attempts 2 to `webhook.MaxAttempts` come with waits of `Backoff[1..4]`, and that after attempt 6 the delivery stays `failed` with no `pending` row left. Today only the first wait (`Backoff[0]`) is checked, in `TestAFailingReceiverIsRetriedThenTurnedOff`. (decided in #415: the five retries wait `Backoff[0]` to `Backoff[4]`)
- [x] Turned off with a retry pending: while attempt 2 is `pending`, `PATCH /webhooks/{webhookID}` with `enabled: false`. Then assert that the worker records it as `cancelled` with "The webhook was turned off before this was sent." and nothing reaches the bin. When the worker turns an endpoint off (`countFailure`), assert that pending rows that were not sent by hand become `cancelled` and a manual one does not. Today the test only checks that no new delivery is queued after the webhook is off.
- [x] Topic filter: a webhook on `requirement.revised` alone gets no delivery row for a comment, a link or a baseline in its project. Today only the project filter is checked for absence (`otherBin`).
- [x] `POST /webhooks/{webhookID}/deliveries/{deliveryID}/redeliver` with a delivery that belongs to another webhook answers 404 `not_found`, and neither webhook's log grows. Today only a random delivery id is tried.
- [x] Redelivery while a retry waits: attempt 1 `failed` and attempt 2 `pending`. "Send again" on attempt 1 takes attempt 3. Then attempt 2 fails as well, and the test asserts that an automatic attempt is still queued after it. Today the retry is lost to the `ON CONFLICT (endpoint_id, event_id, attempt) DO NOTHING` in `record` (see the separate report). (decided in #415: #346 had already fixed the lost retry; the test now asserts attempt 3 by hand and the automatic attempt 4)
- [x] `Prune`: plant a `delivered`, a `failed` and a `pending` row with `created_at` older than `webhook.DeliveryRetention`. After `Service.Prune`, only the pending row is left and the answer says 2. No test calls `Prune` today.
- [x] Failure sentences: a receiver that never answers within the send timeout is `failed` with "The receiver did not answer in time." A host that does not resolve is `failed` with "The receiver could not be reached." Both count a failure and queue a retry. Today only a 503 and a blocked host are asserted.
- [x] A sealed secret that no longer opens: overwrite `secret_sealed` with the secret of another endpoint through the superuser. The next attempt is `failed` with "Rotate the secret and give the receiver the new one." and nothing is posted. Today only the box is unit tested (`TestASealedSecretOpensOnlyForItsEndpoint`).
- [x] A delivery planted with `version` 99 is `failed` with the "does not send" sentence. `failures` on the endpoint is unchanged and no retry is queued, as `send` promises for `ErrUnknownVersion`.
- [x] A receiver that answers 307 to `http://10.0.0.1/` is `failed` with the blocked sentence (`whyBlocked`) on the delivery, and its error names no inner host or port. Today the redirect check is only tried on the bare client, in `netguard_test.go`.
- [x] Two `SendDue` passes run side by side over 50 due deliveries: each delivery reaches the bin exactly once. Today only the outbox events have this check, in `TestTwoWorkersNeverHandleOneEvent`.
- [x] Audit: `PATCH /webhooks/{webhookID}` writes one `webhook.updated` row and `POST /webhooks/{webhookID}/rotate-secret` writes one `webhook.secret_rotated` row. Neither row holds the secret or the address's path. Today only `webhook.created`, `webhook.deleted` and `webhook.disabled` are read back.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] Delivery log: let a revision fail against a bin that answers 503. "Send again" (`data-action="redeliver"`) on that row, once the bin answers 204, adds a delivered attempt. The bin then holds the same event id twice, under two delivery ids. Today the e2e never clicks `redeliver`.
- [x] "Rotate the secret" (`webhook-rotate`) after the confirm shows the new secret once. "Copy secret" (`copy-webhook-secret`) puts it on the clipboard (read it with `navigator.clipboard.readText` under a granted permission). The next ping verifies with the new secret and not with the old one. Today the secret is read from the field and rotation is never clicked.
- [x] A webhook the worker turned off shows "Turned off: failing" with its hint. "Turn on" (`webhook-toggle`) clears it, and the next revision is delivered. "Delete" (`webhook-delete`) after the confirm removes the row and its log. Today only "Turn off" is clicked, and deletion is done through the API in `cleanUp`.

Component (vitest):
- [x] Copy secret: a resolved `navigator.clipboard.writeText` gets the secret, and a rejected one shows "Copying did not work. Select the secret and copy it yourself." Turning the confirm down on "Rotate the secret" or "Delete" sends nothing. Today `webhooks.test.tsx` stubs the confirm to true and never copies.

Go unit:
- [x] `netguard.Reserved`: decide on and assert `192.0.0.0/24`, `198.18.0.0/15`, `64:ff9b::/96` with an embedded private IPv4 address, and `2002::/16` (6to4). Also assert that `Transport` refuses an inner address when `HTTPS_PROXY` is set (see the separate report). `why` maps `netguard.ErrBlocked`, a deadline and any other error to its sentence. Today none of these are tried. (decided in #415: kept as #339 made them, already asserted; the proxy from the environment is checked in a child process)

## Done when
- Every delivery state (`delivered`, `failed`, `withheld`, `cancelled`, `pending`) and every failure sentence in `deliver.go` is reached by an integration test that reads the log row.
- The retry chain is followed to `MaxAttempts`, and the log is pruned under test.
- Every control on `/settings/webhooks`, including "Send again", "Copy secret", "Rotate the secret", "Turn on" and "Delete", is clicked by a browser scenario that checks what the receiver or the log shows.

issues.title: Call every MCP tool and test the rest of OAuth and tokens
issues.body:
Tokens and OAuth are among the best tested parts of the API. `tokens_test.go` and `token_rls_test.go` cover making, scoping, read-only, project limits, revoking by the owner and by an administrator, and expiry. `oauth_test.go` covers the metadata, the 401 challenge, every authorize refusal the RFCs name, PKCE, a code or refresh token used twice ending its grant, revocation and confidential clients. `oauth_grants_test.go`, `oauth_narrow_test.go`, `oauth_apps_test.go` and `oauth_exchange_test.go` cover reading and project grants, narrowed tokens, connected apps ended by their person or an administrator, and partner apps with their policies. `mcp_test.go`, `mcp_resources_test.go` and `mcp_review_test.go` drive the protocol's own Go client, check every answer against the tool's output schema, and cover resources and prompts. In the browser, `oauth.spec.ts` allows, denies and disconnects an app, `tokens.spec.ts` makes and revokes a read-only token, and `partner-apps.spec.ts` registers and removes a partner. What is missing is breadth on MCP: 42 tools are named by no integration test or e2e spec (`mcp-never-called.txt`), and `write_requirements` is only tried without its argument. On OAuth, nobody tests an expired code or access token, a consent answered twice, a refresh or revocation by another client, a second consent replacing the first grant's tokens, or the sweeper. Partner apps are refused to a member only for list and create. In the browser, nobody opens `/settings/all-connected-apps` or revokes on `/settings/all-tokens`, nobody copies a token or a partner secret, and nobody rotates a partner secret.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these writes were never answered 403: `DELETE /oauth/clients/{clientID}`, `PATCH /oauth/clients/{clientID}`, `POST /oauth/clients/{clientID}/rotate-secret`, `POST /oauth/register`, `POST /oauth/requests/{requestID}`, `POST /oauth/revoke`, `POST /oauth/token`, `DELETE /tokens/{tokenID}`; these were never answered 422: `POST /mcp`, `DELETE /oauth/clients/{clientID}`, `PATCH /oauth/clients/{clientID}`, `POST /oauth/clients/{clientID}/rotate-secret`, `DELETE /oauth/grants/everyone/{grantID}`, `DELETE /oauth/grants/{grantID}`, `POST /oauth/register`, `POST /oauth/revoke`, `POST /oauth/token`, `DELETE /tokens/everyone/{tokenID}`, `DELETE /tokens/{tokenID}`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #426: the RFC endpoints answer 400, 401 or 429 in the RFCs' shape and never 403 or 422; routes without input answer a malformed id 400 and an unknown one 404; `POST /mcp` refuses a malformed body 400 and a tool's refusal is `isError` in a 200)
- [x] MCP, test executions: one assistant scenario calls `start_test_execution`, `list_test_executions`, `list_my_test_executions`, `get_test_execution`, `get_test_execution_case`, `record_test_result`, `file_test_failure_issue` (against the Armature stub), `close_test_execution`, `list_test_plans`, `get_test_plan` and `get_test_case_results` through `connectAssistant` and `callTool`, so each answer is held to its output schema. Assert that the result recorded is what `GET /test-executions/{executionID}/cases/{reqKey}` answers. A read-only token gets `isError` from `record_test_result` with "can only read". No test calls any of these tools today.
- [x] MCP, evidence and trace: `get_test_results`, `get_code_links`, `run_trace_check` and `get_trace_graph` on a requirement with an uploaded result and a code tag answer what the HTTP calls answer. A token limited to another project gets `isError` for each. None is called today.
- [x] MCP, risks: `list_risks`, `get_risk_scheme`, `get_risk_matrix`, `get_risk_report` and `get_risk_mitigations` on a project with one risk mitigated by a requirement. Assert the counts in the matrix cell and the mitigation's key. None is called today.
- [x] MCP, history and workflow: `list_revisions`, `get_revision` (revision 1 after an update), `diff_revisions` between 1 and 2, `list_transitions` and `transition_requirement` with a stale `baseRevision`. The stale call is `isError` and names the revision, and a fresh one moves the status. Only the bulk `transition_requirements` is called today. (decided in #426: a transition takes no `baseRevision`; a call carrying one is refused naming `baseRevision` as a field it does not take, and nothing moves)
- [x] MCP, reading a project: `get_project`, `get_tree`, `list_requirements` with a filter, `search_requirements`, `list_links`, `list_comments`, `list_terms`, `list_people`, `list_dashboards` and `get_dashboard_widget` each answer within their schema and agree with the HTTP call. A token limited to another project gets `isError` from `get_project` and `get_tree`. None is called today.
- [x] MCP, quality and reviews: `check_requirement_text` on a vague sentence returns a finding, `get_quality_findings` and `get_similar_requirements` on a near duplicate return it, and `get_review_session` and `list_review_sessions` list a session made over HTTP. None is called today.
- [x] MCP, installation: `server_info` answers the version that `GET /meta` answers. `list_audit_log` as an administrator's token lists a row the test just caused, and as a member's token is `isError` naming the permission. A token limited to projects is not offered `list_audit_log` at all, since it is org-wide. Neither tool is called today.
- [x] MCP prompt `write_requirements` with `projectKey` and `source` returns messages that embed the source text and name `create_requirement`. Today only the missing `source` refusal is tried, in `mcp_resources_test.go`.
- [x] `POST /oauth/requests/{requestID}` answered twice: the second answer is 404 and leaves one grant and one `oauth.granted` row. A request past `RequestTTL` (moved back through the superuser) is 404 on both GET and POST. Today the e2e opens only an unknown request id.
- [x] Deny over the API: `POST /oauth/requests/{requestID}` with `allow: false` sends the client back with `access_denied`, `state` and `iss`. No `oauth_grant`, `oauth_code` or audit row is written, and the request is gone. Today only the browser checks the redirect.
- [x] A code past `CodeTTL` (moved back through the superuser) is refused with `invalid_grant`. An access token past `AccessTTL` gets 401 with `error="invalid_token"` at `/api/v1/mcp`. Today neither expiry is tried.
- [x] Refresh and revocation by another client: client B sends client A's refresh token to `/oauth/token` and is refused with `invalid_grant`. Client A's grant must still refresh afterwards, so check that the refusal does not end it as a reuse would. Client B posting A's access token to `/oauth/revoke` answers 200, and A's token still works. Today revocation is tried only by the owning client and an unknown one.
- [x] Consent again for the same client: the first grant's access and refresh tokens stop (`Decide` deletes the old grant), and `GET /oauth/grants` lists one grant. Today a new consent is made in several subtests, but the old tokens are never tried afterwards.
- [x] Partner apps refused: a member's `PATCH /oauth/clients/{clientID}`, `POST /oauth/clients/{clientID}/rotate-secret` and `DELETE /oauth/clients/{clientID}` are 403 `forbidden`, and the app and its secret digest are unchanged. After a rotation the new secret authenticates at `/oauth/token`. Today only list and create are refused, and only the old secret's failure is checked.
- [x] `oauth.Sweeper.Once`: plant an expired request, code and access token, a grant left with no code and no refresh token, a registered client unused for longer than `UnusedClientTTL` and a partner with no grant. After one sweep, all are gone except the partner and a live grant. No test runs the sweeper today.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] `/settings/all-connected-apps`: bob connects an app through consent. Alice opens the page from settings, "Disconnect <app> of Bob" (`data-action="end-app"`) after the confirm removes the row, and bob's access token gets 401. The route is never visited today.
- [x] `/settings/all-tokens`: bob makes a token. Alice revokes it there with "Revoke <token> of Bob" (`revoke-token`), and bob's script gets 401. Today the page is only opened by the axe check in `a11y.spec.ts`.
- [x] Tokens page: "Copy token" (`copy-token`) puts the secret on the clipboard (read it back with a granted clipboard permission), and "Done" (`token-done`) hides it so a reload never shows it. Today the secret is read from the field.
- [x] Partner apps on `/settings/installation`: "Copy secret" (`copy-partner-secret`) copies it. "Give <app> a new secret" (`rotate-partner-secret`) after the confirm shows a new secret once. Then `/oauth/token` with the old secret answers `invalid_client`. Neither control is clicked today.
- [x] Consent narrowed to a project: tick one project, allow, trade the code, and `tools/call list_projects` with the token lists that project alone. Today the e2e narrows only to reading and never picks a project.

Component (vitest):
- [x] TokensPage and PartnerApps: "Copy" calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText` with the secret, and a rejected copy shows the "copy it yourself" sentence. Neither test file touches the clipboard today.

Go unit:
- [x] `oauth.HTTPFetcher` against an `httptest` server: a 302 is not followed and is refused, a 200 body of `MaxClientMetadataBytes`+1 is refused, and a 404 is refused with its status. Wrapped in `netguard.Client` with no allow list, a document on 127.0.0.1 is refused with `netguard.ErrBlocked`. Only `keepFor` is unit tested today (`service_test.go`), and the integration test uses a stub fetcher (`documents`).

## Done when
- Every tool in the MCP catalogue is called at least once by an integration test through the protocol's client, with its answer held to its output schema, and `mcp-never-called.txt` comes out empty.
- Every OAuth expiry (request, code, access token) and every cross-client refusal is tried, and the sweeper is run under test.
- Every control on `/settings/tokens`, `/settings/all-tokens`, `/settings/connected-apps`, `/settings/all-connected-apps` and the partner apps panel is clicked by a browser scenario that checks the effect on the API.

issues.title: Test projects, access, sign-on, join requests and the audit log in the browser and the database
issues.body:
The service and most database guards for this area are tested closely. `projects_test.go` and `project_rls_test.go` cover making, keys and their aliases, archiving and deleting. `permissions_test.go` and `permission_rls_test.go` cover grants, the inspector, adding up roles and the guest cap. `members_test.go` covers adding, re-roling and switching people off, and the guards on `app_user` through SQL, including the last active administrator and two administrators switching each other off. `group_roles_test.go`, `sso_settings_test.go`, `sso_test.go` and `sso_rls_test.go` cover the provider, group mapping and sign-in. `join_requests_test.go` covers admitting and declining with their policies, `audit_test.go` covers append-only, retention and every filter at the service level, and `demo_test.go` and `one_installation_test.go` cover the suite demo and renaming. Every component here has a vitest suite. What is missing: the tables `groups` and `group_member` have no policy that keeps them to administrators. Through SQL, a member can put themselves into a group that holds a project's admin role. A member is never refused `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/key`, `DELETE /projects/{projectKey}`, `DELETE /oidc-provider/group-roles/{groupRoleID}`, `DELETE /users/requests/{userID}` or `POST /installation/suite-demo/links`. In the browser, nobody saves the provider, maps or unmaps a group, lets somebody in or turns them away, copies a made password, switches OAuth off, links the demo again, discards or removes a grant, or filters the audit log by person, kind or date. A role change and a switch off are checked on the administrator's screen only, never on the other person's.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these writes were never answered 403: `POST /auth/logout`, `POST /installation/suite-demo/links`, `DELETE /oidc-provider/group-roles/{groupRoleID}`, `DELETE /projects/{projectKey}`, `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/key`, `DELETE /users/requests/{userID}`; these were never answered 422: `POST /auth/logout`, `PUT /installation/oauth-connections`, `POST /installation/suite-demo/links`, `DELETE /oidc-provider/group-roles/{groupRoleID}`, `DELETE /projects/{projectKey}`, `DELETE /projects/{projectKey}/archive`, `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/archive`, `DELETE /users/requests/{userID}`, `DELETE /users/{userID}`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #427: operations with no body have no input for a 422; a malformed id and a body that is not the one boolean are 400 `bad_request`, and logout has no permission to refuse, 401 without a session)
- [x] A project administrator by grant, a member given `admin` in `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/grants`, may `PATCH /projects/{projectKey}`, `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/key`, archive and replace the grants. An editor on the same project gets 403 `forbidden` for `PUT /projects/{projectKey}/key` and for `DELETE /projects/{projectKey}` of an archived project, and the project and its key are unchanged. Today every change is made by the installation's owner, and a member is refused only `PATCH`, archive and unarchive.
- [x] `DELETE /oidc-provider/group-roles/{groupRoleID}` by a member is 403 and the mapping stays. Posting the same group again with another role changes the one row in place (as the operation's summary says), and the next sign-in follows the new role. Today a member is refused only GET and POST, and no group is mapped twice.
- [x] `DELETE /users/requests/{userID}` by a member is 403 and the request stays. `POST /users/requests/{userID}/admit` with `role: "guest"` makes a guest who sees no project, and with `role: "wizard"` it is 422 with the person still waiting. Today a member is refused only list and admit, and only `member` and `owner` are tried. (decided in #427: admitting as `guest` is 422 on `role` like `wizard`, the person still waiting, as in Armature)
- [x] `PUT /oidc-provider` without `clientId` is 422 naming `clientId`, and `GET /oidc-provider` still answers the saved provider. Today only an issuer without a scheme is tried, in `sso_settings_test.go`.
- [x] `POST /installation/suite-demo/links` by a member is 403 and no demo job is queued. Today a member is refused only GET and POST of `/installation/suite-demo`.
- [x] `GET /audit` over HTTP with `target`, `targetType`, `from` and `to`, and walking with the cursor from one page to the next with no entry repeated. `GET /audit/export?action=member.role_changed` holds only those rows, and its `audit.exported` entry names the filter. Today the filters are tried through `audit.Service` in `TestTheAuditLogIsWalkedAndNarrowed`, and over HTTP only `actor` and bad values are tried.

Database guards:
- [x] `groups` and `group_member` keep to administrators: through SQL as `exciter_app`, a plain member's `INSERT INTO group_member (group_id, user_id)` for themselves, into a group granted `admin` on a project, is refused. Afterwards `perm_project_holds(project, member, 'administer')` is still false. `UPDATE groups SET name = ...` and `DELETE FROM groups` touch no row. Today the two tables have only the open `_installation` policy from `00410_policies_without_organization.sql` and no restrictive one. `sso_rls_test.go` reads them as an owner and never writes as a member, so this needs a policy as well as a test (see the separate report). Sign-in writes them with the admin role (`oidc/signin.go`), which the policy would not touch. (done in #336, `TestRawSQLKeepsGroupsToTheAdministrators`)
- [x] `installation` through SQL as a plain member: `UPDATE installation SET oauth_connections = false` and `UPDATE installation SET default_theme_id = NULL` touch no row, under `org_admins_change`. Today only `name` is tried, in `TestTheInstallationIsRenamedByAnAdministrator`.

Browser (e2e scenario):

issues.title: Test the shell, the settings area, home and the profile in the browser
issues.body:
The shell is tested closely in jsdom. `Shell.test.tsx` draws the rail and sidebar, counts unread notifications and waiting reviews, folds the sidebar and its groups and remembers both, swaps in the settings sidebar, walks the quick switcher's places from the keyboard and keeps the installation's settings from a member. `Accessibility.test.tsx` covers the skip link, the landmarks, the account menu from the keyboard and every way the phone drawer opens and closes, and `language.test.tsx` covers the language choice. In the browser, `menus.spec.ts` checks the avatar menu's entries for an administrator and a member, the settings sidebar's two groups, the Settings crumb, "Back to Exciter" from `/search`, the language on Your profile, the palette finding Your profile and the drawer at phone width. `switch-to.spec.ts` covers the other tools in the menu, `login.spec.ts` the password sign-in, a wrong password, the way back after sign-in and a session that ends, and `a11y.spec.ts` runs axe on part of `places.ts`. The backend side (`GET /auth/me`, `PATCH /auth/me`) is covered in `signin_test.go` and `tokens_test.go`. What is missing is the browser doing what jsdom can only pretend to: folding the sidebar and reloading, following the drawer's links, the way back keeping a query, and the palette reaching a settings page and the full search against the real server. `a11y.spec.ts` says it covers every place of `places.ts`, but it leaves out eleven of them. Home's empty state and its "New project" button have no test of their own, and nobody checks the sign-in page's `next` in a real browser.

## Gaps

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] `a11y.spec.ts` claims every place of `places.ts`, but its `PATHS` leave out `/notifications`, `/reviews`, `/settings`, `/settings/profile`, `/settings/notifications`, `/settings/watching`, `/settings/connected-apps`, `/settings/all-connected-apps`, `/settings/stator`, `/settings/stator-account` and `/settings/webhooks`. Build the list at run time from the links of the settings sidebar and the "Where you are" navigation, so a new place cannot be missed. Run each in light and dark. Today `/settings/profile` and `/settings` get axe only in light, from `menus.spec.ts`. (decided in #428: one test per sidebar group and palette walks the links it reads, each page a step)
- [x] Sidebar fold in a real browser: "Collapse the sidebar" (`data-action="sidebar"`) leaves only the rail (`[data-sidebar]` gone). Then reload: the rail is still alone. The rail's "Home", "Search" and "Projects" links, named by their tooltips, still lead to their pages. "Expand the sidebar" brings it back. Folding the "Requirements" group (`[data-sidebar-group="requirements"]`) survives a reload too. Today the button is only measured for its border radius in `themes.spec.ts`.
- [x] Counts in the sidebar against the real server: alice asks bob to review a requirement. Bob's "Reviews" entry then shows `[data-count="reviews"]` with 1, and the count goes once he decides. Bob's "Notifications" entry shows the unread count, which falls when he opens one. Only stubbed counts are checked today, in `Shell.test.tsx`.
- [x] Back from settings keeps the whole address: open `/search?q=brake&project=<KEY>`, open Settings from the avatar menu, go on to Members and then Themes, and press "Back to Exciter" (`back-from-settings`). The address is `/search?q=brake&project=<KEY>` again, with the same results. A new tab opened straight at `/settings/members` goes back to `/`. Today the way back is only tried from a bare `/search`.
- [x] Palette against the real server, as alice: Ctrl K, type "aud". "Audit log", with the hint "Settings", opens `/settings/audit`. Ctrl K again, type "brake pedal" and pick "Search everything for brake pedal". It lands on `/search?q=brake+pedal` with the hits shown. Escape closes the palette and gives focus back to the control that had it. Today only "your profile" and a requirement key are tried, in `menus.spec.ts` and `search.spec.ts`.
- [x] As bob, a member: Ctrl K, type "members". Only "Search everything for members" is offered (decided in #428: no place is offered; requirements of projects open to everyone may match the word too), and typing `/settings/members` into the address bar shows the page bob may not read, not the members. Today a member's palette is only checked in jsdom.
- [x] The drawer at phone width: "Projects" in the drawer closes it and lands on `/projects`. Opening it again, "Close the navigation" (`close-drawer`) closes it, and so does Escape. Each time focus returns to "Open the navigation" (`data-action="drawer"`). The theme button in the drawer's foot switches `html[data-theme]`. `/projects` and a requirement page do not scroll sideways. Today the drawer is only left by "Back to Exciter".
- [x] Your profile shows who is signed in: bob's `/settings/profile` shows his name (`[data-profile-name]`), his email and "Member", and alice's shows "Administrator". Today only the heading and the language are checked.
- [x] Sign-in keeps `next` inside the application: `/login?next=//evil.example/x` and `/login?next=https://evil.example/x`, then a password sign-in, land on `/` of the web origin. `/login?sso=inactive` shows "Your account has been switched off. Ask an administrator." A signed-in alice who opens `/login` is sent home. Today `safeNext` and the reasons are only tried in `LoginPage.test.tsx`.

Component (vitest):
- [x] HomeScreen: an administrator with no projects sees "No projects yet", "Make the first project to start writing requirements." and "New project" (`data-action="first-project"`), which opens `/projects/new`. A member with no projects sees "Nothing here yet. An administrator makes projects." and no button. A failed `GET /projects` shows the error banner, and its Retry asks again. With projects, "Your projects" lists them. No test file exists for HomeScreen today. Its empty state only appears in passing in `themes.test.tsx`.
- [x] QuickSwitcher: when `GET /search/quick` fails, "Quick search is not answering. Press Enter on the last option to try the full search." shows (`[data-quick-switcher-error]`). An answer that comes back for an earlier word is not offered after the word changed (decided in #428: it was offered while the newer answer loaded; fixed there). Picking "Search everything for X" with the mouse goes to `/search?q=X`, and a press on the scrim closes the palette. Today only places and the keyboard are tried.
- [x] ProfilePage: a refused `PATCH /auth/me` shows its error banner and keeps the previous language checked. The radios are disabled while the save is under way, and "Saved." is announced once it is done. Today only a successful choice is tried, in `language.test.tsx`.

## Done when

issues.title: Test the theme editor, theme sharing and the German interface end to end
issues.body:
The theme service is tested closely. `themes_test.go` covers the examples, the refusals on the way in, choosing, a private theme kept from others and a shared one kept from a member's changes, files kept in the bucket and served as downloads, an unsafe SVG and a file in use refused, the default for everyone and deleting a theme. `theme_portable_test.go` and `theme_exchange_test.go` cover export, import and the files travelling between the three tools, and `theme_rls_test.go` and `armature_theme_test.go` try every theme guard straight through SQL. On the client, `ThemeEditor.test.tsx`, `ThemeLoader.test.tsx`, `OrgDefaultTheme.test.tsx`, `themes.test.tsx` and `theme-css.test.ts` cover the editor's start, one colour and the preview, the loader's cache and the compiled CSS. `themes.spec.ts` checks the light and dark switch, a chosen theme applying with no flash, imports from Armature, Stator and Exciter itself, and the default reaching a member. For the language, `i18n.test.ts` keeps the German catalogue as complete as the English one and checks dates and numbers in both, and `menus.spec.ts` chooses Deutsch on Your profile.

What is missing is the theme editor in a real browser. Nobody makes, edits, shares, unshares, deletes or names a theme the default from the Themes page, and nobody uploads or removes a file in the editor. On the server, deleting the default theme, an administrator deleting somebody's shared theme, the file limits over HTTP and a chosen theme that is later unshared are never tried. For the language, no browser test runs with a German browser, no export is ever made for a German reader, and the lookups keyed by what the server sends are not checked against what it can send.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] Specific refusals the integration run never gave. In the access log of one full run of `-tags integration` (servers built with a discarding logger are not counted, so check each before writing it), these writes were never answered 403: `POST /themes`, `PUT /themes/active`, `POST /themes/import`, `DELETE /themes/{themeID}/assets/{assetID}`; these were never answered 422: `PUT /themes/active`, `DELETE /themes/{themeID}`, `POST /themes/{themeID}/assets`, `DELETE /themes/{themeID}/assets/{assetID}`. Where the operation has a permission or an input to refuse, add a test that expects the status and its code and checks that nothing changed. (decided in #429: the 403s come from a read-only token; the listed 422s have no input to refuse as invalid, so a bad id or body is 400 and something missing 404, and those are asserted)
- [x] Deleting the default theme: alice names a shared theme the default with `PUT /themes/default`, then its owner calls `DELETE /themes/{themeID}`. `GET /themes/default` answers null, `installation.default_theme_id` is NULL, and a member who chose nothing gets `theme: null` from `GET /themes/active`. In `themes_test.go` the theme is only deleted after `themeDefault` has cleared the default.
- [x] An administrator and somebody else's themes: alice's `DELETE /themes/{themeID}` on bob's shared theme is 204 and its files leave the bucket. On bob's private theme, `DELETE` and `PATCH` are 404 and the row is unchanged. Today only a member's refusals and the administrator's rename are tried.
- [x] File refusals over HTTP: a member's `DELETE /themes/{themeID}/assets/{assetID}` on a shared theme is 403 and the file is still served. A stranger's `GET /themes/{themeID}/assets/{assetID}` on a private theme is 404. The 65th `POST /themes/{themeID}/assets` is 409 `conflict` with "at most 64 files". A file over 12 MB is 413 `too_large`, and nothing is written to the bucket. A WOFF2 font is accepted and served as `font/woff2`. Today only the visibility of private files is tried, through SQL, and the size only in the `sniff` unit test.
- [x] `POST /themes/import` with a package that carries an unsafe SVG, or a file over the size limit, is refused. No theme row and no bucket object is left behind. Today only a stray JSON file, text, a package naming a file it does not carry and a later format are tried.
- [x] A chosen theme that is later unshared: bob chooses alice's shared theme, alice unshares it, and `GET /themes/active` for bob answers `theme: null`. When an installation default exists, decide whether bob should fall back to it (today `Active` answers the built-in theme with `source` `""`, skipping the default) and assert the decision. Bob's `PUT /themes/active` naming alice's private theme is 404, and his choice is unchanged. (decided in #429: bob falls back to the built-in theme, as in Stator; his choice is kept and returns when the theme is shared again)
- [x] Exports in the reader's language: bob chooses German with `PATCH /auth/me`, then downloads the HTML site export of a project. Its pages say "Inhalt", "Suchen" and "Glossar". The Word export's headings come in German too, and alice's English. The print request bob's PDF sends to the render stub carries `language: "de"`. No integration test sets a German locale before an export today. `siteLabels` and the `language(r)` handlers are reached only in English.

Browser (e2e scenario):
- [x] Make a theme in the editor: "New theme" (`new-theme`) opens `/settings/themes/new`. Pick "Constellation" under "Start from", rename it and press "Save theme" (`save-theme`). The page moves to `/settings/themes/<id>`, the theme is listed under "Mine", and "Use this theme" in the editor applies it to the shell. Today every theme of `themes.spec.ts` is made through the API or an import.
- [x] Colours and preview: on an existing theme, set "Links, the current item" to `#ff0066`. Switch on "Preview on this page" (`preview-theme`): `--color-accent` on the page changes before anything is saved. "Reset Links, the current item" (`reset-token`) takes the preview back. Leaving the editor without saving restores the chosen theme. Save, then use the theme, and the shell has the colour.
- [x] Files in the editor: on the Files tab, "Add a file" (`add-theme-file`) uploads a PNG, which is listed with its size. On the Backdrop tab, choose it and save: the page draws it behind the content. Back on Files, "Remove <name>" (`remove-theme-file`) is disabled while the file is in use. Once the backdrop is cleared and saved, the confirm removes the file. A scripted SVG shows the server's sentence, and a file over 12 MB shows "That file is over 12 MB. Make it smaller and try again." without any upload.
- [x] Sharing from the row menu: alice's "Share with everyone" (`share-theme`) puts the theme under bob's "Shared with me" with "Shared", and bob uses it. Alice's "Stop sharing" takes it away, and bob's next page load has no `style#exciter-theme`. "Delete" (`delete-theme`) asks with the number of people using the theme and removes the row. None of these row actions is clicked today.
- [x] Default from the Themes page: alice's "Make it the default for everyone" (`default-theme`) on a shared theme reaches bob, who chose nothing. "No longer the default for everyone" (`undefault-theme`) takes it off him. Bob's "Stop using" (`stop-theme`) on a theme he chose says "Back to the default for everyone.". After he keeps the built-in theme, "Use the default for everyone" (`org-default-theme`) brings it back. On `/settings/default-theme`, "Built-in theme" (`[data-default-theme-choice="built-in"]`) clears the default for everyone. Today only naming a default on that page and "Use the built-in theme" are tried.
- [x] What a member may not do: on alice's shared theme, bob's row shows its name as plain text, not a link, and "Edit", "Stop sharing" and "Delete" are disabled in "Actions for <name>". Importing a JSON file that is not a theme shows "That is not a theme file" in the error banner, and no row is added.
- [x] A German browser: a context with `locale: "de-DE"`, and bob with no language chosen. `html[lang]` is `de`, the sidebar says "Start", the settings hub, Themes and Members headings are the German catalogue's, and a date on the audit log is written the German way, day first and with a German month name. Choosing "English" on Your profile switches the page at once. "Language of the browser" (`[data-language="browser"]`) brings German back. Today Deutsch is only chosen by hand, and only one heading is read. (decided in #429: run as alice, since Members and the audit log are an administrator's; the audit log's medium date has no month name in German, so day, month and year in that order are asserted)
- [x] German at phone width and under axe: with German chosen, `/`, `/projects`, `/settings/members`, `/settings/themes` and a requirement page pass `expectAccessible` and do not scroll sideways, since German words are longer. Today `a11y.spec.ts` runs in English only.

Component (vitest):
- [x] ThemeEditor tabs: Shape, Type, Cursors, Icons, Backdrop and Advanced each change the spec that "Save theme" sends, for example the control radius, a font file, a cursor with its hotspot, an icon's path data, a backdrop file with `cover` or `tile`, and extra CSS with its size shown. "Reset <label>" removes a colour and the count reads "0 of 44 colours changed.". Today only the Colours tab, the preview and the files list are tried. (decided in #429: with no colour changed the count gives way to "Nothing changed yet: every colour is the stylesheet's.")
- [x] FilesTab: a file over `THEME_ASSET_MAX_BYTES` shows the too big banner and calls no upload. An upload shows "Added <name>". Remove asks first and then deletes. A new theme's Files tab says to save first.
- [x] ThemesPage row menu: the owner gets Edit, Share and Delete enabled. A member gets them disabled on another person's shared theme, and the name is not a link. An administrator gets "Make it the default for everyone" only on a shared theme, and "No longer the default for everyone" on the default. Delete's confirm names how many people use the theme, and a cancelled confirm deletes nothing. Today `themes.test.tsx` covers the list, the sorting and the meta line only.
- [x] Plurals in both catalogues: for every catalogue function that takes one count, `f(1)` and `f(2)` differ in more than the number whenever the English ones do, in German too. Today only `members.count` is checked.
- [x] Lookups keyed by what the server sends: every reason `signInFailure` in `oidc_handlers.go` can put on `/login?sso=`, plus `denied`, has a sentence in `t.login.failures` in both languages, or is `SSO_WAITING`. The same goes for every signing failure behind `t.review.signatureError` and every `Excluded.Reason` behind `t.sessions.excludedReasons`. These are typed `Record<string, string>`, so TypeScript does not notice when one is missing.

Go unit:
- [x] `theme.validateCSS` refuses what it lets through today: `background: image-set("https://evil.example/p.png" 1x)` and an escaped `u\72l(https://evil.example/p.png)` both reach another origin without matching `urlCall`. Add both to `TestAThemeIsValidatedPartByPart`. Today only a plain `url(https://...)` and `@import` are tried. The web server's `img-src 'self'` blocks the request, but the stored theme is still accepted. (decided in #429: both forms were already refused; the exact strings are added to the table)

## Done when
- Every control of the Themes page, the theme editor (all eight tabs) and `/settings/default-theme` is clicked by a browser scenario that checks its effect on the page or on another person.
- Deleting or unsharing the default and a chosen theme, and every theme file limit, have an integration test with the status and the code.
- A browser test runs the interface in German from the browser's language, and an export made for a German reader is checked for German labels.
- The catalogue lookups keyed by server strings and the plurals are checked in both languages.

issues.title: Test the worker's own jobs, migrations, probes and the chart beyond a render
issues.body:
The moving parts underneath Exciter are tested well where they are hardest. `outbox_test.go` covers an event committing and rolling back with its change, the app role adding events only in its own name, two workers never handling one event, a failed event waiting longer, a given up one in the audit log, and the worker holding no lock while it handles. `worker_test.go` covers the retry steps, the mux, `Before` and the chain. `replication_test.go` covers reads on the replica, read your writes while replay is paused, lag and the rotation. `migration_owner_test.go`, `probes_test.go`, `seed_test.go`, `partner_bootstrap_test.go` and `one_installation_test.go` cover the migration owner, the probes and metrics with a database, the bootstrap and partners connecting once, and one installation. `config_test.go` refuses every bad setting in sentences. `render_test.go`, `diagram_test.go` and `s3_test.go` cover the clients of the render service, Kroki and the bucket. `tests/test-helm.sh` checks dozens of rendered values, eleven refusals and two golden renders, `scripts/chart-install-test.sh` installs and upgrades in kind, `tests/test-release.sh` covers release.sh thoroughly, and `tests/test-stack.sh` checks the compose file and the realm. The test execution reminder and the OAuth sweeper are listed with test management and OAuth.

What is missing is the rest of what the worker runs and how it behaves when things go wrong. The review session reminder and outbox pruning are never run. Nothing tries a handler that panics, a lease that runs out or a trace carried through the outbox. No migration is ever run down. `/readyz` is never asked while the database is down. The render service itself has no test. The chart install never shows the worker doing anything, and three of the chart's refusals and several of its settings are never rendered.

## Gaps

Go integration:
- [x] `review.NewReminder(...).Once`: an open session whose deadline is within `ReminderLead` gets `reminded_at` and one `review_session.reminder` event, with the moderator as `actorId`. A second `Once` adds nothing, and so do two run side by side. A closed session, one with no deadline and one due in three days are left alone. No test calls it today.
- [x] Outbox pruning: plant a processed event older than `Retention`, a processed one from an hour ago and an unprocessed one older than `Retention`. Start `events.NewWorker(...).Run`, which prunes on its first pass. Only the first is deleted. No test reaches `prune` today.
- [x] The worker when a handler goes wrong. A handler that panics leaves its event with `attempts` 1 and `last_error` "the handler panicked", and the next event of the same batch is still handled. A worker whose context ends mid batch hands the unhandled events back (`available_at <= now()`), so a second worker takes them at once. An event left claimed by a worker that died is taken again once its lease runs out. Today a failure is only an error returned, in `TestAFailedEventWaitsAndAGivenUpOneIsAudited`.
- [x] A trace through the outbox: a request with a `traceparent` header emits an event. The row's `trace_parent` holds that trace, and the worker's span "events <topic>" belongs to the same trace (`observability.WithSpanExporter` with an in-memory exporter, which no test uses today). The request's access log line carries `request_id` equal to `X-Request-Id`, and `trace_id` equal to the incoming trace. Today only the echoed `X-Request-Id` is checked, in `router_test.go`.
- [x] Migrations down and up again: on a scratch database, `migrate up`, then `migrate down` one step at a time to version 0, then `migrate up` again. Every Down runs without error, and `pg_dump --schema-only` after the second up equals the first. No test runs a Down today, so a broken one is only found during an incident.
- [x] `/readyz` follows the database: with the pool's primary unreachable (the harness's primary paused, or a cluster on a closed address), `/readyz` answers 503 `{"status":"unavailable"}` within `readinessTimeout` while `/healthz` stays 200. Once the primary is back it answers 200 again. `api -healthcheck` exits non-zero for the 503 and zero for the 200. Today only a server with no database at all is tried, in `router_test.go`, and `healthcheck()` never runs.
- [x] Kroki fetches nothing from elsewhere: `POST /diagrams` with `!includeurl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` and with `!include https://example.com/x.puml` answers a drawing (or the renderer's refusal) that holds nothing fetched. Today only a local file include is tried, in `diagram_test.go`.
- [x] Worker startup refusals: with `EXCITER_VALKEY_URL=not a url`, `cmd/worker` exits non-zero and says "is not a valid Valkey URL". With a Valkey that does not answer, it says "connect to Valkey" within `valkeyWait`. Without `EXCITER_SMTP_ADDR`, a mention still writes the in-app notification, and the event is marked done. These paths are only read, never run.

Go unit:
- [x] `cmd/migrate` and `cmd/seed` have no tests. Move the argument checks out of `run` and try them: `migrate frobnicate` names the five commands, `up-to` without a version and `up-to x` are refused in their sentences, and `waitForPrimary` gives up after `connectAttempts` saying how often it tried. Bare `seed` and `seed demo` are refused in production, `seed bootstrap` is refused without `EXCITER_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL`, an unknown command is refused, and partner URLs without an administrator are refused by `connectPartners`.
- [x] `mail.SMTPMailer.Send` against a fake SMTP listener: the envelope sender is the bare address of `Exciter <no-reply@...>`, the headers and the CRLF body arrive as written, and a line starting with "." comes through whole. A relay that accepts the connection and never answers must make `Send` return within a set time. Today it would block, since `Send` ignores its context and `smtp.SendMail` dials with no deadline (see the separate report). Only header encoding is tested today, in `mail_test.go`.

Component (vitest):
- [x] `render/server.mjs` has no test. Run it under `node --test` in a container against a small page server: a body that is not JSON, a path starting `//`, a token with a newline and a language that is no tag each answer 400. A print beyond `RENDER_CONCURRENCY` answers 503, and one past its budget answers 504. A page that asks for another origin gets that request aborted. The bearer token is added only to `/api/` requests of `RENDER_APP_URL`'s origin. `/healthz` answers 503 once the browser has gone.

Chart and scripts (tests/test-*.sh):

issues.body:

issues.title: Keep groups and group membership to administrators in the database
issues.body:
## User story

As an administrator, I want the database to hold groups and their memberships to administrators, as the service already does, so that who is in a group, and so what that group's grants reach, does not rest on the service alone.

## What happens today

This is defense in depth. The service changes `groups` and `group_member` only for administrators, and sign-in keeps provider groups in step through the admin role. The database does not yet hold these two tables to the same rule: they have only the open policy every table has, and no restrictive one for `exciter_app`, as `oidc_provider`, `oidc_group_role` and `org_join_request` have.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Through `exciter_app`, inserting, updating and deleting rows of `groups` and `group_member` takes an administrator of the installation acting with a whole-installation session or token.
- [ ] Reading both tables is unchanged: the people and group pickers, grants naming groups, and reviews and signatures that resolve a group keep working for everybody who uses them today.
- [ ] Sign-in through the identity provider and a partner's token exchange keep joining, leaving and creating provider groups.

## Tests

- **Integration:** straight through SQL as `exciter_app`, a plain member is refused every insert, update and delete on both tables, and a group's admin grant still does not reach them; an administrator still makes each write. `sso_rls_test.go` names both tables among those only administrators write.
- The SSO, group role, permission and review suites still pass.

## Implementation

A migration with restrictive `INSERT`, `UPDATE` and `DELETE` policies for `exciter_app` on both tables, using `current_actor_administers()`. Every writer of the tables today runs as `exciter_admin` or as the superuser in tests, which the policies do not bind.

## Depends on

Nothing. Stator closed the same kind of gap in praetorianer777/Stator#530.

issues.title: The specification's tree does not scroll on its own, and wide screens leave the page a narrow centred block
issues.body:
### What happened, and what did you expect?

On a project's specification (`/p/<key>/spec`) the tree beside the document does not scroll on its own:

- Once the document is scrolled, the top of the tree slides under the page header, which sticks above it.
- The tree is sized to 80% of the window, ignoring the top bar and the header, so its last items lie below the
  visible area and can only be reached by scrolling the whole document.
- Scrolling to the end of the tree carries on scrolling the document.

On a wide monitor the page is a centred block of 72rem, so the tree floats in the middle with empty space on both
sides.

Expected:

- The tree stays just below the page header, fits the visible area and scrolls by itself, without moving the
  document.
- On wide screens the tree sits at the left of the content area, a little wider on very wide screens, and the
  document fills the space beside it with its text kept at a readable width (64rem at most).
- Phone widths keep today's stacked layout.

Tests: a browser test with a project long enough that tree and document both overflow. With the document scrolled to
its end, the tree starts below the header and ends inside the visible area; scrolling the tree to its end shows the
last item and leaves the document where it was. At 2560x1440 the tree starts at the content area's left edge and the
document is at most 64rem wide.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the specification of a project with about 40 requirements, on a window wide enough to show the tree beside the
   document.
2. Scroll the document down: the tree's top disappears under the header.
3. Try to reach the tree's last item without scrolling the document.
4. Widen the window to 2560px: the tree and document stay a centred 72rem block.

### Version or commit

main at 1c4031b

issues.title: A ReqIF import reads as done before the project's tree shows it
issues.body:
## User story

As somebody importing a ReqIF file, I want the project's tree to show what the import made once the import says it is done, so that I do not look at an empty project and import it again.

## What happened

In a full local `make test-integration` on 2026-10-26 (main plus #371, under the whole suite's load), `TestReqIFImportLeavesTheGlossaryOut` failed:

```
reqif_test.go:314: the tree: got [], want [1 requirement Stop]
--- FAIL: TestReqIFImportLeavesTheGlossaryOut (0.65s)
```

`finishedReqIF` had just read the import as `done` with one requirement in `imported`, and the next request, `GET /projects/{key}/tree`, found no requirement. Run alone it passed 5 of 5. CI has not shown it so far.

## Cause

The two answers come from different snapshots, so two reads in a row went to different servers:

- `reqifio.Service.Get` and the tree both read through `db.Read`. `Cluster.readConn` takes a replica for each read on its own when the replica lags less than `EXCITER_DB_MAX_REPLICA_LAG` (2 s by default) and has replayed the caller's own last write.
- The import's rows and its `done` are written by the worker (`reqifio/run.go`, `end`), so they are nobody's own write and no request is pinned to them.
- A read that finds the replica lagging past the limit goes to the primary and sees `done`. The next read, once the replica is back under the limit but still behind, sees the project before the import.

So reads are not monotonic across what the worker writes. A person polling an import sees the same thing: done, then an empty tree until they reload. #307 looks like the same thing in the browser, with the CI result the worker records.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Once a request has seen the worker's write (an import done, a result recorded), the caller's later reads see it too
- [ ] `TestReqIFImportLeavesTheGlossaryOut` passes 20 of 20 in full `make test-integration` runs, and a test makes the replica lag (as the replica tests already pause replay) and shows the tree following the import's state
- [ ] #307 is checked against the fix and closed or updated

## Implementation

Options to weigh:

- Note the LSN of what a read saw for the caller: when a read on the primary answers, record `pg_current_wal_lsn()` (or the transaction's snapshot position) under the caller's freshness key, so their next reads need a replica at least that far. This makes every read monotonic, at the cost of more reads on the primary while a replica is behind.
- Narrower: the import (and the CI result) keeps the LSN of the write that finished it, and `Get` notes it for the caller once it answers `done`.
- Only in the tests: read the tree with `eventually`. This hides the problem from the people who hit it, so not on its own.

## Tests

As in the acceptance criteria.

## Depends on

Nothing.

issues.title: The matrix and chain files of a project past the export cap run out of time
issues.body:
## User story

As somebody exporting the traceability matrix or the chains of a large project, I want the file to arrive cut at the export cap and marked so, so that I get the first 20000 rows rather than a timeout.

## What happened

While closing #315 on 2026-10-27, tests that reach `csvio.MaxExportRows` (20000) were written against a local stack, with the race detector as `make test-integration` runs it:

- **Matrix:** a project of 20001 requirements, written straight through SQL and then analysed (`ANALYZE`, later `VACUUM (ANALYZE)`). The first `GET /projects/{key}/matrix.csv` answered 503 `timed_out` after the 30 s request deadline, in 3 runs of 3. Minutes later the same project answered `matrix.csv` in 7 s, `matrix?limit=1` in 9 s and `requirements?limit=1` in 6 s.
- **Chains:** one need reaching 142 systems, each verified by the same 142 tests, so 20164 lines. `GET /projects/{key}/trace-chains` answered 503 `timed_out` in 2 runs of 3 instead of 422 with the `TooManyLinesError` sentence, and `trace-chains.csv` once answered 503 too. In the run where both answered, the file held exactly 20000 lines with `X-Export-Truncated: true`.
- **Cost in the suite:** writing the 20164 trace links straight through SQL took 98 to 141 s, and purging the project of 20001 requirements takes about 26 s, close to the harness's 30 s bound for one cleanup statement.

So the `X-Export-Truncated` paths of `matrix.csv`, `matrix.xlsx`, `trace-chains.csv` and `trace-chains.xlsx` are not proven by any test, and the gap in #315 is open.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `matrix.csv` and `matrix.xlsx` of a project with more requirements than the cap answer within the request deadline, hold exactly the cap and set `X-Export-Truncated: true`
- [ ] `trace-chains.csv` and `trace-chains.xlsx` with more lines than the cap do the same, and a page of those chains answers 422 rather than timing out
- [ ] Integration tests prove both without writing 20000 rows into the shared stack

## Implementation

- Find where a matrix of 20001 rows spends its time: `search.Keep` reads every row with the tree walk, the quality scores and `perm_requirement_viewable`, and `requirementLinks` reads the whole project again as the candidate columns before matching `trace_link_state` against two arrays of 20001 ids, even when no row has a link.
- Let the suite lower the cap: the export cap could be a field of `httpapi.Server` that defaults to `csvio.MaxExportRows`, set low through `newAPIServerWith` as the coverage cache test already swaps the trace service, so a test reaches it with a handful of rows.

## Tests

As in the acceptance criteria.

## Depends on

Nothing.
