issues.title: Switching a person off leaves their Armature and Stator tokens
issues.body:
## User story

As an administrator who switches somebody off, I want Exciter to stop acting for them in Armature and Stator, so that nobody who left keeps a way in through Exciter.

## What happens

Switching a person off (`DELETE /users/{userID}`, `auth.Service.SetActive` with `active` false) sets `is_active` to false, deletes their Exciter tokens and sessions, and leaves their `armature_token` and `stator_token` rows, pasted or from a sign-in, as they were. `app_user_left` deletes those rows only when the role goes to NULL, which no request does. Nothing in `armature.Service.Viewer`, `stator.Service.Viewer` or the link sync checks `is_active`, so an `armature.links` or `stator.links` event the person queued before they were switched off is still synced as them, and a grant from a sign-in is still renewed.

Found while testing #326, whose item covers the role going to NULL (`TestAPersonWithoutARoleHoldsNoArmatureToken`).

## Acceptance criteria

- Switching a person off deletes their Armature and Stator tokens, pasted and from a sign-in, in the same change as their Exciter tokens, or the Viewers treat an inactive person as not connected. The decision is recorded in `docs/decisions.md`.
- Switching them on again leaves them to connect again, and their account page says so.

## Tests

- Integration: after `DELETE /users/{id}`, no `armature_token` or `stator_token` row of theirs is left, and an event they queued is not synced as them.
- Browser: none needed beyond the members page.

## Implementation

`SetActive` deletes `api_token` rows as `exciter_app`; the partner tokens are only their owner's under row level security, so they go through the admin role, or `app_user_left` grows a branch for `is_active`.

## Depends on

Nothing.

issues.title: A long read on the replica answers 500 when replay cancels it
issues.body:
`TestADocumentPastItsLimitSaysSo` failed in a whole local integration run: `GET /projects/{key}/document` answered 500 with

```
ERROR: canceling statement due to conflict with recovery (SQLSTATE 40001)
```

The document of a large project is a long read, and it ran on the replica. When the primary cleans up rows (vacuum, or a hot update) that the replica's read still sees, the standby has to replay that cleanup; after `max_standby_streaming_delay` it cancels the read instead. `db.Cluster.Read` hands that error up, so the person gets "Something went wrong on our side" for a read the primary could have answered. Neither Armature nor Stator handles it either.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The deployment guide says the same for replicas of one's own.
- [ ] An integration test holds a snapshot on the standby and sees the primary keep rows for it.

Retrying such a read on the primary was weighed and left: many read functions gather rows into variables outside them, so running one twice could answer them twice.

issues.title: Let the push gate reuse layers that already passed on the pushed tree
issues.body:
## User story

As a contributor pushing from Claude Code, I want the push gate to trust layers that already passed on the exact tree I push, so a push does not spend another four minutes running tests I ran a moment ago.

The branch-guard log shows 282 gates with a median of 228 seconds, about 18 hours in total. In 163 of 183 pushes in the recent transcripts, `./run-tests.sh` or the same make targets had already run on the unchanged tree just before the push.

## Acceptance criteria

- A run of `./run-tests.sh` that passes on a clean working tree records each layer it ran against the tree of `HEAD`, in the checkout's own git directory, so worktrees keep their own record.
- Nothing is recorded when the working tree had uncommitted or untracked changes at the start or the end of the run, or when `HEAD`'s tree changed during it.
- Runs on the same tree add to the record: `./run-tests.sh check-go` then `./run-tests.sh check-web` together cover a gate of both.
- A push whose gate layers all passed on the tree being pushed is allowed without running them, and says so: "Gate passed earlier on this tree: ...". A push needing any layer that has no pass recorded for that tree runs the gate as today.
- The guard log marks a reused gate, so a push without a fresh run can be traced.

## Tests

- `branch-guard-test.sh`: a recorded pass for the pushed tree skips the stubbed `run-tests.sh`; a pass recorded for another tree, or one missing a needed layer, runs it.
- A shell test for `run-tests.sh` that runs the `shell` layer's recording on a clean throwaway clone and on a dirty one, and checks the record.

## Implementation

`run-tests.sh` writes `$(git rev-parse --git-path exciter-gate-passed)` with one `<tree>\t<layer>` line per layer that passed, keeping lines for the same tree and dropping others. `branch-guard.sh`'s `run_tests` reads it before starting the gate.

## Depends on

Nothing.

issues.title: The query compiler's bind markers could be rewritten inside future SQL fragments
issues.body:
The query compiler marks bind values as `?N` and `Compiled.Place` rewrites every match of `\?(\d+)` in the finished SQL (`backend/internal/rql/compile.go:38-72`), and `replace()` indexes `marks[n]` without a bounds check (`compile.go:74-79`). Nothing triggers it today: user input only ever reaches bound values, and the literal jsonb operators (`?|` at `compile_attributes.go:68`, `?` at `compile.go:257`) are never followed by a digit. A future fragment such as `?0` in a literal or an operator would be rewritten silently, or panic when `n` is out of range.

## Fix
- Mark bind values with a token that cannot appear in SQL, or write the jsonb operators as `jsonb_exists` and `jsonb_exists_any` so the compiler emits no literal `?`.
- Bounds-check `replace()` with a clear panic message.

## Tests
- Compile every attribute kind and operator; `Place` output contains no `\?\d` and `len(args)` equals the highest `$N`.
- A fragment holding a literal `?0` survives `Place` unchanged.

issues.title: A webhook delivery can be posted twice when more than one sender runs
issues.body:
A webhook delivery can be posted twice, and its failures counted twice, when more than one sender runs, as during a worker rollout or with `worker.replicas > 1`. `Sender` says any number may run (`backend/internal/webhook/sender.go:9-10`) and `SendDue` promises senders never post one twice (`deliver.go:101-103`); neither holds once a batch outlasts its lease.

`SendDue` claims up to `sendBatch = 100` rows and leases them for `ClaimLease = 2m`, then posts them one after another with `sendTimeout = 10s` each (`deliver.go:25-39`, `104-149`). Thirteen hanging receivers outlast the lease, and another sender claims the rows still waiting. `attempt` re-reads the row checking only `state = 'pending'` (`deliver.go:278-303`) and `record` updates `WHERE id = $1` with no lease guard (`deliver.go:361-368`), so both posts land and both outcomes commit: the second overwrites the first, `countFailure` raises `failures` twice, and a second retry row burns through `MaxAttempts` early and can turn the endpoint off sooner.

A single sender never overlaps itself (`Sender.Run` waits for `SendDue`), and `Test` and `Redeliver` post one row inside its lease, so they are safe.

## Fix
- Use the claimed `next_attempt_at` as a lease token: `SendDue` returns it, `attempt` renews the lease with `... WHERE id = $1 AND state = 'pending' AND next_attempt_at = $token RETURNING next_attempt_at` just before posting and skips the row when nothing comes back.
- Add the same guard to `record`'s UPDATE; when it affects no row, count no failure and insert no retry.
- Optionally keep `sendBatch * sendTimeout <= ClaimLease`.

## Tests
- Integration: an endpoint on a stub bin that holds its answer; start `SendDue` A, expire its lease as the admin role, run `SendDue` B, release the bin. Exactly one POST with that `X-Exciter-Delivery` id, `failures` raised once, one attempt-2 row.
- SQL: a `record` UPDATE with a stale token affects no row.

issues.title: A dead API token signs the browser session out
issues.body:
A request that carries a valid session cookie and a dead API token in `Authorization: Bearer` signs the browser user out. The `ErrInvalidToken` branch in `backend/internal/httpapi/middleware.go:174-178` clears the session cookie whenever one is present, even though the failing secret came from the header and the cookie is fine.

The web client sends no Authorization header, so this hits tooling or a CORS-allowed origin that sends a stale token with `credentials: include`.

## Fix
Let `credentialFrom` report which credential it used, and clear the session cookie only when the cookie was the credential that failed.

## Tests
- Unit: valid session cookie plus `Bearer <dead token>`; no `Set-Cookie` that expires the session, and a follow-up with the cookie alone is still signed in.
- Keep the case that a dead cookie on its own is cleared.

issues.title: Webhook deliveries follow redirects to hosts the endpoint does not name
issues.body:
The webhook sender follows redirects. Its client is `netguard.Client` (`backend/internal/webhook/webhook.go:290`), whose `CheckRedirect` only caps hops at `MaxRedirects = 3` (`backend/internal/netguard/netguard.go:25-27`, `179-189`). On a 307 or 308 the signed body is posted again, with valid `X-Exciter` signature and timestamp headers, to a host the admin never configured, or from https to plain http.

Redirects into reserved networks are already refused at dial time, as `TestARedirectIsCheckedAgain` and `TestARedirectIntoTheNetworkIsRefused` prove, and only the receiver can send the redirect, so this is hygiene rather than a new path in. A delivery should still go only where the endpoint says.

## Fix
Give the webhook sender its own `CheckRedirect` returning `http.ErrUseLastResponse`, so a 3xx is logged through the existing "The receiver answered %d" branch (`deliver.go:339-340`). Other netguard users keep their redirect handling.

## Tests
- Unit: two `httptest` servers, the first answering 307 to the second; `post` returns 307 and the second is never hit.
- Integration: a stub bin answering 307 to a second bin; the second receives nothing and the delivery is logged failed with status 307.

issues.title: A review session whose approvers reach nobody opens and can never be decided
issues.body:
A review session whose approvers reach nobody opens anyway and can never be decided. `checkParticipants` (`backend/internal/review/sessions.go:96`) checks only that a named group exists, which is intended: group members take part as they are when they act (`docs/api-contract-m8.md:384-385`). But when the sole approver is an empty group, or a group whose only member is the revision's author, `approversReached` (`sessions.go:231-249`) returns 0, `review_session_pin` (`migrations/00940_review_sessions.sql:131-139`) sets `required = GREATEST(1, ...)` = 1, and every requirement in the session sits in `review_pending` until the moderator closes it.

## Fix
- In `OpenSession`, after `approversReached`, answer 422 on `participants` when it reaches nobody, with a message such as "The approvers reach nobody. Name a person, or a group with members, who approves."
- Refuse the same in `review_session_pin` with a `check_violation`, so the database holds it too.

## Tests
- Integration: sole approver an empty group gives 422 on `participants` and no session; after adding a member, 201.
- SQL as `exciter_app`: a session with an empty-group approver makes `review_session_pin` raise `check_violation`.
- A group whose only member is the author is refused the same way.

issues.title: A CORS origin configured with a trailing slash never gets CORS headers
issues.body:
An origin configured with a trailing slash, as `EXCITER_CORS_ORIGINS=https://app.example/`, is trusted by the cross-site check but never gets CORS headers, so the cross-origin client fails with no clear error. `splitList` (`backend/internal/config/loader.go:207-215`) only trims spaces; `cors` (`backend/internal/httpapi/edges.go:27-34`) compares the raw string with the browser's `Origin`, which never ends in `/`, while `sameSite` (`edges.go:57`, `69`) trims it. The two disagree in the safe direction, so requests are refused, not let through.

`append(allowed, s.AppBaseURL)` at `edges.go:56` can also write into the spare capacity of the configured slice; nothing reads it today, but it is fragile.

## Fix
- Normalise origins once at config load (trim spaces and a trailing `/`, check with `url.Parse`) and have `cors` and `sameSite` use the same set.
- Build the list with `slices.Concat` instead of `append`.

## Tests
- Config unit: `"https://a.example/, https://b.example"` loads as `[https://a.example https://b.example]`.
- Router unit: with `https://a.example/` configured, an OPTIONS from `Origin: https://a.example` gets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.

issues.title: The Go coverage gate rounds a total up and passes it below its floor
issues.body:
The Go coverage gate lets a total just below its floor pass. `scripts/coverage.sh:22` prints the Go total with `%.1f`, which rounds to nearest, and the floor check compares that rounded figure, so 75.96% prints as 76.0 and passes the floor of 76 in `coverage/go-integration.floor`. The web branch already rounds down to one decimal, as CONTRIBUTING.md's rounded-down rule expects.

## Fix
Round the Go totals down to one decimal, as the web branch does, for the total and for each package.

## Tests
A shell test in `tests/` feeding `scripts/coverage.sh go` a profile at 75.96% against a floor of 76 expects a failure, and one at exactly 76.0 a pass.

issues.title: A Floor-lowered trailer lets a coverage floor fall by any amount
issues.body:
A `Floor-lowered` trailer lets a floor go down by any amount, and covers every drop of that floor on the branch. `tests/test-coverage-floors.sh:8` gathers the trailer names from every commit in `$base..HEAD` and, for a floor below main's, only asks whether its name is among them (`:16`).

- A commit with `Floor-lowered: web-lines x` can take the floor from 86 to 0 and the check prints ok. Nothing compares the new floor with the measured total, so one loosely worded trailer turns the ratchet off for that layer.
- An early commit lowers a floor with a trailer and a later commit lowers it again for an unrelated reason; the second drop passes on the first commit's reason.

CONTRIBUTING.md allows a floor down only when the measurement itself changes, which the trailer records but the check does not hold to.

## Fix
- Accept a lowered floor only at the layer's new total rounded down, read from `reports/coverage-<name>.tsv` when the layer has run, or have the trailer name the value, as `Floor-lowered: web-lines 86 <reason>`, and require the file to match it.
- Match the trailer against the commit that changes the floor file, not the whole range.

## Tests
A shell test that builds a throwaway repository with a `main` and a branch, and checks: a drop with no trailer fails; a drop with a trailer naming another floor fails; a drop with a matching trailer and value passes; a second drop after a trailed one fails.

issues.title: Web coverage reads a point lower in CI than locally, so a local pass can fail CI
issues.body:
Web line coverage reads about a point lower in CI than on a local run of the same commit, so a change can pass the floor locally and fail it in CI. For 73e798b the commit message records 87.11% locally and 86.08% in CI, against a floor of 86 in `coverage/web-lines.floor`. The floor follows the rule and sits at the CI total rounded down, so the next few uncovered lines fail CI while `./run-tests.sh` still passes on the contributor's machine.

## Fix
Find what differs between the two runs: the file set vitest counts, a test that is skipped in one environment, sharding, or the Node version. Then make the local run measure what CI measures, or have the gate report the CI figure.

## Tests
Running the web layer locally and in CI on one commit gives the same `total` in `reports/coverage-web-lines.tsv`.

issues.title: Pin vitest and its coverage provider to the same version
issues.body:
`web/package.json` pins `@vitest/coverage-v8` to `5.0.5` (`:44`) but lets `vitest` float as `^5.0.5` (`:55`), while the provider's peer dependency is exactly `vitest 5.0.5` (`web/package-lock.json:3250-3253`). A lockfile refresh or a dependency update can move vitest to a later 5.x without the provider and give a peer-dependency error or a changed coverage reading, which matters now that the web floor sits close to the measured total.

## Fix
Pin the two the same way, both exact or both `^`, so they move together, and group them in dependency updates.

## Tests
`npm ci` and the web layer pass; `npm ls vitest @vitest/coverage-v8` shows one version for both.

issues.title: Let people in by their groups only when an administrator turns it on
issues.body:
Armature lets people in by their groups only once an administrator says so (Cloudster1/Armature#301). Exciter admits anyone in a mapped group as soon as the group is mapped, with no switch, no sentence that says so and no record of why someone got in. The three tools share one realm, so an administrator should find the same setting, with the same name and default, in each of them.

What Armature does, as the reference:
- `admitByGroup` on `PUT /oidc-provider`, default false, shown on the sign-in settings page as "Let people in by their groups", with a sentence saying what it does.
- When it is on, a person without standing whose groups claim holds a mapped group is created and let in with that group's role. This happens at sign-in and at a partner's token exchange.
- When it is off, such a person waits to be let in, as anybody in no mapped group does. A person switched off is refused either way.
- The audit log records each admission as admitted by group <name>.

## Done when
- Exciter has `admitByGroup` on `GET` and `PUT /oidc-provider`, and the switch on Settings, Single sign-on, worded as Armature's.
- Off: mapping a group still sets the roles of people already in at their next sign-in, but lets nobody new in, neither at sign-in nor at a token exchange.
- On: what happens today, and the audit log names the group that let each person in.
- An installation that already maps groups keeps working: the migration turns the setting on where a group role exists.
- Tests cover sign-in and token exchange for a new person in a mapped group with the setting on and off, a person in no mapped group, and a person switched off.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XsypREK6CTfvi1885SVu2k

issues.title: Split Settings from Admin and lay Admin out as the suite's standard
issues.body:
The three tools follow one standard for settings, [docs/administration.md](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo/blob/main/docs/administration.md) in Dynamo (praetorianer777/Dynamo#75). Armature is its reference. Exciter keeps everything under one `/settings`, with a hub of plain links, a refusal on each admin page, and single sign-on as a page of its own.

## Done when
- `/settings` holds only the person's own pages. The hub gives each a sentence on what it is for.
- `/admin` holds the installation's pages, in the sections People and access, Work, Integrations and Records, as the standard places them:
  - People and access: Installation (with the default theme), Access (with Members), Users (join requests, switching accounts off);
  - Work: Link types;
  - Integrations: Armature, Stator, Connected apps (taking in all tokens and all connected apps), Webhooks;
  - Records: Audit log.
- The Admin index lists every page with its sentence, and its section nav sits beside it, or is a menu on a narrow screen.
- `/admin` refuses anybody but an administrator once, as a whole. Pages stop refusing on their own.
- Administrators find one "Admin" entry in the work sidebar, the account menu and the palette ("Admin / <page>").
- Every `/settings/<page>` that moved redirects to its new address.
- Single sign-on is a tab of Access with the standard's form: issuer, client ID, client secret, groups claim, "Let people in by their groups", Set up or Save, and "Turn it off". Scopes, creating groups and the callback address leave the form.
- The wording follows the standard: "installation", "people", "administrator".
- The browser tests reach every Admin page through the new navigation.

Related: the access model (roles, matrix, groups and grants) is its own issue.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XsypREK6CTfvi1885SVu2k

issues.title: Grant access through roles, a permission matrix, groups and grants
issues.body:
The three tools grant access one way, set out in [docs/administration.md](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo/blob/main/docs/administration.md#access) in Dynamo (praetorianer777/Dynamo#75): roles, a permission matrix, groups and grants, as Armature has them (Cloudster1/Armature `backend/migrations/00010_rbac.sql`, `web/src/features/access/RoleMatrix.tsx`, `RoleTable.tsx`, `GroupList.tsx`, the `/roles`, `/permissions`, `/groups` and `/role-assignments` endpoints).

Exciter has fixed organization roles today (owner, admin, member, guest) and grants in projects (`project_grant`, migration 00110): a person, a group or everyone holds one of four fixed roles, viewer, reviewer, editor or admin, whose rights `perm_role_rights` hard-codes in SQL. There is no matrix, no role one can define, and no grant across all projects; group roles map a provider group straight to Member or Admin.

## Done when
- **Roles** are data: built-in ones that cannot be deleted, and ones administrators add, rename and delete.
  - The built-in roles are an administrator over the whole installation, and in a project viewer, reviewer, editor and project administrator.
  - Each lists its permissions outright, with no inheritance.
- **The Matrix tab** lists every permission Exciter checks against every role. A box saves when ticked; the administrator's right to administer stays ticked.
- **Groups** are added by hand or carry a provider claim. Provider memberships are replaced at every sign-in. A built-in Everyone group holds every member.
- **Grants** are a role, a scope (the whole installation or one project) and a subject (a person or a group). What somebody may do in a project is the union of the grants that reach them; `perm_project_holds` reads roles from the database instead of `perm_role_rights`. The "everyone" subject becomes the Everyone group.
- **Guests:** a guest still never holds project administration, as `project_grant_guest_check` keeps today.
- **Buttons** are decided by permission, never by a role's name.
- **Migration:** every project grant and group role of today moves to the grant of the built-in role it amounts to, so nobody's access changes. The upgrade test proves that for a seeded installation.
- **Single sign-on:** "Let people in by their groups" (#469) admits by a group that holds a grant.
- **The database** keeps the guards it has: row level security reads the grants, and the installation keeps an active administrator.
- **Tests:**
  - grants through a person, a group, Everyone and the whole installation, a guest refused administration;
  - a renamed role and a new role reaching buttons and the API;
  - a provider group removed at sign-in taking its grants along;
  - the migration.

Related: the Admin layout is its own issue, and the Access tabs live there.

issues.title: Lay out project settings as the suite's standard
issues.body:
Exciter's project settings are one route with 14 tabs whose choice is lost on a reload (`?tab=` is read only when the page opens). Permissions is a route of its own and Trash sits in a folded "Project admin" group.

The standard is [administration.md](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo/blob/main/docs/administration.md#settings-of-a-project-or-space) in Dynamo (praetorianer777/Dynamo#75). Where it differs from what follows, the standard wins.

## Done when
- Project settings live at `/projects/<key>/settings/<section>`, one route per section; `/p/<key>/...` redirects to `/projects/<key>/...` and `?tab=` to its section. The workflow designer moves to `/projects/<key>/settings/workflows/<id>`.
- Sections in the standard's order: General (Details, with archive, delete and changing the key at its foot), Work items (Types, Attributes, Fields), Workflow (Workflow, Approval), Links and trace, Quality and risks, Templates, Members and permissions (today's `/p/<key>/permissions`), Import and export (Import, ReqIF, Word), Trash and archive.
- The tabs sit in the page header, in `Page width="content"`, and the crumbs are the project, then Settings.
- One "Settings" entry in the project's sidebar for every member replaces the "Project admin" group.
- Members keep seeing the settings read-only; sections only administrators use are hidden, and a link to one says who to ask, worded as the standard says.
- Saving shows a toast; deleting asks in a `ConfirmDialog`, archiving offers Undo.
- The browser tests reach every section by its address.

issues.title: Follow the suite's shell and feedback
issues.body:
Exciter's feedback and shell drifted from Armature's and Stator's.

The standard is [look-and-feel.md](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo/blob/main/docs/look-and-feel.md) in Dynamo (praetorianer777/Dynamo#75). Where it differs from what follows, the standard wins.

## Done when
- **Feedback**: toasts, `MutationErrorToasts` and `ConfirmDialog` as the standard says; no `window.confirm` (e.g. `features/tokens/TokensPage.tsx`, `features/reviews/ReviewPanel.tsx`). Dialogs take the standard's API: `open`, `size`, `description`, a pinned `footer`.
- **Page widths** come from `Page`; no page types its own `max-w-*`.
- **Narrow strip**: 48 px with the menu button, the installation's name and the bell.
- **Build stamp** is the shared `BuildStamp`, not written in the sidebar.
- **Account menu**: the avatar beside name, address and role, separators, and the tools' logos in one format (not webp and png mixed).
- **Palette**: actions and recents beside requirements, places and search, in groups read out as groups; the sidebar shows the translated hint, Cmd on a Mac.
- **Notifications** keep their page, named "Notifications".

Exciter's kit, formats, themes and strings drifted from Armature's and Stator's.

The standard is [look-and-feel.md](https://github.com/praetorianer777/Dynamo/blob/main/docs/look-and-feel.md) in Dynamo (praetorianer777/Dynamo#75). Where it differs from what follows, the standard wins.

issues.title: Read a large spec document within the request limit again
issues.body:
The release pull request #476 failed `TestADocumentPastItsLimitSaysSo`. Two things went wrong:
- `GET /api/v1/projects/{key}/document` still ran after 10 s and answered 500 (`spec_document_test.go:236`, `slow_request_test.go:25`).
- The test took 79.7 s.

#471 made every permission check dearer, and three paths on the milestone branch already crossed their limits: the member list, the import and deleting a link. Those were fixed in #475, and this is the next one. The spec document reads requirements, links and their ends in batches, where a plan that checks visibility row by row over the whole table costs most.

## Done when
- Reading a project's spec document costs about what it did at migration 1520, measured on a database shaped like a full integration run.
- No guard is loosened: the old and new reads return the same rows for the same people, guests and tokens.
- `TestADocumentPastItsLimitSaysSo` passes in CI, and the release can go out.

issues.title: Report oauth.partner-tokens@1 for the partner OAuth Exciter already serves
issues.body:
## User story

As a partner tool in the suite, I want Exciter's `GET /api/v1/meta` to say that it lets partner apps in over OAuth, so that I can tell from its capabilities alone, as I can at Armature and Stator.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `capabilities()` reports `oauth.partner-tokens@1`, with the promise Dynamo's `docs/compatibility.md` gives it, and the operations Exciter serves: `POST /oauth/register` (RFC 7591), `GET /oauth/authorize`, `POST /oauth/token`, `POST /oauth/revoke`, the authorization-server and protected-resource metadata, and `POST /mcp`
- [ ] Where Exciter differs from the shared promise (a registered app is active at once rather than pending until an administrator allows it), the promise or Dynamo's compatibility doc says so

## Tests

The capability unit test in `backend/internal/httpapi/capabilities_test.go`.

## Implementation

Exciter serves all of it (`httpapi/oauth_handlers.go`) but reports only `mcp@1` and `oauth.token-exchange@1`. Armature and Stator report `oauth.partner-tokens@1` for the same thing. Dynamo lists what each tool offers in praetorianer777/Dynamo#92; Rotor (Cloudster1/Rotor) registers at Exciter this way.

## Depends on

- praetorianer777/Dynamo#92

issues.title: The realm check fails since Dynamo's realm gained the rotor client
issues.body:
The shell layer's `make realm-check` fails on main and on every branch, so the push hook and CI block every change. Dynamo's canonical realm gained a `rotor` client and gave it the clients' and administrators' group (praetorianer777/Dynamo d10ecce, Dynamo #105), and `deploy/keycloak/realm.json` no longer matches it: the first difference is at line 205 of the key-sorted realm.

## User story
As a contributor, I want the gate to pass on main again, so that changes can be pushed and merged.

## Acceptance criteria
- `deploy/keycloak/realm.json` equals Dynamo's `deploy/keycloak/realm.json` on main, and `make realm-check` passes.
- The stack starts with the new realm, and sign-in works in the browser suite.

## Tests
- `make realm-check`, and the whole gate `./run-tests.sh`, including the integration and browser layers that sign in through Keycloak.

## Implementation
Copy Dynamo's realm into `deploy/keycloak/realm.json`, as 9152b3e did, and recreate the stack.

## Depends on
Nothing.

issues.title: The suite demo holds a written specification of each tool, with test cases and a test run
issues.body:
## User story

As someone trying Exciter with Armature, Stator and Rotor, I want the suite demo to hold a written specification of each tool, with its requirements, test cases and a test run, traced to the issues that built it and the guide pages that describe it, so that I see what requirements management in the suite looks like when it is done properly.

Extends the suite demo of #270. Part of one suite demo with Cloudster1/Armature#486 (the issues, now with Rotor) and praetorianer777/Stator#457 (the user guides and docs).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Four projects:** `ARM`, `EXC`, `STA` and `ROT`, the last from a Rotor snapshot taken like the others.
- [ ] **Written requirements:** each project holds a specification written for its tool rather than one derived from issue titles: stakeholder needs; functional requirements, one section per function area; non-functional requirements with measurable criteria; the interfaces the tool offers and uses in the suite; and the architecture section as today (one written for Rotor). Each requirement has a priority, a rationale and a verification method, and the software requirements refine the stakeholder needs.
- [ ] **Test specification:** a section of test cases with preconditions, steps with their expected results and parameters where they help; each test case verifies one or more requirements, and every requirement is verified by one or names why not.
- [ ] **A test run:** per project a test plan of all its test cases and one closed execution against a baseline named "Demo baseline", with results that are mostly passed and a few failed or blocked, so coverage, the matrix and the dashboards have something to show.
- [ ] **Status:** a requirement whose issues are all closed is Implemented, or Verified when its test cases passed; the rest are Approved.
- [ ] **Traces:** a requirement implements the Armature issues that built it (`ARM-123`) and is described by its Stator guide page, found by the page's label (`demo-arm-guide-boards`). "Link the demo again" also links what was missing when the demo was added.
- [ ] The content is in the repository, so adding the demo needs no network.

## Tests

- Go unit: the specification format is parsed into sections, requirements, test cases and links; a lint over the shipped content that every issue it names is in the snapshot, every link target exists and every requirement is verified or says why not.
- Integration: the demo makes four projects with their types, sections, links, test plan, execution, results and baseline; a second add is refused.
- Playwright: add the demo, open a requirement with its issue and guide page, and the coverage of a project, with the accessibility check.

## Implementation

- `backend/internal/demo/service.go`: `Keys` gains `ROT`; `snapshot/rotor.json`.
- The specifications live in `backend/internal/demo/spec/<tool>/*.md` and are parsed like `architecture/*.md` (`ParseArchitecture`).
- Projects from the software template, with the test case and test procedure types of the test template.
